Sports.title: Cherries on top! Bournemouth make European history as Sunderland score last-gasp winner and Brighton enjoy easy win... but Crystal Palace fall to defeat in five-goal thriller against Lyon
Sports.content:
Cherries on top! Bournemouth make European history as Sunderland score last-gasp winner and Brighton enjoy easy win... but Crystal Palace fall to defeat in five-goal thriller against Lyon

This was a night for Bournemouth to look back as much as it was to look forward.

A night to reflect on how far they’ve come, from navigating a 17-point deduction that put their Football League status at risk in 2008 to playing – and winning – their first ever European home game, thanks to a sublime treble from Evanilson, Rayan and Alvaro Rodriguez, who added the cherry on top with a late penalty.

There was a special tifo behind one goal to mark the historic night, with a record crowd of 12,010 packed in to witness it.

It was Adam Smith, who has been with Bournemouth since 2010 when they played in League One, leading them out as club captain.

Here was owner Bill Foley, seeing his vision to get Bournemouth into Europe, a target he ambitiously but explicitly set back in December 2022, occurring a year ahead of his five-year target.

But when Smith’s cross in from the right was expertly flicked up into the air by Evanilson, looping over Sturm Graz goalkeeper Daniil Khudyakov, it was a moment for Bournemouth to look forward, too.

Tournament favourites before they beat Real Sociedad in San Sebastian last time out and back-to-back European wins has done little to rubbish that label. Bournemouth have had to take the long way to the top but now they are here, they are showing just how much of a punch they pack.

Evanilson scored Bournemouth's first European goal at home in their 3-0 win over Sturm Graz

Bournemouth fans celebrated the club's journey pre-match, with the club now among the leading contenders to win the Europa League

Boss Marco Rose, who made five changes for this one, described the weekend’s 5-1 drubbing at the hands of Chelsea as a ‘good slap’.

Bournemouth were ruthlessly dismantled in south-west London. But to paraphrase the iconic ‘Tubthumping’, a song by British band Chumbawamba, when you get knocked down, you get up again, and that’s exactly what Rose’s side did.

It was a suffocating first half for a Sturm Graz side that started with a back five before pivoting to a back four at the interval.

Bournemouth had 10 efforts on goal to the visitors’ zero, with Ben Gannon-Doak and Evanilson a constant threat down the Bournemouth right.

Good sides ride their luck at times, too, and Bournemouth are no different. Sturm Graz wanted a penalty just before half-time when Belmin Beganovic was clumsily felled by Smith, only for the referee to adjudge Beganovic to have dived.

In a much improved second half, Graz struck the post when Jurgen Heil was picked out in the area.

But when you’ve battled back from the brink of minus-seventeen in League Two, and all the perils that come with trying to gatecrash the Premier League elite from a starting base in the fourth tier, adversity in Europe is light work.

Second halves have been an issue that have pockmarked Rose’s tenure on the south coast so far, coming into this one having led in six out of eight, only going on to win two of them. It was an irritation away to Sociedad, and here was proof that Rose and his players are learning lessons on the fly.

Marco Rose wants his side to take their performance against Sturm Graz into the Premier League

Justin Kluivert, Rayan and Ryan Christie all formed part of the cavalry sent on by Rose in a bid to settle the game and allow the party atmosphere to kick into another gear and that roll of the dice paid off with 15 minutes to go.

Khudyakov dealt poorly with a Bournemouth corner and after dropping it in his six-yard box, Rayan smashed in as Rose threw both arms into the air in celebration.

Rose is already looking ahead to how they can now secure their first league win of the season - starting on Sunday, when Sunderland visit the Vitality.

'Performance-wise, clean sheet, attitude, effort - a deserved win and now we have to continue, have to get consistent in these things and Sunderland is the next challenge,' said Rose.

'I believe in this team and know they are always confident despite a difficult situation. The squad is working, everyone is keen to play, everyone deserves to play and its good for us for the busy weeks to have a competitive squad.

'If we stick together and play like this and we have our fans then we are hard to play and it's hard to beat us. That's what we should take into the next game.'

For all the fireworks, tifos, light shows, and noise that lit up the night sky, here was proof of just how far Bournemouth have come… and how much further this ascending group can go with Champions League football in their sights.

Torreense 1-2 Sunderland: Sadiki scores last-gasp winner

By Michael Pavitt

Regis Le Bris was forced to call on the cavalry to rescue his side as Sunderland came from behind to win their first European away match in 53 years in stoppage time against Portuguese second division side Torreense.

Noah Sadiki struck in the dying minutes prompting wild celebrations from the near 4,000 travelling supporters, who had earlier seen summer signing Jules Ahoka cancel out a spectacular opener from Torreense defender Volnei Feltes.

The winner owed much to the creativity of Enzo Le Fee and Granit Xhaka as the pair, who began the night on the bench, underlined their importance to the Black Cats.

Having watched their team-mates struggle to break down Torreense, Le Fee produced a delightful dinked pass into the penalty area to find Xhaka, with the Swiss flicking the ball first time into the path of Sadiki to score his first goal for the club.

‘When Granit touched it I heard him scream shoot and I didn’t think twice,' Sadiki said. 'I just hoped it was going in and the keeper wouldn’t save it. I’m really happy. It was a beautiful moment.’

Le Bris had taken the understandable risk by deciding to make seven changes for the fixture against arguably their weakest Europa League opponents, with Torreense currently lying 15th in the Portuguese second tier.

Noah Sadiki scored a stoppage time winner as Sunderland beat Portuguese side Torreense

Sunderland were forced to fight back following a stunning opener from Volnei Feltes

With just four points in the Premier League and five matches left to play this month, this was the match to give an opportunity to fringe members of the squad.

Torreense, though, have proved they are more than capable of springing a surprise. Their journey to the Europa League is one to rival Sunderland’s own having stunned Sporting Lisbon in last year’s Portuguese Cup final to qualify.

Their opening goal proved just as unexpected as that triumph.

Feltes was well inside his own half when he received possession and opted to embark on a forward run. After driving towards the Sunderland box, the Brazilian defender chopped between the challenges of Malick Fofana and Nilson Angulo and curled magnificently into the top corner.

Whatever happens to the minnows, they will come away with one of the best goals of this year’s competition.

Sunderland were forced to be patient when trying to break down their opponents, who dropped deep in the second half.

Le Bris turned to his bench moments after Nilson Angulo saw a header superbly kept out by goalkeeper Lucas Paes, with Omar Alderete failing to convert the follow-up.

His quadruple change of Xhaka, Le Fee, Reinildo and Nordi Mukiele proved crucial. The latter's cross for Ahoka to equalise with a header while Xhaka and Le Fee were central to Sadiki's winner.

'Winning this game just at the end is really special,' Le Bris said. 'It’s important for the club and the fans – they were fantastic once again.

'We are growing and we need experiences and I think the team showed the belief until the end which is really important for us. We showed again we have this mindset.'

Lyon 3-2 Crystal Palace – Eagles defence struggles again

By James Sharpe

Now Pierre Sage knows how Oliver Glasner feels. He knows how it feels to return to your old stomping ground, one where you achieved great things, and come away with nothing.

Just as Glasner took his new Nottingham Forest side back to Selhurst Park at the weekend and lost, so too did Sage as Crystal Palace endured a frustrating night in Lyon where he once helped save the French side from relegation.

In truth, a night like this has been coming. Palace cannot keep defending like this, be so open and unorganised, and expect to win matches. Sooner or later, you leave yourself with too much of a hill to climb.

It took Forest just three minutes to open the scoring at the weekend and Lyon needed only seven minutes and 31 seconds here. As always, it was all too easy.

A bog-standard corner into a crowded six-yard box and, despite the hordes of black Palace shirts, the ball still dropped to Lyon captain Corentin Tolisso.

Only this time, Lyon didn’t miss the rest of the chances that came their way like Forest did. On the stroke of half-time the hosts cut through Palace with simple passes and Keito Nakamura squared for Ernest Nuamah, who darted ahead of the defenders to finish. Tyrick Mitchell, for all his goalscoring exploits this season, made little effort to track his run.

It was this leakiness that caused a few shudders in the Palace boardroom, letting in 11 goals in their opening four matches, and sparked rumblings that Sage could be the first Premier League managerial casualty of the season.

Pierre Sage saw his Crystal Palace side fall to a 3-2 defeat against his former club Lyon

Ernest Nuamah was among the scores as Lyon capitalised on poor Crystal Palace defending

If there is a saving grace to which Palace can cling, it’s that when they do get it right under Sage, they do look menacing. There was little of that in a dreadful first half but, after the break, they clicked into gear. They are just, as yet, unable to find the balance.

Having wantaway forward Ismaila Sarr back in the line-up always helps with his directness in the final third.

And when you have the precision of Adam Wharton in your midfield, you will always stand a chance. It was his delightful first-time through ball to Yeremy Pino after a fine short corner routine that helped fire Palace back into the game.

The introduction of Daichi Kamada swung momentum further Palace’s way. He was bundled over inside the box but Palace’s furious protests fell on deaf ears. He had a shot from close range saved and, eventually, found the net after some chaos inside the box.

The only problem was that, by then, Lyon had already added a third courtesy of Pavel Sulc’s cheeky backheel flick.

Palace kept pushing as Chris Richards saw a late header from a corner saved but, ultimately, in vain. This time, it wasn’t enough. This time, they didn’t get away with it. This time, they gave themselves too much to do.

'I’m really frustrated about the result but really frustrated with the way of playing in the first half,' Sage said.

'Our game started at half-time and it was too late.

'We play too quickly sometimes with the idea to play out the back quickly in transition but we are not a team like this, we have only one or two players able to run and make the difference with the speed.

'That’s why we have to move with the ball, travel with the ball, and we did that in the second half.'

Brighton 4-0 Kauno Zalgiris – Seagulls cruise in Conference League

By Kieran Gill

It must be up there with the finest feelings in football – the relief that washes over when your team finally finds a way through that dastardly low block in front of them.

For Brighton, that arrived just before half-time. There was no blaming Kauno Zalgiris for their tactical approach. Hardly anyone other than Fabian Hurzeler, who was perhaps being polite when listing the Lithuanian side’s attributes before kick-off, gave them a hope in hell of escaping their first-ever fixture in the main stage of a European competition without losing.

Once Georginio Rutter found that first goal after 41 minutes, this turned into a much more enjoyable evening at the Amex Stadium. Even more so when Jack Hinshelwood, back from his ankle injury and appearing for the first time since August, added a second before the break.

With that, the floodgates opened, Brighton started their Conference League campaign in style, and truthfully, this competition should sit high on Hurzeler’s priorities this term.

Georginio Rutter scored the opening goal as Brighton overcame Lithuanian side Kauno Zalgiris

While we often praise Brighton for the way in which they work – including in the talents they find that the richer clubs then seek to steal – all that is missing is the silverware to complement it all.

Despite being brilliantly run, they have never won a major trophy in their history, and the Conference League is an opportunity to correct that. Other English clubs such as West Ham and Brighton’s rivals Crystal Palace have used it well. To sides such as Kauno Zalgiris, these are giants they are competing with, opponents competing on an entirely alien level to their own.

While Hurzeler had explained why Kauno Zalgiris would be confident – he warned us they were the champions of Lithuania and that they had won the Lithuanian Cup at the weekend – Brighton are in a happy place, too. This made it five successive victories for them in all competitions.

They are third in the Premier League behind only Manchester City and Arsenal, and into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup after winning away at Manchester United – a club now linked with liking Hurzeler in case they move on from Michael Carrick.

With that, we had an inkling as to how this game would go. Brighton would attack, and Kauno Zalgiris would defend, and the opening 30 minutes was all about blocks. From Anton Tolordava, from Nosa Iyobosa Edokpolor, from any Kauno Zalgiris player with a body for throwing at the ball.

But then arrived the breakthrough. It was a nice finish from Rutter despite the on-field officials thinking the ball had gone behind for a goal-kick in the build-up. It had not, and VAR overruled to award Brighton their opener. Hinshelwood added a second before the break before Rutter grabbed the third goal and Matt O’Riley the fourth.

‘We want to keep improving every game,' said Hinshelwood. 'What’s happened in the past has gone now. We want to look forward to the future.’

It was a good way to warm up for Palace in the Premier League on Sunday, though Brighton may be reminded by the Amex’s away end which side have won a trophy of late. Hurzeler should be embracing this European competition as a way to give his supporters a season to cherish.

Sports.title: FA pile pressure on Gianni Infantino - with chair saying he 'is not fit to be FIFA president' if he refuses to answer questions over World Cup sell-off
Sports.content:
Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt says Gianni Infantino is 'not fit to be FIFA president' if he does not answer questions about his World Cup sell-off plan or the Folarin Balogun case. Hewitt, also a FIFA vice-president, was one of the FIFA Council members who tried to hold Infantino to account in Zurich on Thursday at its first meeting since the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan came to light. Infantino apologised in the meeting for what he called 'mistakes that we made in relation to the communication and consultation process'. Hewitt said Council members had not received answers to 'anything we had specifically requested' regarding FFE or the Balogun incident, where the USA striker’s one-match ban was suspended following a call to Infantino from US President Donald Trump. Hewitt told reporters in Zurich: 'The man has to answer those questions, and if he doesn’t answer those questions, no, he’s not fit to be FIFA president, and that was what was shared in the meeting. 'He’s told us to submit those questions. There were so many of them, and now it’s up to him to do that, and do that in the open way. Debbie Hewitt has called for Gianni Infantino to answer questions over his World Cup sell-off plan and the Folarin Balogun affair ahead of FIFA's presidential elections 'The minimum is having the papers from FFE, because if there’s nothing to hide, then share them with us.' The FFE plan first became public knowledge in July. Infantino sought to create a company to manage the commercial interests of FIFA’s competitions, including the World Cup, but wanted a minority stake to be made available to private investors. The lead investor was set to be Thrive, a company founded by President Trump’s son-in-law’s brother, Josh Kushner, but the plan was abandoned on August 1 after three continental confederations rejected it. Among those within to publicly disagree with Infantino's plan were FIFA general secretary Mattias Grafstrom, senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro, chief operating officer Kevin Lamour and Arsene Wenger, who serves as FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development. Hewitt has previously written to Infantino demanding the release of documents related to FFE, while European football’s governing body UEFA has also submitted legal applications in the US seeking disclosure, which FIFA has challenged. Hewitt’s September letter to Infantino is also understood to have requested information on how the Balogun ban came to be suspended. Infantino has always maintained the decision was made independently of him by the FIFA disciplinary committee. Trump bragged about calling Infantino in the wake of Balogun's red card in the build-up to the USA's next game against Belgium, confirming that he 'asked for a review by FIFA'. 'I'm good at this stuff,' Trump added. 'That wasn't a foul. That wasn't even an infraction.' Hewitt said it was 'reasonable' for Infantino to request the submission of questions in writing, adding: 'He gave us the opportunity to say what we felt, and I think anybody that didn’t say what they felt in there, they’ve missed their opportunity. 'I have no new information that makes me feel any differently about how I felt when I went in, other than we do have a president of FIFA who is apologetic about what has happened, and secondly, a promise again that we will get the information that we’ve requested.' Infantino said 'everyone had the opportunity to ask questions and express their views' on FFE. He added in a video released by FIFA: 'I apologised for the mistakes that we made in relation to the communication and consultation process related to the FIFA Forward Enterprise project which then led to many consequences. 'But what is important to remember is that it was a proposal, so in no way a done deal. Just a proposal that actually intended to enable FIFA to invest more in our member associations, as opposed to replacing support from existing resources.' UEFA has vowed to identify a credible candidate to stand against Infantino in next March’s presidential elections, having declared its loss of confidence in him in August over the FFE plan. The deadline for candidacies to be submitted is November 18.

Sports.title: Arsenal star Mikel Merino admits he's 'fortunate to be alive' after 'an angel' saved him during Borussia Dortmund bus bombing
Sports.content:
Arsenal star Mikel Merino admits he's 'fortunate to be alive' after 'an angel' saved him during Borussia Dortmund bus bombing

Arsenal midfielder Mikel Merino has admitted he is 'fortunate to be alive' after 'an angel' prevented him from being injured in the 2017 Borussia Dortmund bus bombing.

The football world was shaken when the German side were victims of an attack by Sergej Wenergold, which saw three pipe bombs detonated near the bus when it was on its way to a Champions League match.

Dortmund defender Marc Bartra was left hospitalised with a wrist injury following the attack, while a police officer was also treated for injuries and unable to return to work.

Merino, meanwhile, escaped unscathed – but that may not necessarily have been the case.

'I think I have an angel on my shoulder,' Merino, who was 20 at the time, told The Players' Tribune. 'I'm actually fortunate to be alive at all.

He added: 'There was a deafening noise, and then I remember the bus nearly tipping over. I looked behind me and saw blood on the floor. Smoke, screams. I remember being at the hospital later that night, waiting for Marc Bartra, who had his wrist badly cut up.

Arsenal's Mikel Merino has said he is 'fortunate to be alive' after being onboard Dortmund's team bus during a bombing

The Dortmund bus was targeted in 2017 when on its way to a Champions League quarter-final

'The next day, someone told me that a huge piece of shrapnel was lodged in the headrest of the seat next to Marc. My usual seat. That day, the seat was empty.

'My legs were feeling a bit tight, and the seats in the front reclined. So I sat up there instead, and it may have saved my life. So yeah, I just have this belief that things happen for a reason.'

The pipe bombs were hidden in hedges by the side of the road and detonated at around 7.15pm local time. Dortmund were on the way to their stadium to face Monaco in the Champions League quarter-finals.

The bombs were filled with metal pins and had a reach of around 100 meters.

After a lengthy investigation, Wenergold, then 29, was charged with 28 counts of attempted murder for the attack. He was sentenced to 14 years in prison.

He said during the trial that he did not intend to kill any of the players but make money by betting on a fall in Borussia Dortmund's stock market price.

The match against Monaco was postponed but played the following day - a decision led to some heavy criticism of UEFA.

England coach Thomas Tuchel was manager of Dortmund at the time and after the match branded the decision to play the game 'absurd'.

'We were informed by text message that UEFA was making this decision,' he added. 'A decision made in Switzerland that concerns us directly. We will not forget it. It is a very bad feeling.

'There is a feeling of helplessness. What we think has not interested anyone. We weren't asked about playing the game.

'Everyone has their own way of reacting to events. The players had the choice not to play, but no-one chose this option.'

Sports.title: Louis van Gaal insists Man City's scandal contributed to 'all the consequences and suffering' that followed his Man United exit - as ex-boss believes 'for sure' his reign would've ended better
Sports.content:
Louis van Gaal has blamed Manchester City's financial doping for the 'suffering' that he endured in his torrid 2016 Man United exit. The Dutch manager was given his marching orders on the heels of the 2015-16 season, which saw the Red Devils narrowly miss out on a place in the following term's Champions League. Both Man City and Man United wrapped up with 66 points, but the Cityzens, playing their final season under Manuel Pellegrini had the superior goal difference which secured their spot at Europe's top table. Van Gaal was despatched despite ending the season having won the FA Cup, and in correspondence with the Athletic, stressed that he believed that failing to qualify for the European top flight had prompted the club's Glazer ownership group to swing the axe. 'For me, at the time, that (missing out on the Champions League in 2016) was probably the deciding factor in my dismissal from Manchester United and all the consequences and suffering this entailed,' he stated. The former Barcelona boss added that 'for sure', things might have been different if he had been playing in a fair competition. Louis van Gaal admitted that he believes his time at Man United might have ended differently if not for Man City's financial manipulation The former manager was dismissed at the end of the 2015-16 season after missing out on a spot in the Champions League, despite finishing level on points with City Van Gaal subsequently took a hiatus from management, which he described at the time as being a 'sabbatical'. He only returned to the dugout in 2021, when he was appointed as head coach of the Dutch national team. Van Gaal's tenure at Old Trafford fell during the period between 2009 and 2018 that Man City have been found guilty of artificially inflating revenue made through sponsorship. City were found to have used 'sham' contracts and agreements to cook their books by around £900million over a nine-year period, claiming a commercial income of £949.94m of which only £119.25m had come from sponsors. The Premier League said the panel found City arranged ‘sham contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners, as well as relying on ‘sham’ agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club’s revenues and reduce its costs’. Deals with a number of sponsors were part of ‘a disguised funding scheme, whereby those companies were only required to pay a portion of the relevant sponsorship fees’, the statement added, saying that ‘the remainder was funded by Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club’. The result was that the club had ‘filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators’. Man City have doubled down on their innocence and appealed the verdict, with the club underscoring that they are in possession of 'irrefutable evidence' which will clear their name. For Van Gaal, he admitted that there was little he could do as he 'cannot turn back history now.' 'Not even the English Football Association can (do that),' he added. But the 75-year-old is not alone in wondering what might have been had Man City not been able to inflate their revenue and in turn, invest in some of the players fundamental to their multi-year successes. Former Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard admitted that he wanted the club to 'suffer' after 'stealing memories', with the Reds icon going without a Premier League medal during their era of dominance. Liverpool came second to Man City when they claimed the title in 2013-14, and although Gerrard was circumspect last week as he discussed Man City's potential punishment, he ultimately called for the club to be sanctioned heavily. 'I think I have come to terms with that I have never won the Premier League, that I was short in that department in terms of winning it,' Gerrard said last week. 'I have come to terms with the incident that happened to me at the back end of that season and I have heard a lot of City players, a lot of City fans, and celebrity fans say "you can't take those moments away from us". 'What about the memories they have taken away from not just possibly me, and the team that I played in but over that period of time, nine, ten years? 'Spurs fans, United fans, Everton fans, teams at the bottom, teams in the cups? City, ex-players, current players, and City owners, everyone connected with City have got to think about the memories they have stolen away from everyone else. 'Multi-year punishments, that would be my opinion,' he added when asked what was deserved. 'I'm not saying that's the right opinion, but that's just how I feel sitting here in this chair. 'I think putting them down to the Championship is not fair on the EFL. I don't think it's enough, because they'll bounce back. You look at that team yesterday. Can you imagine that in the Championship? With all due respect, it's not fair on the teams playing against City week in, week out. It's not fair on the potential team that could be the third team to come up. 'I think it needs to be a transfer ban. I think it needs to be points over a period of time. And make them suffer like they've made everyone else suffer for the nine, ten years that they've done it for. That would be my opinion. But there needs to be an example set.'

Sports.title: Man United outcast Andre Onana concedes directly from a corner - after Mo Salah stunner had put their Trabzonspor side in control of Conference League clash
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United goalkeeper Andre Onana conceded a goal directly from a corner in the Conference League on Thursday night. The 30-year-old, who is still contracted to United but on loan at Turkish side Trabzonspor, was playing in his side's European game against Kuopion Palloseura of Finland. His side started well, with former Southampton forward Paul Onuachu putting them ahead in the third minute of the game as Thomas Reis's side looked to start the competition on a positive note. Then, in the 44th minute, Liverpool legend Mohamed Salah, who moved to Turkey in the summer after leaving the Reds, made it 2-0 with a fine finish to pick up his eighth goal of the season in ten games. The forward ran onto a blocked shot that was bouncing in the box, and finished high with the inside of his left foot to seemingly put the game beyond the hosts. Franculino Dju then made it three just after the break, but veteran Petteri Pennanen got his side back into it with the help of Onana's error. André Onana is unable to keep it out as KuPS score directly from a corner 🤯 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/91Wv44oSzt — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 15, 2026 Manchester United's Andre Onana conceded a goal directly from a corner on Thursday night Onana found himself on the floor in his goal after failing to keep the ball out The midfielder put in a corner minutes after his side went 3-0 down, and Onana jumped but was unable to keep the effort out of the goal. The Manchester United loanee lay on the floor as his team-mates walked away, and had to gather himself for the rest of the game. He would concede again just before full-time, with the game ending 4-2. United fans rushed to social media to give their verdicts, with one fan writing on X: 'Do not miss this man, no matter how bad we are.' Another wrote: 'Nice to see he is still an absolute liability.' A third added: 'One of the worst goalkeepers I have seen.' Onana is rebuilding his career out in Turkey after a calamitous spell at United – who he joined in 2023 – which resulted in him losing his place and, eventually, being loaned out. His wages are not being covered by the Red Devils, and it is expected he will leave permanently either this summer or when his contract expires in 2028. Mo Salah with a BEAUTIFUL finish to double Trabzonspor’s lead ✨ 📺 Stream on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nF15dy6wcI — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) October 15, 2026 It has been a mixed season for Trabzonspor so far, having been knocked out of the Europa League in the play-offs and thus dropping into the Conference League. Trabzonspor are currently fifth in the league table after seven games, having won four of their matches so far. Onana has formed an unlikely friendship with Salah, who has been an instant hit with the club's fans.

Sports.title: Andy Goode names English sides who can break France's Champions Cup dominance
Sports.content:
Andy Goode names English sides who can break France's Champions Cup dominance

Andy Goode believes Northampton and Bath, who shared 119 points over the weekend, can both challenge for European honours

View Image Andy Goode will be on Premier Sports duty throughout the Investec Champions Cup campaign (Image: ©INPHO/Morgan Treacy)

Andy Goode believes Northampton Saints have a realistic chance of ending the French ‘stranglehold’ on the Champions Cup title as they prepare to kick off their continental campaign.

‌



‌



The East Midlanders fell to fellow PREM side Bath in the quarter-finals last year, having made the final in the previous campaign, and open up against Cardiff this time around. Two-time reigning champions Bordeaux Begles made it six consecutive victories for French sides last season and former England fly-half Goode believes Saints’ entertaining style can help them challenge.

‌



Goode, who will be at DPD Stadium at Franklin’s Gardens on Premier Sports duty on Sunday evening, said: “Whenever you start a competition, one of the first things that people look at is who are the favourites, who's going to win it or who's going to be in the mix to win it.

‌



“Ultimately, Saints, from an English perspective, are a team that play an exciting brand of rugby. It's a real exciting team to watch. I've watched them for quite a few years as this team has developed, grown, and gained experience. This isn't an easy competition to win - anyone who has won it will tell you that. It is the ultimate test of any club rugby player in the world.”

Saints’ 71-48 victory against Bath last weekend was the second-highest scoring match in PREM history, drawing praise for outstanding attacking rugby, as well as criticism for seemingly leaky defences. But Goode, who is the second-highest points scorer in the league’s history, believes such entertainment is only good for the sport.

‌



He said: “Northampton play the brand that they do with the exciting players they've got, like Henry Pollock, JJ Van der Mescht, Curtis Langdon and some of the forwards. They've got Alex Coles, who's on fire. The fact their mindset is ‘let's go out and attack and try and score whenever we've got possession’ is a testament to the coaches - and a testament to how the players want to play and the skill level that they drive in the week.

“I've been to watch Saints train a couple of times and over the last season or so and saw the skill level of what they put out last week and attacking at the line with the different options, the offloading, the ball out of contact. I don't think [their match against Bath] was down to bad defences, it was down to unbelievable attack. Defences weren't able to get set to try and offer team.”

Eight English teams are participating in the Champions Cup, which will again be shown exclusively live on Premier Sports, with Goode also part of the team heading to Kingsholm on Friday night as Gloucester host champions Bordeaux. Northampton share Pool Four with keen rivals Bath, as well as Montpellier, Stade Francais, Bulls, and Cardiff.

Article continues below

Goode said: “From an English perspective, Northampton and Bath are the two best equipped teams to try and break that French stranglehold.”

Sports.title: Mark Chapman will not present Match of the Day this weekend as BBC decision confirmed
Sports.content:
Mark Chapman will not present Match of the Day this weekend as BBC decision confirmed

The BBC has confirmed its Match of the Day line-up for this weekend's shows and Mark Chapman won't be in the studio

View 3 Images Mark Chapman will not feature on Match of the Day this weekend (Image: Getty)

Mark Chapman won't feature on Match of the Day this weekend. He shares presenting duties on the show with Kelly Cates and Gabby Logan.

‌



‌



In January 2025, the BBC announced that three seasoned presenters would replace long-time lead Gary Lineker. Chapman, the veteran host of Match of the Day 2 and a BBC Radio 5 Live staple, was one of these.

‌



The others are senior BBC Sport anchor Gabby Logan and Kelly Cates, who extended her Beeb role to television after leading Premier League coverage for Sky Sports.

‌



When it comes to Match of the Day, the trio rotate week by week. The BBC has confirmed that, for the next round of top-flight fixtures, Cates will front the show on Saturday and Logan will take over on Sunday. Chapman tags out, having hosted last Sunday's episode.

Man Utd told to suspend Lisandro Martinez immediately despite new public statement READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss sports' biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

View 3 Images Match of the Day has three hosts (Image: PA)

‌



On Saturday, Cates will be joined in the Match of the Day studio by ex-Liverpool and Fulham star Danny Murphy, who is a regular. Former Manchester City goalkeeper Joe Hart is the other guest.

The episode will cover five Premier League matches: Everton vs Chelsea, Brentford vs Liverpool, Fulham vs Hull City, Manchester City vs Ipswich Town and Newcastle vs Aston Villa.

Sunday's edition will be fronted by Logan, who'll be joined by former top-flight goalkeeper Shay Given as well as BBC stalwart Dion Dublin.

‌



Four Premier League matches will be covered by these three: Bournemouth vs Sunderland, Brighton vs Crystal Palace, Leeds vs Manchester United and Nottingham Forest vs Arsenal.

Cates and Chapman made headlines 11 days ago when it was revealed that they had started dating. Chapman had split from Dubai-based property specialist Clere Collier in April.

The romance has drawn warmth from the public as both Chapman and Cates, the daughter of Liverpool icon Sir Kenny Dalglish, have endured personal hardships in recent years.

‌



View 3 Images Cates and Chapman appeared on Gogglebox (Image: Channel 4)

In 2020, Chapman's wife, Sara, to whom he had been married for nearly two decades, tragically passed away from cancer at the age of 44. The pair had three children together, whom the presenter continues to raise.

Cates split from TV producer Tom Cates in 2021, after 14 years of marriage. She said on her colleague Logan's Life At The Mid Point podcast five years ago: "I don't have a picture in my head of why a middle-aged, slightly overweight mother of two could possibly be attractive.

Article continues below

"I can't get my head round that. It's not that I'm putting myself down and it's not a lack of confidence or low self-esteem. It's just I don't know what that would look like."

Reports now claim she and fellow Match of the Day host Chapman have coupled up. The two most recently appeared together in an episode of Channel 4's Celebrity Gogglebox in July.

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Florian Wirtz's biggest issue identified as Andoni Iraola admits dilemma
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Florian Wirtz's biggest issue identified as Andoni Iraola admits dilemma

Liverpool's latest news round-up includes a verdict being made on Florian Wirtz's biggest struggle

View 3 Images Andoni Iraola's side bounced back after their first Premier League defeat of the season (Image: Paul ELLIS/AFP via Getty Images)

Liverpool bounced back from their 3-0 defeat to Manchester City with an emphatic 6-3 victory over LASK. The Reds earned their second Champions League win of the season on Wednesday against the Austrian side.

‌



‌



It was an impressive performance from Andoni Iraola's side, albeit with some questionable defending late on that saw the European minnows score three past Alisson Becker in the last 30 minutes.

‌



Bradley Barcola netted the first senior hat-trick of his career, while Lewis Koumas scored his first goal in the prestigious competition. Florian Wirtz registered an assist in the match, but his struggles have been discussed, while the Spanish boss opened up about the dilemma he faces within his squad.

‌



Mirror Football delves into the latest stories coming out of Anfield...

Wirtz's biggest issue

Steven Gerrard claimed that Florian Wirtz's total lack of confidence is behind his inconsistency at Liverpool. The 23-year-old has failed to live up to expectations at Anfield since joining the club in a £116million deal last year.

Wirtz had his best performance of the season in midweek, assisting Bradley Barcola's second goal of the game, but he remains without one himself in the 2026/27 campaign.

‌



Chelsea leading race for £100m-rated Alex Scott as Bournemouth face January decision READ MORE :

Andoni Iraola learns key lesson as Bradley Barcola makes Liverpool mark in goal fest READ MORE :

Make sure you don't miss the best Liverpool coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

The former Reds captain opened up about Wirtz's situation on the Stick to Football podcast, but insisted the German star can still come good at Liverpool. "I am not denying that he is underperforming and that we should have seen a lot more given his price tag," Gerrard said.

"But I just think there is a chance, and it's happened previously, that players can turn it around. I think he's got the talent to turn it around, but his confidence is shot at the moment."

‌



View 3 Images Florian Wirtz remains without a goal this season (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

Iraola reveals dilemma

Liverpool's six-goal offering in Austria included four goal contributions from defenders Jeremie Frimpong and Ronald Araujo. The Dutchman notched two assists and a goal, while the summer signing netted his first goal for the club.

Five of Araujo's nine appearances have come at right-back due to Frimpong's weaknesses in defence and Conor Bradley being sidelined due to injury. However, they played alongside each other on Wednesday and Iraola admitted the stark contrast between their styles at right-back makes a marked difference in how the rest of the team performs.

‌



View 3 Images Andoni Iraola opened up about an issue with Liverpool's selection (Image: AP Photo/Denes Erdos)

He said after full-time: "It is clear the difference in the team when we play with Jeremie and Ronald. The demands we put on the players are completely different. Jeremie helps us more offensively as he can arrive in the final third positions, but that does leave more space behind because you can’t cover everything.

"Ronald is the opposite because he is more comfortable defending as a centre-back, but he doesn’t give us the runs in behind, overlaps, or the options that Jeremie does. It is about us seeing what we need from the game, but we need to keep them both in a good place so we have those options during games. Until we recover Conor, I am happy to have those options."

Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Michael Carrick replacement 'has said yes' as Prem rival backed to take over

Michael Carrick's weakening position as Manchester United manager is the talk of the town after the club's winless streak was extended to five games

View 2 Images Antonio Conte is reportedly open to replacing Michael Carrick as Manchester United boss (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester United manager Michael Carrick could find his position soon becomes untenable without a sudden turnaround in form. Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid has left United with just two wins from nine games this term.

‌



‌



It means Sunday's visit to rivals Leeds could be a make-or-break moment for the Old Trafford icon. United have already made their worst start to a league campaign in four decades but there's always room for things to get deteriorate further.

‌



Speculation is rampant as to whom could take over the club if Carrick is shown the door. Mirror Football dissects the latest headlines around Old Trafford as the incumebent boss strains to keep his head above water.

‌

Conte 'would say yes' to United

Free agent Antonio Conte would reportedly be open to taking over at United if offered the chance. Calciomercato reports Conte "would accept" the job and is supposedly awaiting an offer as Carrick's position grows increasingly uncertain.

Roy Keane tears into Bruno Fernandes and Harry Maguire as Lisandro Martinez fine demanded READ MORE :

The former Chelsea boss, who won the Premier League with the Blues in 2017, is a free agent after leaving Napoli at the end of last season. Conte, 57, won the Serie A crown in Naples in 2025 before tensions within the club reportedly led to his exit.

‌



According to talkSPORT, Conte is one of the frontrunners in free agency to take over if Carrick receives the boot. Former Germany and Bayern Munich boss Julian Nagelsmann is the other leading candidate currently without a club.

Despite his previous exploits in England, there is an element of risk for United concerning Conte. His stints with Chelsea and Tottenham each ended in acrimony, while the Italian may be better off arriving in between campaigns when he can implement a full pre-season.

‌



Nonetheless, murmurs out of Italy suggest he's receptive to the idea of an Old Trafford takeover. And a firmer hand at the helm may be just what's needed to get the most out of this United squad.

Hurzeler tipped as 'the real deal'

View 2 Images (Image: Mike Hewitt/Getty Images)

United legend Paul Scholes has said Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler "looks the real deal" amid links to Old Trafford. The German, who already knocked United out of the EFL Cup this term, is touted as one of several names prominently linked as Carrick's potential successor.

‌



Hurzeler became the youngest head coach in Premier League history when he took over Brighton two years ago at just 31. The former St. Pauli boss has led the Seagulls to consecutive eighth-place league finishes in England's top flight, leading to rumours he's ready for a considerable step up.

"He’s done great. He looks the real deal," said Scholes on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast. "But again, Man United is different.

"The scrutiny is on you every single week. If Brighton didn’t win a game for the next 10 games, nobody would really be that bothered."

He continued: "The one thing that someone like Hurzeler has got over Michael is that he’s done a body of work in the Premier League. Michael did okay in Middlesbrough with what he had. I think Middlesbrough were probably expecting more with the budget they had."

Scholes even suggested there may be a part of Carrick that wants out of his old club amid the downturn in results. He said his old team-mate could be thinking "I'll take a few quid" to start afresh.

Sports.title: Ryan Wilson tells Glasgow  to 'dig deep' to break Champions Cup duck
Sports.content:
Ryan Wilson tells Glasgow to 'dig deep' to break Champions Cup duck

The Scottish side reached last year’s quarter-finals as one of the top two seeds in the group stages, before being upset at home by Toulon.

View Image Ryan Wilson will be on Premier Sports duty during the opening weekend of the Investec Champions Cup (Image: Premier Sports)

Ryan Wilson believes Franco Smith holds the key to Glasgow Warriors breaking the glass ceiling and pushing for Investec Champions Cup glory for the first time this season.

‌



‌



The Scottish side reached last year’s quarter-finals as one of the top two seeds in the group stages, before being upset at home by Toulon. And while former club captain Wilson believes Glasgow have it in them to challenge the best again this season, he knows that they only have a chance of becoming the first Scottish winners of the competition if Smith can create some depth after a summer that saw the departures of the likes of Huw Jones, Adam Hastings and Jack Dempsey.

‌



“The problem with both squads (Glasgow and Edinburgh), and I guess you could say it's across all the teams in the competition, it's always how deep do the squads go?” said Wilson, part of the Premier Sports team broadcasting the opening round of this year’s Investec Champions Cup and EPCR Challenge Cup.

‌



“That's probably my one worry with the Scottish teams, is how deep do they actually go and how can they stay away from injuries? Both teams were hampered with injuries last year and Glasgow have lost a fair few players.

“I hope to see them push on. I think they've got the team that can do it. Have they got the depth of the squad? We’re yet to see. They're going to have to dig pretty deep.

‌



“I said that again at the beginning of the season, for Glasgow to do well this year, Franco's going to have to work his magic. But if there's a bloke that can do it, it's certainly Franco Smith.”

Glasgow are one of just two unbeaten teams in club competition this season, along with Edinburgh, and kick off their Champions Cup campaign away to Sale Sharks. They got the better of Sale at the same stage a year ago, on their way to topping a high-class pool, on a day when Jamie Dobie played the final half-hour at scrum-half. He has since emerged as an international option both in the No.9 jersey and on the wing.

And while the man himself is keen to play scrum-half primarily, Wilson feels the most important thing is that he is involved somewhere at international level, such is the X-factor he offers.

Article continues below

He added: “Jamie Dobie is untouchable. I want to see him get a bit more time in the nine jersey because to have someone that's that adaptable and able to play across the back line like he does in the way that he does, for the size of the man, he's a special player.

“I was really gutted for him when Kyle Rowe pulled out at the weekend. He then got shifted back to the wing and everyone's asking what is his preferred position? I know he wants to play nine. I know he prefers getting increasingly involved. That's what you want to see, as you see moments of magic from him in the game.”

Sports.title: Louis van Gaal claims Man City antics influenced 'deciding factor' in Man Utd sacking
Sports.content:
Louis van Gaal claims Man City antics influenced 'deciding factor' in Man Utd sacking

Louis van Gaal was sacked by Manchester United in 2016 having missed out on the Champions League - with Manchester City topping them during a period where they were breaching financial rules

View 2 Images Louis van Gaal lasted two years before being sacked by Man Utd (Image: PA)

Louis van Gaal has bemoaned Manchester City's cheating scandal with his Manchester United sacking coming after he narrowly missed out on the Champions League - with their neighbours the ones to pip them to fourth spot.

‌



The Dutchman lasted two years at Old Trafford, but a fifth place finish in 2016 proved to be the final straw and he was shown the door with Jose Mourinho replacing him.

Van Gaal's final game was the FA Cup final, where he claimed victory over Crystal Palace, but 24 hours later he received his marching orders, owing to a poor league campaign that saw United capitulate from December, finishing outside the top four on goal difference.

‌



It was City who edged them and Van Gaal believes that their league position was the "the deciding factor" in him losing his job - and that frustration has only furthered after the Etihad outfit were found guilty of 114 financial breaches from 2009 to 2018.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Van Gaal told the Athletic: “For me, at the time, that (missing out on the Champions League in 2016) was probably the deciding factor in my dismissal from Manchester United and all the consequences and suffering this entailed.”

City's guilty verdict came after years of investigating, and has already been appealed by those on the blue half of Manchester, but Van Gaal claims irrespective of what happens next “I cannot turn back history now. Not even the English Football Association can (do that).”

Van Gaal saw his United team claim four points in the games against City in the 2015/16 season - drawing at Old Trafford before they secured a statement win at the Etihad with a young Marcus Rashford scoring the only goal of the game.

‌



View 2 Images Man City beat Man Utd into fourth place in 2016

Despite Van Gaal's frustration United can only have themselves to blame with fourth spot within their grasp going into the final weeks of the season. They had control of their own destiny but they lost at West Ham in the penultimate game of the campaign and that gave City the breathing room they needed.

Van Gaal left United having won 54 of his 103 games, giving him a 52 percent win rate. He was the second manager to take charge in Manchester after Sir Alex Ferguson's retirement, replacing David Moyes in the aftermath of the World Cup in 2014. He finished fourth in his first season, but couldn't repeat that feat.

Sports.title: Alex Scott quits Disney+ job just weeks after new role began following BBC Football Focus exit
Sports.content:
Alex Scott quits Disney+ job just weeks after new role began following BBC Football Focus exit

Alex Scott has fronted Women's Champions League coverage on Disney+ after previously presenting Football Focus on the BBC for five years before it was cancelled

View 2 Images Alex Scott will no longer present Women's Champions League coverage on Disney+ (Image: Getty Images)

Alex Scott has left her role presenting Women's Champions League on Disney+ after fronting the streaming service's coverage. The decision comes barely a month after her production company, First Cap Productions, launched its first show, One More Word.

‌



‌



Scott, 42, incorporated First Cap in May, weeks before hosting the final episode of Football Focus, which the BBC cancelled at the end of last season. She spent five years fronting the programme and became its first full-time female presenter in 2021.

‌



Her emphasis now appears to be on the Women's Super League. One More Word covers England's highest-level women's football league.

Lisandro Martinez makes Man Utd apology after meeting with Michael Carrick and club chiefs READ MORE :

The Guardian reports that Scott has left her Disney+ role to focus on other projects, including the new show. Women's Champions League rights were secured by the platform only last May in a five-season deal covering all 75 matches.

A spokesperson for Disney+ stated: "We would like to extend our sincere thanks to Alex Scott for her contribution to our coverage of the UEFA Women's Champions League on Disney+.

"Her passion for the women's game and the competition shone through throughout her time with us, and we are grateful for all she contributed. We wish her every success."

View 2 Images Alex Scott also presents Women's Super League matches on the BBC (Image: WSL Football via Getty Images)

Coverage of the Women's Champions League on Disney+ has drawn criticism this season. Viewers have highlighted technical problems with the ESPN-produced broadcasts they use.

s notably interrupted their coverage of the match between Arsenal and HB Koge. About three minutes of the second half were not shown, with the message "commercial break in progress" displayed for some viewers.

Scott spoke about the subject to the Observer, saying: "Ultimately, do I agree with all the decisions that were made? Absolutely not. Did I try and advise? Yes, but I can only do so much.
