Sports.title: Devin Haney Claims Shakur Stevenson Wanted Rehydration Clause
Sports.content:
Update: Devin Haney fired back at Shakur Stevenson, stating he initially accepted 145 pounds before Stevenson vanished for days and tried sneaking in a rehydration clause.

“You’re cap.. I agreed to 145 u went missing for days. Tried to put a rehydration clause on me. I wasted 6 months negotiating with you,” Haney posted on X. “I been negotiating with u since i was gonna sign to Zuffa. Yall did every thing for this fight not to happen even tried to throw Keyshawn in my way.”

Haney brings a crucial detail into public view. His original stance was 145 pounds with zero weight limits on fight morning. If Stevenson demanded a ceiling on Haney rehydrating after the weigh in, that altered the deal completely.

That explains Haney shutting down the catchweight talk. Trimming down two extra pounds while keeping the freedom to bulk back up on fight night is completely separate from accepting strict secondary limits. Haney skipped over Stevenson’s claim that an attorney formally demanded 147 pounds, but his message makes his anger obvious.

For Haney, who already had to dry himself out to shave two pounds off the 147 welterweight limit, that restriction is brutal. Capping Haney at 155 on Saturday morning prevents him from drinking freely, forces him to go to bed dehydrated, and leaves him depleted inside the ring.

That is why Haney walked away. Offering the two-pound concession at 145 was already a compromise.

Devin Haney Has Reasons to Reconsider Shakur Catchweight

Shakur Stevenson claims Devin Haney pulled out of their agreed 145-pound catchweight to demand the full 147-pound welterweight limit, blowing up a deal that looked locked down earlier this month.

Shakur has plenty of reason to be furious. Still, Haney can always rethink whether draining himself below welterweight makes sense against a slick target who rarely gets hit cleanly.

“At the 11th hour, after agreeing to 144 and then 145, DeeHoe had his lawyer email and say that he would only fight at 147. Big waste of everybody’s time,” Shakur posted on X.

Haney originally offered 145 with no rehydration limits, which Shakur took on October 8 with a quick reply: “145.0 U GOT A DEAL.” If Stevenson is telling the whole story, Haney backed off the exact compromise he put on the table.

Fans will call him out for it, but Haney does not have to sign off on terms that leave him depleted in the ring. Two extra pounds below welterweight might sound like nothing from the couch, but that extra pull can easily ruin a camp.

Stevenson is stepping up from 140 to take a shot at Haney’s WBO welterweight belt. Haney can legitimately question why he should drain his body for a challenger whose defensive mastery already makes for a nightmare night at the office.

Haney holds the chips here. He carries bigger commercial pull, so Stevenson is hardly his only ticket to a monster bag. Sitting back to see what happens between Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez gives him another massive payday with far less hassle.

Nobody has seen the lawyer’s email yet, and Shakur never explained what prompted the change. His anger makes complete sense after shaking hands on a public deal, but Haney has to protect his physical edge while weighing the bigger options waiting for him.

Once a fighter shows weakness on the scales, the other camp smells blood and starts picking at the money.

Catchweight concessions always shift the psychological leverage. If Haney drops down to 145 just to accommodate Shakur moving up from 140, Shakur immediately feels like the A side dictating terms. From that vantage point, Shakur starts pushing for an even split or demanding parity he has not earned at the box office.

Sports.title: William Zepeda Replaces Shakur Stevenson Atop Ring Rankings
Sports.content:
Stripping Shakur Stevenson of the top spot at lightweight was long overdue. The Ring finally bumped William Zepeda to number one, updating the board to reflect reality since Shakur departed for junior welterweight.

Shakur hasn’t stepped into the ring at 135 pounds since his 2025 scrap with Zepeda. He snatched the WBO junior welterweight belt off Teofimo Lopez in January. Keeping him perched above fighters who actively compete in the weight class makes zero sense.

Leaving a division means stepping aside for the next man up, whether Shakur likes it or not. He got the official win over Zepeda, sure. That win shouldn’t grant him lifetime ownership over a division he completely walked away from.

That bout was much tighter than the lopsided scorecards indicated anyway. Zepeda relentlessly marched forward for twelve complete rounds, pressing Shakur hard without offering any real breathing room. On my scorecard, that fight was a draw. Shakur landed cleaner single shots, but those flashes never created the massive margin the judges turned in.

Now Zepeda sits atop an exciting lineup featuring Abdullah Mason, Floyd Schofield, plus Andy Cruz. This crew brings serious offensive firepower, giving 135 pounds a fresh identity beyond Shakur’s ultra-defensive fencing routine.

Every single one brings a distinct look. Zepeda drowns opponents in relentless volume. Mason pieces together crisp, heavy combos. Schofield loves trading shots in the pocket. Cruz flashes elite technical timing, bringing an offensive arsenal that belongs against the division’s best.

Getting these contenders inside the ropes together is the real challenge now. Deep rankings do not mean much when promotional walls keep top talent apart.

Shakur earned his respect at lightweight, but holding the crown requires actually fighting there. The 135-pound scene has plenty of momentum to move forward, giving Zepeda the green light to take over the division.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Wanted $1.73 Million for Devin Haney
Sports.content:
Liam Paro’s reported $1.73 million asking price was more than Devin Haney wanted to pay for a welterweight unification. The figure offers an explanation for why talks failed to produce a fight between the two champions.

Paro would have brought his IBF belt into a contest with WBO champion Haney. That gave Haney an opportunity to collect another title, but the sides still needed to agree on the cost of making it happen.

Australian journalist Peter Badel described Paro’s financial expectations in comments reported by EverythingBoxing, which credited @JaiMcAllisterx.

“Liam Paro — a little bit has gone quiet there. Look, I’ve been talking to his team. They’ve been a little bit frustrated. They’re trying to get the right fight at the right price for Liam,” Badel said, as quoted by EverythingBoxing. “I’m told he was seeking around 2.5 million Australian dollars [$1.73 million US] for a fight against Haney. Haney didn’t want to pay him that amount.”

EverythingBoxing identified the comments as being eight days old. Badel’s account gives Paro’s reported asking price without revealing Haney’s offer or how far apart the sides were.

Haney’s position involves more than choosing his next opponent. He operates Devin Haney Promotions and has worked through co-promotional agreements, giving him a business interest in the cost of putting a fight together.

Another championship gives Haney something to pursue, but his side must also decide whether an opponent’s price fits the event’s budget. Paro has his own title to bring to negotiations and a financial return he wants from risking it.

The reported $1.73 million request alone does not establish that Paro priced himself out. Equally, declining that figure does not establish that Haney wanted to avoid him.

The missing piece is the counteroffer. Without knowing what Haney’s side offered, it is difficult to judge whether Paro’s expectations prevented an agreement or whether the available money simply fell below his price.

Sports.title: Rico Verhoeven Accepts Deontay Wilder Fight Offer
Sports.content:
Rico Verhoeven has accepted an offer to fight Deontay Wilder on December 11, potentially adding another heavyweight bout to the Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua undercard in Cardiff.

Wilder’s response is still outstanding, and the terms need to be negotiated. However, Verhoeven has made his willingness clear as he looks to continue boxing after his stoppage loss to Oleksandr Usyk.

“I can’t confirm just yet,” Verhoeven told talkSPORT. “What I can tell you is that they offered me the fight. They offered me Deontay Wilder. I said yes.” “The details need to be talked about still. But for that, I’m waiting on a response. So, if there’s a yes from the other side, it’s going to happen.”

Verhoeven did not identify who made the offer. His comments introduce another possible opponent for Wilder, who had been linked with a fight against Jai Opetaia on the same card.

Wilder would give Verhoeven an opportunity to turn the praise he received against Usyk into a victory over an established heavyweight. Going deep into a fight with Usyk earned him attention, but beating Wilder would give him something firmer to build on.

There is an obvious danger in treating Wilder as a faded name to collect. His right hand still gives Verhoeven a reason to be careful. Yet Wilder’s reduced activity and hesitant offense in recent performances could allow the Dutchman time to settle into the fight.

Verhoeven also made clear that he intends to remain in boxing after considering several offers.

“I want to make a statement,” he said. “I want to show that … I am able to transition into the sport of boxing.”

Peter Fury remains in his corner, and Verhoeven is already looking beyond the proposed December appearance. He hopes Joshua beats Fury because he wants that fight himself.

“I hope that Anthony Joshua’s winning that fight because then I’m next for him.”

Beating Wilder would give that ambition a stronger foundation. First, Wilder needs to accept.

Putting Wilder against Verhoeven spares Jai Opetaia a bizarre heavyweight detour that threatened to derail his cruiserweight meeting with David Benavidez. That alone makes it slightly more tolerable than the initial rumor, but it remains a carnival booking.

Wilder has looked completely spent for years. At 40, his trigger is hesitant, his balance is compromised, and the reflex to pull the trigger on his right hand has eroded. Grinding past an aging Derek Chisora by a 12-round split decision did not erase the one-sided beatings he took against Joseph Parker, Fury, or Zhilei Zhang.

Verhoeven, 37, proved his toughness by surviving into the eleventh round against Oleksandr Usyk, but surviving is not contending. He is an elite kickboxer with a tiny boxing resume, still learning basic ring craftsmanship under boxing rules.

Sticking two aging names together with mismatched pedigrees belongs on the preliminary streaming portion of the broadcast, not sharing equal billing right beneath Fury against Joshua. It caters to novelty rather than sport.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Rates Dubois Wardley Rematch Even
Sports.content:
Frank Warren still views Daniel Dubois against Fabio Wardley as a 50-50 fight heading into Saturday night at the O2 Arena in London. Even though Dubois won their violent clash in May, Wardley dropped him in the first and third rounds, proving his power can alter the course of the bout instantly.

Dubois weathered that storm to secure the stoppage, yet those early visits to the canvas give Wardley massive confidence that he can flip the script. The real challenge for Wardley will be finishing the job if he gets Dubois in trouble again.

“I just feel that either of them can win. I think it’s still an even-money fight,” Warren told talkSPORT. “Daniel will go as favorite because he’s probably … got more experience as amateur as well as pro.”

Surviving clean bombs once does not guarantee Dubois can take them a second time. At the same time, reckless aggression could cost either man dearly.

“You’ve got to remember he called for this rematch,” Warren said of Wardley. “It was a brutal fight in May, and here we are now, and it’s on, and he believes that he can win it.”

Warren believes victory hinges on establishing the jab instead of hunting for wild knockout blows right away. For Dubois, a sharp jab keeps Wardley on the outside and stops him from landing cold early.

“For me, the key to this fight is getting behind the jab,” Warren said. “Not looking to lead with big punches, to actually go out and try and … jab and then let your shots go.”

Both heavyweights know what to expect after their first battle. The winner will be the man who made the right adjustments and capitalizes on them first. Neither fighter is built to play it safe, which is why Warren expects another explosive finish before the final bell sounds. Dubois proved his resilience, Wardley proved his firepower, and both step into the ring knowing one clean shot can end it.

When promoters preach boxing fundamentals and patience for a high-profile rematch, they are usually trying to protect their fighters from another grueling brawl. The problem is that fans are paying for fireworks, not a tactical chess match.

“They know each other’s strengths and weaknesses,” Warren said. “It’s who’s learned from the last fight and who can exploit what he’s learned.”

If Dubois and Wardley actually listen to Warren and spend 36 minutes trading cautious jabs from ring center, public reaction will be brutal. Paying premium pay-per-view prices on DAZN just to watch two sluggers neutralize each other behind the lead hand is the exact opposite of what made their May fight thrilling.

“I don’t think the fight’s going to go the distance, whatever happens.”

The thin undercard makes that risk even worse. Here, there is zero safety net. If the headliner devolves into a safety-first sparring session, the whole broadcast will disappoint, and the backlash from paying customers will land squarely on Warren.

Sports.title: Ermal Hadribeaj Taunts Sebastian Fundora Ahead Of Upset Bid
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora gave Ermal Hadribeaj an icy glare during Thursday’s final presser at The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas. Tension spiked when Hadribeaj aimed an imaginary sniper rifle directly at the champion’s chin.

Fundora kept his cool. The towering titlist didn’t swat the hand away. He didn’t shove the challenger. He simply stared him down, leaving the theatrics entirely to the Albanian contender.

Many boxing fans dismiss Saturday’s DAZN broadcast as a total mismatch. They might be forgetting history. Brian Mendoza knocked Fundora out cold in 2023. Erickson Lubin battered him. Tim Tszyu landed heavy leather on him. Those past fights prove the champion absorbs massive punishment when his defense gets sloppy.

The height gap between the two southpaws is ridiculous. DAZN’s faceoff clip showed the eight-inch difference clearly. Hadribeaj stands five feet ten inches tall, forcing him to point his fake rifle skyward toward Fundora’s 6’6″ stature.

Landing real leather will prove vastly tougher than gesturing on stage. Hadribeaj has to slip past huge reaching punches. He must escape clean counters. Closing distance against the champion is tricky because Fundora actually loves trading in tight phone booths.

That exact habit offers Hadribeaj his clearest path toward an upset. Fundora constantly surrenders his height by planting his feet inside. Shorter opponents suddenly find themselves in prime position to connect clean shots.

Mendoza exploited that flaw with a brutal left hook. Hadribeaj hasn’t demonstrated that kind of world class power against elite fighters yet. Still, writing off the challenger ignores the defensive gaps Fundora regularly presents.

The champion stayed composed on stage. Bringing that same discipline into Saturday night keeps the challenger outside, preventing Hadribeaj from getting the messy close-quarters brawl he desperately craves.

Hadribeaj’s taunting is unlikely to get Fundora to fight with reckless anger. Fundora has been through heated build-ups before, taken real damage in wars with Lubin and Tszyu, and generally keeps an even temper outside the ring. At the presser, he watched the sniper pantomime without flinching or retaliating.

The interesting part is that Hadribeaj probably does not even need to make Fundora angry to get the fight he wants. Fundora naturally surrenders his eight-inch height advantage without any emotional prompting. His default setting is to march forward, plant his feet, and throw uppercuts and hooks in a phone booth.

He gives up range as a matter of style, not because his temper got the better of him. That was how Mendoza caught him, and that was how Tszyu landed punishing overhand rights before the cut changed the dynamic.

Hadribeaj’s hurdle is what happens when he actually gets inside. Fundora is lethal in close quarters, throwing sharp uppercuts that chew fighters up as they try to stay under his reach. If Hadribeaj spends energy looking for one theatrical, loaded-up counter shot against a guy who throws heavy volume in the pocket, he risks getting overwhelmed by the sheer number of punches coming back at him.

Sports.title: Devin Haney-Shakur Stevenson Purse Clash Could Sink Fight
Sports.content:
Devin Haney and Shakur Stevenson finally agreed on 145 pounds, but dividing the revenue could scuttle their bout before either man steps into the ring.

Talks have reached a critical point, putting the targeted November 28 date in Atlanta in real jeopardy. Settling on a catchweight gave both camps a clear target. Splitting the revenue creates a deeper rift because it hinges entirely on personal market valuation.

Haney’s November 28 date allows almost no room for further haggling. Just over six weeks remain on the calendar, meaning both boxers require signed contracts right now to launch proper training camps. Every day squandered bickering over percentages pushes that target closer to collapse.

Haney has every right to challenge an even split. He already proved his drawing power as a headline attraction. Agreeing to parity would concede commercial ground that his team believes Shakur has yet to earn.

Backing from Turki Alalshikh changes the financial landscape. Deep financial support guarantees a massive overall purse, but funding a guarantee is not the same as generating revenue through paying customers. Haney’s side will almost certainly demand terms that honor that distinction.

“A potential fight between Devin Haney and Shakur Stevenson is facing obstacles,” Mike Coppinger reported, adding that negotiations were “reaching a critical stage to keep this fight alive.

Coppinger did not reveal the figures being discussed, but if Shakur wants an equal or larger share, that could be where the talks are getting stuck.

Haney holds the cards here. Devin has options, commercial value, and a willing audience. Shakur cannot afford another inactive stretch where he sits around polishing belts while the division moves on without him. If he lets his ego dictate both the scale and the purse split, Haney will simply walk, leaving Shakur with an empty calendar and nobody to blame but himself.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia-Teofimo Lopez Talks Advance For Early 2027
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez are moving closer to a welterweight title fight in the first quarter of 2027, according to Mike Coppinger.

The January-through-March target gives Ryan a major payday to pursue without squeezing in another appearance in December. No firm date or venue was included in the update, and the fight has yet to be announced.

“Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez are now in advanced talks to fight in the first quarter of 2027, sources tell. Expect this welterweight title fight to happen next. And it’s a big one,” said Coppinger on X. “I believe the Garcia-Teo fight will happen regardless of the WBA’s ruling here. Catterall could end up being elevated.”

Teofimo’s WBA mandatory obligation to Jack Catterall remains unresolved, but that doesn’t have to stop the Ryan fight. The WBA belt isn’t needed to sell this matchup. Ryan’s WBC championship would still be available, and the appeal comes largely from putting these two recognizable names together.

The belt’s greater value to Teofimo could be at the negotiating table. Arriving as a fellow champion gives him another argument when discussing his share of the money. Relinquishing it would remove that bargaining point.

However, if Ryan, his promoters, and the financial backers are willing to offer Teofimo comparable money without the WBA title, keeping it becomes harder to justify. He could surrender the belt, remove the mandatory obligation, and proceed directly toward the bigger payday.

Facing Catterall first would introduce a risk that negotiations alone cannot remove. Teofimo could lose, suffer an injury, or come through a difficult fight needing more recovery time. Any of those outcomes could affect the timing or financial terms of a Ryan matchup.

Catterall has publicly opposed stepping aside. The WBA ordered the fight and gave the camps until October 22 to reach an agreement, leaving Teofimo with a decision if the organization insists on enforcing its mandatory.

That makes the financial terms of the Ryan negotiations especially interesting. If the offer depends heavily on Teofimo bringing his championship, he has a reason to seek permission to bypass Catterall. If the money is essentially the same either way, relinquishing offers a straightforward route.

The WBA can determine what Teofimo must do to retain its belt. Whether that belt is worth keeping could ultimately come down to how much Ryan’s side is willing to pay him without it.

Ghana News.title: Mahama announces $2bn annual investment to accelerate industrialisation
Ghana News.content:
President John Dramani Mahama

President John Dramani Mahama has announced plans to invest $2 billion annually over four years under the government’s proposed $10 billion New Economy Programme to accelerate industrialisation, boost production, create jobs and position Ghana as a manufacturing and logistics hub for West Africa.

The President said the programme would channel investment into productive sectors of the economy, with 50% of the funding earmarked for agriculture and agro-processing.

The remaining allocation would support industry and the infrastructure required to connect producers to markets. The initiative is expected to strengthen local production, expand economic opportunities and support Ghana’s ambition to become a regional industrial centre.

President Mahama made the announcement on Thursday, October 15, 2026, when he cut the sod for the commencement of construction works on the Afienya Industrial Park.

The project is expected to expand the country’s industrial capacity, attract investment and create employment opportunities.

He explained that the development was a strategic response to growing investor interest in Ghana and the limited space available at the Tema Export Processing Zone to accommodate new businesses.

Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, who also chairs the Board of the Ghana Free Zones Authority, underscored the importance of securing land free from litigation to support industrial development.

Drawing on her 22 years of experience at the Bar, she said cooperation from traditional authorities and local communities deserved recognition, noting that access to undisputed land was critical to helping businesses establish factories, expand operations and avoid costly delays.

Ghana News.title: Amin Adam urges monthly disclosure of Sinking Fund as Ghana prepares for DDEP repayments
Ghana News.content:
Former Finance Minister Dr Mohammed Amin Adam has called for monthly disclosure of Ghana’s Sinking Fund activities as the country prepares for major repayments under the Domestic Debt Exchange Programme in 2027 and 2028.

The analysis placed the fund’s balance at GH¢15.6 billion on July 22, 2026, against a year-end projection of GH¢30 billion. The government is expected to face DDEP principal repayments of GH¢58 billion in 2027 and GH¢53 billion in 2028, bringing the total to GH¢111 billion over the two years.

Dr Amin Adam said prefunding the Sinking Fund could help smooth the repayment burden, but cautioned that borrowing to accumulate cash could impose additional costs if the fund earned less than the government paid on the debt used to finance it.

“Prefunding is prudent, but it means part of the 2026 increase in debt may be cash held for future redemptions rather than deficit financing,” he wrote.

He recommended that the government publish the fund’s monthly inflows, including the share derived from the allocation of 7% of non-oil tax revenue and any bond proceeds.

The reports, he said, should also show investments, returns, the proportion of the fund financed through borrowing and planned drawdowns. Such disclosure would help the public assess whether the fund was adequately preparing for the repayment cliff and whether its resources were being managed cost-effectively.

Ghana News.title: Stronger banks will fuel business growth and jobs – ADB MD
Ghana News.content:
Managing Director of ADB, Edward Ato Sarpong

The Managing Director of Agricultural Development Bank (ADB) PLC, Edward Ato Sarpong, says stronger capital positions across Ghana’s banking sector will help expand access to credit, support businesses and create sustainable jobs.

He commended the Bank of Ghana (BoG) and the government following the central bank Governor’s announcement that all 23 banks had met their regulatory capital requirements.

Mr Sarpong described the development as an important milestone in building a stable and resilient banking industry capable of supporting investment and economic growth.

He said a well-capitalised banking sector was essential to Ghana’s efforts to strengthen private-sector participation, promote enterprise development, and widen financial inclusion.

According to him, the achievement also underscores the importance of effective regulatory supervision, prudent financial management, and banks' responsibility to maintain strong capital positions.

Strong banks require discipline

Mr Sarpong said the resilience of a banking system must be deliberately built and sustained through disciplined financial management, effective governance, responsible risk-taking and strong regulatory oversight.

He noted that capital strength goes beyond meeting regulatory requirements. It also underpins public confidence, financial stability and the ability of banks to serve businesses and households.

He commended the central bank’s supervisory work and acknowledged the role of a supportive macroeconomic policy environment in helping financial institutions operate sustainably.

Mr Sarpong urged banks to adapt to changing economic conditions and emerging risks while maintaining the confidence of depositors, investors and the public.

Sustaining the gains

The ADB Managing Director called for continued collaboration among the Bank of Ghana, government, banks, investors and other financial sector stakeholders to consolidate the progress made.

He said the milestone presented an opportunity to strengthen Ghana’s appeal as an investment destination, but sustaining the gains would require consistent policy implementation and sound institutional governance.

Mr Sarpong stressed that a stronger banking sector must ultimately contribute to a stronger Ghana.

Ghana News.title: Galamsey: ‘Rivers that fed our grandparents now run the colour of chocolate milk’ – Sam Jonah
Ghana News.content:
Renowned Ghanaian businessman and mining executive Sir Sam Jonah has warned that illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey, is inflicting serious damage on the country’s natural resources, with far-reaching consequences for the economy, public health and the welfare of future generations.

Speaking at the Methodist University Ghana International Conference 2026 on Thursday, October 15, Sir Sam expressed concern about the deteriorating condition of rivers, forests and farmlands, noting that water bodies that once sustained communities had become heavily polluted by mining activities.

“Illegal mining, galamsey, is destroying our rivers, our forests and our farmland. Rivers that fed our grandparents now run the colour of chocolate milk,” he said.

He stressed that the consequences extended beyond environmental degradation to threaten livelihoods, food production, biodiversity and access to safe drinking water.

Pollution of rivers, he noted, could also increase the burden on water treatment systems and the cost of providing potable water to affected communities.

He described the destruction as an economic and public health concern that also raised serious questions about the country’s responsibility to protect its natural heritage.

Sir Sam further argued that the crisis reflected a failure of stewardship, emphasising that responsible conduct should extend beyond land and natural resources to include the management of money and talent.

“It is what happens when people gain all they can and forget Wesley’s condition about not hurting their neighbour. But stewardship is not only about the land. It is also about money and talent,” he said. His remarks were made at the conference organised to commemorate Methodist University Ghana’s 25th anniversary.

Ghana News.title: We have been scammed by NDC, government is only doing PR – Abanga Fuseini
Ghana News.content:
The National Youth Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Abanga Yakubu Fuseini, has accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of failing to fulfil its promises to Ghanaian youth, describing the government’s initiatives as public relations exercises.

He said the NDC had made several promises, particularly on job creation, but young people were yet to see the expected results.

“We have been scammed by the NDC. They are just doing PR,” he said in an interview on Asempa FM’s Ekosii Sen show.

Mr Fuseini said the government continued to launch initiatives without adequately addressing youth unemployment, describing the situation as embarrassing given the expectations created during the election campaign.

He expressed gratitude to delegates and supporters who voted for him, saying his victory demonstrated that consistency and hard work within the NPP could be rewarded.

“I am grateful to all my supporters for voting for me to win. Consistency works in the NPP, so as a youth, if you are working for the party, my advice is that you continue the hard work and your reward will come to you,” he said.

Mr Fuseini said his immediate priority as National Youth Organiser was to mobilise young people across the country and work towards securing victory for former Vice President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia in the 2028 general election.

He urged NPP youth to become ambassadors for Dr Bawumia by communicating his achievements and outlining what he could offer the country if elected President.

“Most of the successful initiatives that are working in this country were championed by the NPP, so we are not intimidated by the NDC,” he said.

Mr Fuseini also outlined his plans for the party’s youth wing, saying he intends to intensify grassroots mobilisation and expand the party’s presence across the country during his first 100 days in office.

He said he was targeting a strong presence in at least six to seven regions as part of efforts to strengthen the party’s structures and prepare for the next general election.

“In my first 100 days in office, I want to capture a lot of regions, at least six to seven regions fully. I am actively working day and night,” he said.

He added that the support he received from delegates had encouraged him to work harder to meet their expectations.

According to him, he had undertaken nearly 84 engagements within his first two weeks in office as part of efforts to connect with party members and advance his mobilisation agenda.

Mr Fuseini said he remained committed to strengthening the NPP’s youth wing and ensuring that young people played a central role in the party’s campaign to return to power.

Ghana News.title: Republic Bank–JoyNews Habitat Fair opens in Ho today
Ghana News.content:
The Republic Bank–JoyNews Habitat Fair opens today, Friday, October 16, at the Ho Sports Stadium, bringing housing opportunities, building solutions and financial services closer to prospective homeowners in the Volta Region.

The three-day event, which runs until Sunday, October 18, brings together property developers, construction companies, building-materials suppliers and other businesses to help visitors take the next step towards owning or building a home.

Nineteen institutions and businesses are participating, giving visitors the opportunity to explore property options, compare products and services, and seek practical guidance for their housing and construction projects.

Republic Bank will engage visitors on banking solutions relevant to their housing and financial needs.

For those exploring property ownership and investment, Nestas Homes Limited, Adonai Estate Limited, and TDC Ghana Limited are among the real estate and property development companies participating.

Visitors planning construction projects can also engage with Lipe Builders & Contractors and Akwaaba Building Materials, as well as suppliers offering products for different stages of the building process.

Interplast will showcase plastic piping and related products, while Vol-link Roofing System and Sintex Tanks will offer roofing and water storage solutions, respectively.

DoorMaster will present door and access solutions, while Virtual Security Africa will provide information on security options for homes and other properties.

MTN is also participating, adding connectivity and digital services to the fair's range of offerings.

Other participating businesses include C Techi GH Limited, Waylead Company GH Ltd, Ayuda App, Rhoyak Ventures, Simef Gold Limited and Lesh Fortune Ltd.

The fair offers prospective homeowners, property investors and people preparing to build a chance to meet exhibitors directly and gather information to guide their decisions.

Ghana News.title: BoG pledges stability to attract investment, urges stronger Africa–Asia partnerships
Ghana News.content:
Dr Mumuni Zakaria, First Deputy Governor, Bank of Ghana

The First Deputy Governor of the Bank of Ghana (BoG), Dr Zakari Mumuni, has reaffirmed the central bank’s commitment to maintaining a stable and credible monetary environment to attract foreign direct investment into Ghana.

He said the bank’s role in safeguarding monetary and financial stability complements fiscal efforts to create an enabling environment for investment.

However, he stressed that the Bank of Ghana and other central banks in the region cannot determine the commercial success of individual investment projects.

Dr Mumuni was speaking at the High-Level West Africa–Asia Capital Dialogue in Bangkok, Thailand, on the sidelines of the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank.

Organised by the ECOWAS Bank for Investment and Development (EBID), the dialogue examined the barriers constraining Asian capital flows into West Africa and the steps needed to unlock greater investment.

Dr Mumuni said central banks have a responsibility to maintain price stability, safeguard financial stability, support efficient payment systems and ensure transparent foreign exchange arrangements.

“Just like other central banks in West Africa, the Bank of Ghana is also interested in innovations that improve cross-border payments and support trade and investment,” he said.

Attracting FDI: Lessons from Ghana

Sharing Ghana’s experience, Dr Mumuni said elevated inflation, exchange rate pressures and debt challenges had required “difficult but necessary policy adjustments and significant reform efforts”.

He said these experiences underscored the importance of macroeconomic stability in attracting and retaining long-term investment.

“Macroeconomic instability increases risk, raises financing costs, and discourages long-term investment,” he said.

Conversely, he noted, price stability, sustainable public finances and credible institutions provide the foundation for private sector growth.

“At the Bank of Ghana, our role is to maintain monetary and financial stability and support confidence in the economy,” Dr Mumuni said.

He stressed, however, that stability alone would not deliver sustainable investment.

“Sustainable investment ultimately depends on a strong pipeline of productive opportunities and competitive businesses,” he said.

Dr Mumuni outlined four priorities to help Ghana and other West African countries attract more investment.

First, he called for better risk-sharing arrangements, with development finance institutions, export credit agencies, governments and private investors working together to allocate risks to those best equipped to manage them.

Second, he urged stronger project preparation, saying a robust pipeline of investment-ready projects was essential to attracting long-term capital.

Third, he advocated financing structures suited to the lifespan of investment projects. He said long-term investments require long-term financing, while greater use of local-currency financing, where feasible, could reduce currency mismatches and improve project viability.

Finally, he called for stronger institutional partnerships that combine Asian capital and expertise with African market knowledge and investment opportunities.

Ghana News.title: Amin Adam warns treasury bill dependence could expose Ghana to refinancing risks
Ghana News.content:
Former Finance Minister Dr Mohammed Amin Adam

Former Finance Minister Dr Mohammed Amin Adam has cautioned that Ghana’s growing reliance on Treasury bills could expose the government to refinancing risks, particularly as substantial domestic debt repayments approach in 2027.

Treasury bill holdings increased from GH¢133.9 billion in January to GH¢165 billion in July 2026, a rise of GH¢31.2 billion, or 23.3%.

Bills consequently increased from 39.3% to 41.6% of domestic debt, significantly above the Medium-Term Debt Strategy benchmark of 15% plus or minus five percentage points.

The analysis also found that the stock of 364-day Treasury bills almost doubled, rising from GH¢49.3 billion to GH¢98.4 billion. Meanwhile, the stocks of 91-day and 182-day bills declined by GH¢11.6 billion and GH¢6.3 billion respectively.

Although the shift towards one-year instruments lengthened the bill portfolio, it concentrated a large volume of repayments around mid-2027.

“A Government that must refinance a large stock every few months is vulnerable to auction undersubscription, sudden yield repricing, and liquidity shocks,” Dr Amin Adam wrote.

He warned that the GH¢31.9 billion in net one-year issuance recorded in June and July would mature in the same year as the first DDEP bond redemptions.

He recommended predictable issuance calendars, stronger benchmark-bond markets and a transparent liability-management framework to reduce the risk of refinancing pressures disrupting public finances.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: China tells Israel to stop ‘forced establishment’ of West Bank settlements
World.content:
“The Palestinian question is the greatest historical injustice of this century,” China’s foreign minister said.

China’s Foreign Minister Wang Yi has told Israeli President Isaac Herzog during a meeting in Azerbaijan that Israel should stop and reverse its “forced establishment” of West Bank settlements, China’s foreign ministry said in a statement.

Wang told Herzog that China has consistently viewed the Palestinian question as the greatest historical injustice of this century, the ministry said in the statement on Friday.

Wang emphasised that the “two-state solution” is the right path to a resolution and said the immediate priority is to fully open access to the Gaza Strip so a humanitarian “catastrophe” is not allowed to spread.

Wang added that China is willing to work with the international community to push all parties to return to dialogue as soon as possible and seek a political settlement.

Wang is attending the Seventh Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia, held in Baku, Azerbaijan, as the special representative of President Xi Jinping, China’s state news agency Xinhua reported.

China urges new Middle East framework

In September, Chinese President Xi Jinping visited Cairo for the first time in a decade and called on Middle East countries to oppose external influence and consider reshaping the region’s security order.

Xi’s rare visit arrived as Beijing seeks to expand its influence in the region amid the US-Israel war on Iran.

The talks covered the US-Israel war on Iran, with both presidents urging “diplomatic solutions” to reach a “comprehensive agreement to end the war”, according to a statement from Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi’s spokesperson.



In March, China criticised the US and Israeli attacks on Iran, with Beijing demanding an immediate halt to the joint attacks. Wang told his Israeli counterpart, Gideon Saar, that the attack on Iran came as negotiations between Washington and Tehran had “made significant progress, including addressing Israel’s security concerns”, China’s foreign ministry said in a statement following the start of the war.

China was Iran’s largest trading partner, buying up to 90 percent of its oil, according to the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission. In 2021, Beijing signed a 25-year “comprehensive strategic partnership agreement” with Tehran.

At the same time, Beijing has spent the past decade cultivating closer ties with Gulf countries, including Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, and remains a top trade partner of both the US and Israel.

World.title: Argentine students protest on campus over Milei’s austerity
World.content:
“This cannot go on!” students shout during an assembly in the middle of the central hall of the University of Buenos Aires Exact and Natural Sciences building.

It is part of Argentina’s prestigious public university system.

The faculty’s central hall is covered with dozens of banners protesting President Javier Milei’s spending cuts. Students have called an assembly to announce the occupation of the university, a traditional form of protest in Argentina meant to raise public awareness and pressure the government.

They say they will take over the building for a day. Many students and professors here are concerned about the impact of Milei’s austerity policies on public universities and say the future of free higher education is at risk.

“Our best professors are leaving en masse. With salaries that cannot cover their basic needs, they are leaving for private universities,” Emiliano Gato, a physics student who is part of the group, told Al Jazeera.

“I dream of doing research and teaching at the public University of Buenos Aires. It’s a prestigious school. But now, with this austerity plan, I don’t know what will happen.”

Public universities in Argentina have become a major battleground of Milei’s austerity plan. Students and professors are protesting the lack of funding and the erosion of salaries, which they say is a major threat to the country’s public education.

Milei is implementing one of the harshest austerity plans in Argentina’s history.



Since taking office in 2023, he has laid off thousands of state employees, shut down ministries, reduced subsidies and cut government-funded programmes. The measures were meant to fight high inflation, which was a major problem in Argentina. Almost three years later, inflation has fallen to around 2 percent a month. Milei says his plan is going well.

“Argentina is growing at a remarkable pace. We have now recorded 27 consecutive months of sustained growth, and today the country is expanding at four times its historical rate. This growth is being felt across almost every sector of the economy,” said Milei during a recent visit to Washington.

Ripple effects

But not everyone agrees. His plan is also having a profound impact on public education, welfare plans for people with disabilities, pensioners and others who depend on state support. The opposition has tried to block many of Milei’s reforms.

Last year, Congress overturned presidential vetoes and approved two laws, one increasing funding for public universities and another declaring a disability emergency. But Milei’s government has refused to implement them, arguing that Congress failed to identify how they would be financed.

A federal judge has now begun fining the government 100,000 pesos (around $70) a day for failing to implement parts of the financing law, which requires Milei’s government to restore university salaries and student scholarships lost to inflation, regularly update budgets and provide funding for research, hospitals and infrastructure.

And that’s why thousands of people took to the streets on Thursday to demand that the government implement it. All around Buenos Aires, long columns of people blocked the centre of the city as they called for a general strike. Although the protest was meant to be peaceful, it soon turned violent. Police fired tear gas and rubber bullets as protesters threw rocks.

The plaza in front of Congress resembled a battleground. At least 25 people were detained, and several others were injured, including members of the security forces.

Maria Teresa de Jesus is a professor in the University of Buenos Aires chemistry department. She says she makes around $700 a month and it has become difficult to make ends meet. “I have come to this protest as a last resort. I am professor. I love teaching, doing research. I shouldn’t be here,” she told Al Jazeera. “Public education is crucial in this country, to make education accessible to all. And the government is ignoring it.”

Many in Argentina continue to support Milei’s economic plan. They are hoping the government’s plan to exploit the country’s vast natural resources will pay off and translate into more jobs, higher wages and improved living standards.



But many others have stopped believing and are prepared to raise the stakes. They accuse Milei’s government of protecting the interests of a privileged few while asking the rest of the country to bear the cost of his economic plan.

World.title: Myanmar’s coup leader-turned-president wins back neighbours despite war
World.content:
From Thailand to Malaysia, ASEAN leaders are embracing Min Aung Hlaing, but critics warn it emboldens a military that is still bombing civilians.

Yangon, Myanmar – When Malaysia invited Myanmar’s coup leader-turned-president Min Aung Hlaing for a visit in September, it insisted the trip did not amount to recognition. The purpose, an official said, was to address the “longstanding issue” of refugees and migrants from Myanmar in Malaysia.

But when Min Aung Hlaing arrived in Kuala Lumpur last week, the former general – whose power grab in 2021 triggered a devastating civil war – received a red carpet welcome, complete with an honour guard.

After an official luncheon on Thursday, Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Myanmar was prepared to take its nationals back at its own cost, a message with appeal in a country where anti-refugee sentiment is growing. Malaysia hosts about 193,000 Myanmar nationals, most of them from the persecuted Rohingya Muslim minority.

“Because the weather is favourable, I will dispatch Navy ships to repatriate them,” Min Aung Hlaing said.

For his part, Anwar pledged to help reintegrate Myanmar into the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), the 11-member regional bloc that has barred Min Aung Hlaing from its high-level meetings for refusing to carry out its peace plan. Malaysia was a vocal supporter of the plan, which is known as the Five Point Consensus and calls for an end to violence and “constructive dialogue” between the warring parties.

The civil war in Myanmar is now in its fifth year and has killed as many as 100,000 people and displaced at least 3.5 million, according to monitoring groups.



“Malaysia will do whatever is possible to make sure that we … ultimately, take Myanmar as part of our community of nations, without prejudice, and particularly in the context of ASEAN,” Anwar told reporters.

Malaysia is the fifth ASEAN nation to host Min Aung Hlaing since he became president in April, after an election held in December and January, which major opposition parties were barred from participating in. In recent months, he has visited Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos.

Following his return from Malaysia, his spokesperson said Indonesia and Brunei could be next.

“Malaysia’s reversal on Min Aung Hlaing has broken a dam of opposition to the junta,” said Bridget Welsh, an honorary research associate at the University of Nottingham’s Asia Research Institute in Kuala Lumpur. She said regional leaders who have welcomed Min Aung Hlaing, despite accusations that he has committed crimes against humanity, were putting pragmatism ahead of human rights.

“It is a step back for ASEAN as an organisation, and for Myanmar,” she said. “It does not offer any concrete path to the resolution of the Myanmar crisis, and in fact, arguably worsens it by giving the military legitimacy internationally, a legitimacy it does not have in Myanmar itself.”

‘Convenience plays a part’

Min Aung Hlaing’s rehabilitation extends beyond Southeast Asia.

Since April, the former general has also visited India, China, Russia and Belarus. At each stop, he has tried to present his government as stable and “on the path to democracy”, while pitching trade and infrastructure deals.

Even the United States appears to have opened the door.

Washington has begun direct talks with Min Aung Hlaing’s government, the Reuters news agency reported last week, despite sanctions on him over human rights abuses. These include the 2017 crackdown on the Rohingya, which sent more than 700,000 people fleeing into Bangladesh and which the US has called a genocide.

Reuters said the latest talks have focused on shutting down scam centres operating from Myanmar that have defrauded Americans of billions of dollars.

Khin Zaw Win, director of the Tampadipa Institute in Yangon, said Min Aung Hlaing’s quest for international legitimacy has been aided by a coordinated push from China, India and Thailand, all of which share borders with Myanmar. The three neighbours have experienced spillover from the war, such as fighting near their borders, disrupted trade and influxes of refugees.

Khin Zaw Win said the three countries “have the biggest stakes in how Myanmar pans out” and want the military-installed government recognised. Russia and Belarus, meanwhile, are both major arms suppliers to Myanmar, and Naypyidaw has backed Moscow’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine.



“Convenience plays a part for all of them,” he said.

The growing diplomatic recognition, however, has done little to resolve the conflict.

While Min Aung Hlaing has invited all armed groups to peace talks, fighting continues to rage across much of the country. His forces have launched offensives to retake territory lost to opposition armed rebels and ethnic armed groups in Rakhine, Chin, Kachin and Karen states and the Sagaing region. They have been aided by an intensified air campaign and a recruitment drive that has added tens of thousands to their ranks. China, too, has helped by brokering ceasefires between the military and powerful ethnic armed groups on its border.

Still, Laetitia van den Assum, a former Dutch diplomat, said the military is unlikely to regain control of the whole country.

“That would require a huge occupation army and not – as now – a garrison army that controls a particular location,” she said. “That is why Min Aung Hlaing… bets on an increasing number of temporary ceasefires in some parts of the country so that troops can be directed to areas where he wants to continue fighting”.

Van den Assum said she found it “quite surprising” that ASEAN nations are seeking Rohingya repatriation from the very man accused of orchestrating crimes against them.

Myanmar has long denied the Rohingya citizenship, so it is unclear whether it would accept them as nationals. And with much of Rakhine State – their homeland – now held by the ethnic Arakan Army, it is far from clear where they would go.

“It is the blind speaking to the blind,” she said.

‘Low-cost, high optics’

Min Aung Hlaing has made other gestures.

Shortly before his trip to Thailand in August, he allowed the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) to see Aung San Suu Kyi, the civilian leader he deposed in 2021. The 81-year-old Nobel laureate has been held incommunicado since the coup, and the ICRC visit on August 3 produced her first photographs in years.

Sai Kyi Zin Soe, a research fellow at the University of Sydney, called the move a “low-cost, high-optics gesture rather than a real political opening”. The visit confirmed only that Aung San Suu Kyi is alive, “nothing more”, he said.

He noted that the military’s air raids have continued unabated even as ASEAN leaders roll out the red carpet, including a September 28 strike on a market in Rakhine State that killed an estimated 50 people.

The continuing attacks, he said, were the “strongest evidence that soft diplomacy hasn’t produced any deterrent effect”.

Sai Kyi Zin Soe also warned that the legitimacy conferred by the foreign visits would embolden the military further.

“Given the near-total absence of deterrence, no meaningful sanctions enforcement, an ASEAN pivoting toward re-engagement, and continued arms and fuel access via China and Russia, the military has every structural incentive to keep escalating, particularly in contested zones like Sagaing and Rakhine, where its grip is weakest,” he said.

Much now depends on the Philippines and Singapore, ASEAN’s current and incoming chairs.



Phil Robertson, director of Asia Human Rights and Labor Advocates, said the two countries must set an agenda that pushes back hard on entreaties from others in the region to allow “Myanmar fully back into the fold” and keep pressing the bloc’s five-point peace plan.

He also urged the US, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and the European Union to adopt targeted sanctions, such as an aviation fuel ban, rather than leaving “the whole Myanmar conundrum” to the regional bloc.

“International accountability is now more urgent than ever, whether that comes through additional universal jurisdiction cases or some sort of breakthrough to refer Myanmar’s generals to the International Criminal Court,” he added.

Zaheena Rasheed reported and wrote from Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.

World.title: Three children and teacher killed in US primary school shooting
World.content:
"We are stunned and heartbroken by this senseless tragedy," Steven Cook, the top administrative official of the local school district, said in a statement.

"No words can adequately express the grief our community is experiencing."

Police said the attacker was a local 16-year-old boy, but they did not release any further details on him or the identity of the victims.

Police were alerted to an active shooter at Silver Rail Elementary at 12:59 local time, Bend Police Department spokeswoman Sheila Miller told reporters.

The first call came from a person who said that an unknown suspect was shooting into their car with a long gun, police said. Photos released from the scene show a red truck with bullet holes.

Minutes later, the local county dispatch received 911 calls reporting that the attacker had entered the school.

Police said he shot at locks on the doors in order to force his way inside.

Local media reports suggested the school received new classroom doors in 2022 which can be locked with the flip of a switch.

A bystander saw the shooting begin to unfold, pursued the attacker into the school and shot him dead, police said.

Three minutes later, officers first arrived at the scene. They confirmed that the attacker had been killed, and then searched the school.

World.title: 'It's really hard to believe' - How Oregon primary school shooting unfolded
World.content:
Four victims, including a teacher and three children aged 5, 8 and 11, were killed in a shooting at a primary school in the US state of Oregon, local police say.

A 16-year-old suspect forced his way into the school by firing at locked doors. He was also killed in the shooting by an armed member of the community who followed the suspect inside the school, police said at a press conference.

Two additional victims, a 7-year-old and another teacher, were hurt and transported to hospital in critical condition.

World.title: Ship attack reports near Hormuz reach record high as oil exports slow
World.content:
The number of ships that have reported being attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz has hit a record high, BBC Verify analysis of data from a UK maritime agency shows.

Twelve vessels were attacked between 5 and 11 October - the largest number of weekly strikes reported to the UK's Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) agency since the US-Israeli war with Iran began. The previous week saw 10 ships reporting attacks.

Six of the vessels were struck last Sunday, according to the UKMTO - a one-day high. So far this week, there have been four reported attacks.

As the number of strikes has risen, the recovery in oil shipments through the strait seen last month has slowed, industry data suggests.

BBC Verify collated incident reports published by the UKMTO on its website and created a timeline based on the first date cited in each report. This is approximate because some incidents use the date of the attack and some the date on which it was reported.

World.title: Trump calls off livestream of Fort Hood attacker's execution by firing squad
World.content:
US President Donald Trump has called off plans to livestream the execution of former US army psychiatrist Nidal Hasan by firing squad.

Trump had previously said he approved of showing the death of the Fort Hood attacker, while Vice-President JD Vance cast doubt on whether it would happen and said he would not watch it.

Trump's decision to cancel the livestream came after widespread criticism in the US and globally. On Thursday, he said that "many very good and well meaning people would rather not watch him die".

"I think streaming the execution for all to see might have been a strong deterrent for the World to witness how America deals with Terrorists and SCUM like Hasan," Trump said.

"He will die, as scheduled, by firing squad, but this event will not be streamed," the president added in the post on Truth Social.

Hasan fatally shot 13 unarmed US military personnel and injured 32 others at a military base in Texas in 2009. His execution by firing squad will be the first military execution in more than 60 years.

Trump said the families of the victims can still view the execution in person if they wish.

"They deserve to witness JUSTICE!" he said.

After the Pentagon announced last week that it would execute Hasan on 3 December 2026 by firing squad and livestream the event, a cascade of criticism quickly followed from human rights groups and many others. The United Nations called the plans "abhorrent".

While there were more than 2,700 executions across 17 countries last year, only two nations carried them out publicly. According to Amnesty International, 11 public executions were known to have been carried out in Iran in 2025 and another six in Afghanistan.

US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth defended his decision to air Hasan's execution online, saying that "people need to understand that there's serious consequences for these types of things".

World.title: Russia accuses Ukraine of attacking oil refinery after Zelensky says strikes to resume
World.content:
The Kremlin said Kyiv had "attempted a large-scale attack" on a refinery south of Moscow early on Thursday.

According to Russia's defence ministry, four missiles and dozens of drones were intercepted and the falling debris caused a fire at the site in Ryazan.

Zelensky said dozens of Ukrainian cities had come under Russian attack in the past day.

He previously said he would agree to the "energy ceasefire" announced by US President Donald Trump on Sunday if Moscow also abided by it.

But he accused Russia of ignoring the proposed deal within hours of it being announced, with strikes leaving hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians without power. The Kremlin never said it had agreed to the deal.

Zelensky agreed that he felt betrayed by the US when asked by Piers Morgan on Wednesday night, after Washington appeared to withdraw key elements of its support.

European leaders have rallied around the Ukrainian president. Italy's Defence Minister Guido Crosetto told the BBC that the US restricting its intelligence-sharing with Kyiv would be a "complete mistake".

"Because it is a fundamental form of support. This means denying a country any chance of defending itself."

He added: "Peace will be achieved when Putin will be convinced that there is a stalemate... that he cannot advance anymore. But if he sees a weakness on the Ukrainian front, if the United States takes its resources away, then Putin will think he can win, and so he will continue the war."
