Zelensky met Nato chief Mark Rutte as a two-day summit of European leaders began in Brussels on Thursday. The head of the military alliance said they had discussed "the importance of implementing an energy ceasefire as well as Nato allies' continuous support for Ukraine".

Zelensky told the FT that Ukrainian officials had been told by US counterparts that "if you will not stop [the strikes], we will block intelligence".

Ukraine's military relies on US early-warning alerts of incoming Russian aerial attacks to mount air defences, limiting successful strikes, while Starlink internet links are used throughout its war effort to guide drones and protect its skies.

There were suggestions a technical glitch was to blame for the sudden Starlink restrictions on Tuesday evening, but owner Elon Musk appeared to deny this and suggested it was the Trump administration's doing.

"It was not a technical problem, it was the will," Zelensky told the FT.

Trump has denied halting intelligence-sharing. Starlink's sister service Starshield is provided to Ukraine under a US defence department contract. The BBC has approached the US authorities for comment.

World.title: Bus hits train stopped on French side of Channel Tunnel, with 19 injured
World.content:
"Two trains were on either side of the platform. One was being loaded by heavy goods vehicles ahead of a cross-Channel journey, and another train that had previously been loaded was departing," Cury said.

"For a reason that currently remains unknown, the minibus collided with the departing train.

"The bus did not overturn, it is still upright â but the shock and the collision caused injuries to the people involved."

The incident involved a minibus transporting workers who were about to board Le Shuttle. All were men of different nationalities, she added.

It is not clear whether any British nationals are among the injured.

Cury said it was "the first time an incident of this type has occurred" on an Eurotunnel loading platform.

The BBC's Evan Davis, who was travelling through the Eurotunnel to Calais at the time of the incident, witnessed blue light vehicles "concentrated on one of the platforms" as he entered France.

"There were plenty of cars queueing up at check-in when I drove past just now, and I saw some cars going through check-in, so despite the collision they weren't being held," he said from the scene.

Photos published by local French newspaper La Voix du Nord, external showed a small bus with damage to its front and side standing alongside a train, among a crowd of emergency workers.

Eurostar has released an update saying: "An incident occurred several kilometers away from the Channel Tunnel.

"This incident does not involved or impact Eurostar trains running from and to London. All of Eurostar trains will run as expected."

World.title: Maduro pleads not guilty to new torture-related charges in New York
World.content:
Venezuela's former leader NicolÃ¡s Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, appeared in court on Thursday to plead not guilty to new charges of conspiracy to commit torture.

The US government initially accused Maduro of narco-terrorism, drug trafficking and weapons-related offenses, before adding new charges against him and Flores last week.

Maduro and Flores were captured in January during a US military raid, after which they were taken to New York, where they remain in jail.

The couple has pleaded not guilty to the allegations and both have argued to have the case thrown out on the grounds that they qualify for sovereign immunity. Their trial is scheduled for June 2027.

In a new indictment last week, government prosecutors alleged Maduro and Flores "created and maintained a violent system of repression" that saw "thousands of Venezuelans" killed, harassed, and tortured.

Nicolas Maduro denied the new charges brought against him by the US government, telling a court on Thursday he denied the "false accusations and false testimony against me."

"I reject this document entirely," Maduro said in Spanish through a translator.

Judge Alvin Hellerstein interrupted Maduro, and declared the court would enter a plea of not guilty for Maduro.

"I am completely innocent. I am not guilty," Flores said through a translator.

Maduro and Flores wore beige jail uniforms and both appear to have lost weight during their detention in Brooklyn.

The alleged torture methods included "electric shock, asphyxiation, rape, forced nudity, prolonged isolation, starvation, punishment cells, and psychological torture", the indictment states.

The US also accused Maduro of authorising the use of torture "against specific individuals" and alleges US citizens were tortured under this system.

Prosecutors already have accused Maduro, his wife and son, and their accomplices of engaging in a cocaine-trafficking conspiracy and partnering with cartels designated as terrorist groups.

Maduro previously called such charges a tool to further "imperial" plans for getting access to Venezuela's rich oil reserves.

He and his wife's lawyers have argued that Maduro is the leader of a sovereign country and therefore immune from prosecution. They contend the US taking him by force is illegal.

Flores unsuccessfully petitioned a judge to allow her to be released on bond while she awaited trial, arguing she had heart problems and other health issues while detained at the notorious Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn.

World.title: At least 33 pupils and teacher killed after school roof collapses in Pakistan
World.content:
At least 33 pupils and a teacher have been killed after a school roof collapsed in the north-western Pakistani city of Peshawar, according to hospital officials.

More than a dozen others are injured, with some in a critical condition.

Emergency services were called to the private Al-Khair school in Dir Colony at 08:48 (03:48 GMT) on Thursday after lessons had begun, rescue official Bilal Faizi told the BBC.

The roof of an upper-floor classroom had collapsed, he said, causing ceilings below to cave in and trap children beneath the debris.

Announcing the arrest of the school's owner, police chief Mian Saeed promised a thorough inquiry into "whether there were any violations of building codes".

Warning: This article contains distressing details

An English teacher from a nearby school said he immediately rushed to the site with other local residents when they heard sirens and the sound of ambulances.

Together, they pulled more than 20 children from the rubble, he said.

"I personally pulled out six children with my own hands. Most of them were alive and talking. But later it was found that they had passed away."

"There was a lot of blood," he said. "One child said he was in a lot of pain. His tongue had dried up in his mouth, [and he was] asking for water."

Sohail, another local resident, said he and others tried to remove children from under the rubble "using shovels".

World.title: Mining cooperation: A new chapter in China-Africa common development, By Yu Dunhai
World.content:
On 13 October, 2026, Chinese President Xi Jinping put forth a four-point proposition on advancing China-Africa mining cooperation during his meeting with President Duma Gideon Boko of Botswana, who was on a state visit to China. Grounded in the profound transformation of the global critical minerals landscape and Africa’s urgent need for independent development, and anchored in the broader context of traditional China-Africa friendship, the proposition charts the course for China-Africa mining cooperation in the new era.

As the Chinese Ambassador to Nigeria, I am keenly aware of the strategic vision, forward-looking perspective, and practical relevance of these four points. They present a concrete embodiment of the concept of a China-Africa community with a shared future, and provide strong support for Nigeria and other African countries in transforming their resource endowment into development dividends. Drawing on the realities of China-Nigeria mining cooperation, I would like to share with Nigerian friends a deeper understanding of the rich substance of this four-point proposition.

First, we must adhere to the principle that African resources belong to Africa. This is the fundamental premise of mining cooperation with African nations. Africa has long been locked at the lower end of global industrial and value chains by an inequitable international division of labour–a historical injustice that must be corrected. Resource sovereignty is an integral component of national sovereignty, and the ability to control one’s own resource destiny is the cornerstone of sustainable development for African countries. China fully understands and respects Africa’s legitimate aspirations. We have always respected the development paths independently chosen by African countries and stand ready to share our experience to help them formulate mining development plans suited to their national conditions. China supports Nigeria and other African countries in independently charting their mining development paths, ensuring that decision-making power and the benefits of resource development remain firmly in their own hands.

Second, we must uphold the principle of pursuing the greater good and shared interests, and seeking mutual benefit and win-win results. This is the core philosophy of China-Africa mining cooperation. In conducting mining cooperation, China and Africa must uphold a correct view of righteousness and benefit. China never pursues unilateral maximization of benefits in its cooperation with Africa, and always adheres to win-win cooperation and common development. In Nigeria, Chinese enterprises involved in energy and mining sector not only bring capital and technology, but also adhere to localized operations, and attach importance to skills training and community contributions. The Chinese Embassy will continue to guide Chinese enterprises in Nigeria to enhance their operational capabilities, transfer green technologies, strengthen public welfare assistance, drive local employment and talent training, and promote South-South cooperation in the mining sector.

Third, we must pursue high-quality development. This is the direction of progress for China-Africa mining cooperation. Promoting local processing, extending industrial chains and increasing value addition are the key pathways for Africa to convert resource advantages into development strength. China has always been a doer in supporting Africa’s development and will continue to drive the transformation of China-Africa mining cooperation towards higher industrial value addition. We will deepen the alignment between China’s 15th Five-Year Plan and Nigeria’s “Renewed Hope” Agenda, push projects further into deep processing and high-value-added segments, and help Nigeria build a more complete industrial system. In this way, resources can truly become a driver of modernisation rather than a source of so-called “resource curse.”

Fourth, we must maintain a fair and open cooperation environment. This is an important safeguard for mining cooperation with Africa. Africa’s resources should never be turned into tools of geopolitical rivalry. Any attempt to politicize or instrumentalize African resource issues as well as to create confrontation and division will seriously damage the fundamental interests of the African people. China consistently advocates open cooperation and fair competition. We welcome all parties that genuinely wish to support Africa’s development and stand ready to work with African partners to maintain a stable and predictable market environment for mining cooperation, thereby creating more favourable conditions for enterprise investment and operations. China is ready to join hands with Nigeria in rejecting any attempt to treat mineral resources as bargaining chip in geopolitical games, ensuring that resource development always serves development and benefits the people.

I would like to emphasise in particular that the Chinese government requires all Chinese enterprises and citizens in Nigeria to strictly abide by Nigerian laws and regulations and to operate in a lawful and compliant manner. We maintain a zero-tolerance policy toward illegal mining and other criminal activities. China supports Nigeria in taking strong measures to strengthen mining governance. The facts show that the overwhelming majority of Chinese mining enterprises in Nigeria operate in accordance with the law, actively fulfil their social responsibilities and protect the environment. Isolated and inaccurate allegations that exaggerate individual cases or distort the facts are neither fair nor conducive to the overall China-Nigeria friendship and cooperation. We stand ready to work with the Nigerian side to further regulate market order, jointly combat illegal mining, and foster a healthy and transparent business environment.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

China and Africa share a common future and a bright outlook. Mechanism platforms such as the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation continue to provide solid support, while the dividends of China’s zero-tariff policy for all diplomatic partners in Africa continue to unfold, creating favourable conditions for deeper China-Africa cooperation. I am convinced that as long as both sides uphold mutual respect and mutual benefit, we can turn Africa’s resource endowment into tangible development outcomes, deliver greater benefits to the Chinese and African peoples, and make greater contributions to building a China-Africa community with a shared future.

China stands ready to work hand in hand with Nigeria and other African countries to fully implement President Xi Jinping’s four-point proposal on China-Africa mining cooperation, write a new chapter of high-quality development in China-Africa mining cooperation, ensure that Africa’s resources truly serve the development of the African people, and make China-Africa mining cooperation a model of South-South cooperation and an important force in advancing Africa’s modernisation.

Yu Dunhai is the Chinese ambassador to Nigeria.

World.title: Child Trafficking: Police rescue 11-year-old girl
World.content:
The police in Ebonyi State have rescued an 11-year-old girl, allegedly abducted in May 2026 by a child trafficking syndicate.

Joshua Ukandu, the police spokesperson in Ebonyi, told reporters in Abakaliki on Thursday.

Mr Ukandu, a superintendent of police, said the breakthrough followed months of sustained and discreet investigations into the girl’s abduction and the activities of the suspected trafficking syndicate.

He said police operatives traced and arrested Nneka Ibekwe at Nkpor, Onitsha, Anambra, on 6 October over her alleged involvement in the crime.

According to him, preliminary investigations revealed that Mrs Ibekwe allegedly purchased the girl from the syndicate in June 2026.

Mr Ukandu said Mrs Ibekwe told investigators that she approached Benedicta Umeh, also known as Nwanyi-Okigwe, after learning that she operated an orphanage and allegedly worked with welfare office officials to facilitate child adoptions.

He added that Mrs Ibekwe claimed she had expressed interest in adopting a child and was asked to provide a consent letter from her church and a medical certificate of fitness.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The police spokesperson said Mrs Ibekwe further alleged that she paid about ₦4 million to Mrs Umeh before the child was handed over to her, adding that the claims remained subject to further investigation.

He said the rescued girl was safe, while efforts were ongoing to reunite her with her family.

Mr Ukandu said the Commissioner of Police in Ebonyi, Hope Okafor, commended the officers for their diligence and commitment to the investigation.

He said Mrs Okafor assured the public that anyone found culpable would face the law.

She also advised prospective adoptive parents to conduct proper investigations and follow due process before taking custody of any child.

The police commissioner urged members of the public to remain vigilant and promptly report suspicious activities involving children to the nearest police station.

World.title: One in four children under five stunted in Akwa Ibom, survey shows
World.content:
Nearly one in four children under five in Akwa Ibom State is stunted, highlighting the scale of chronic malnutrition confronting the state as the government moves to coordinate nutrition interventions across its 31 local government areas.

The 2023–2024 Nigeria Demographic and Health Survey (NDHS) puts the prevalence of stunting in Akwa Ibom at 24.1 per cent, confirming figures cited by the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF). Nationally, 40 per cent of children under five are stunted, according to the survey.

Stunting occurs when children are too short for their age because of chronic undernutrition. It can impair physical growth and brain development, undermine learning and affect productivity in adulthood.

The figures were highlighted on Tuesday during the inauguration of Local Government Committees on Food and Nutrition across Akwa Ibom’s 31 local government areas.

The Akwa Ibom State Ministry of Budget and Economic Planning organised the event in Uyo in collaboration with UNICEF.

UNICEF’s nutrition specialist, Oluniyi Oyedokun, said the state’s stunting burden required coordinated action to address the factors responsible for childhood malnutrition.

He explained that stunting is linked to inadequate nutrition, particularly during the first 1,000 days of a child’s life, from conception to the second birthday.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The period is critical for physical growth and brain development. Prolonged nutritional deprivation during this stage can have lasting consequences for children’s health and development.

Mr Oyedokun warned that stunted children face an increased risk of impaired cognitive development, poor school performance, frequent illnesses and reduced productivity in adulthood.

He said establishing nutrition committees in all 31 local government areas was intended to bring interventions closer to communities and strengthen implementation of the National Policy on Food and Nutrition.

He called for collaboration among the health, agriculture, education, water and sanitation sectors, noting that tackling malnutrition requires action beyond the health sector.

The Akwa Ibom State Government said the committees would coordinate, monitor and implement nutrition interventions in their respective local government areas.

The Commissioner for Budget and Economic Planning, Nsikan Nkan, said the inauguration of the 217-member committees aligned with Governor Umo Eno’s ARISE Agenda, which prioritises human capital development and a healthy, productive population.

The committees are expected to improve coordination among relevant government agencies and other stakeholders in addressing food insecurity and malnutrition at the grassroots.

World.title: Senate probes death of ex-SUG president in Enugu NYSC camp
World.content:
The Nigerian Senate has ordered an investigation into the death of a member of the National Youth Service Corps (NYSC), Etimbuk Daniel, at the NYSC camp in Enugu State.

PREMIUM TIMES previously reported that Mr Daniel died while undergoing his compulsory three-week orientation course at the NYSC.

The deceased corps member was the immediate past president of the Students’ Union Government (SUG) of the Akwa Ibom State University. He hailed from Akwa Ibom State, South-South Nigeria.

Investigation

Anietie Ekong, a media aide to the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, announced the Senate’s decision to investigate the NYSC member’s death in a statement posted on Facebook on Thursday.

The media aide said the Senate resolved to investigate Mr Daniel’s death following a motion of urgent public importance moved by Akwa Ibom North-East Senator Aniekan Bassey, calling for a review of medical services in NYSC camps nationwide.

He said the upper chamber resolved that the investigation would be carried out by the Senate Committees on Police Affairs, Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters, Ethics, Code of Conduct and Public Petitions, as well as Youth Development and Health.

Mr Ekong said the committees would carry out the probe in conjunction with the Nigeria Police Force and the State Security Service.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the Senate would also investigate the state of health infrastructure in NYSC camps across the country.

He said the Senators noted with concern the sudden, untimely death of the NYSC member, describing him as a vibrant, patriotic young Nigerian and a shining light in his community who had only set out to serve the country.

The media aide said the lawmakers equally expressed concern over reports that Mr Daniel died from complications arising from a “minor” headache after allegedly experiencing a delay in obtaining timely and adequate medical attention at the camp clinic.

He said the Senate further expressed worry that the incident was not isolated, but highlighted a recurring pattern of systemic negligence, poor medical infrastructure, and absence of qualified emergency personnel and rapid referral protocols across NYSC camps.

World.title: 2027: On election day, APC will realise they’ve made very serious mistakes – Kwankwaso
World.content:
The 2027 vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, has tackled 31 Nigerian governors for backing President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid instead of working in their states.

Mr Kwankwaso, a former governor of Kano State, spoke on Channels TV’s Politics Today on Thursday night.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that at least 31 governors have publicly endorsed the 2027 re-election bid of Mr Tinubu of the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC).

Some of the governors – such as Osun State’s Ademola Adeleke and Anambra’s Charles Soludo – are not members of the APC.

Speaking on the Channels TV show, Mr Kwankwaso argued that both the governors and Mr Tinubu were teaming up ahead of the 2027 general elections because they lacked confidence in winning re-elections on their own.

“I think a lot of mistakes were being made by the governors to the extent that they themselves believe that they are not competent enough to win elections on their own.

“Therefore, they had to lean towards the president. And I believe the president also believes that he can’t do it himself. He has to lean towards the governors,” he said.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

‘APC and governors are worried about NDC, Peter Obi’s popularity’

Mr Kwankwaso boasted that the NDC presidential candidate, Peter Obi, is very popular in Southern Nigeria ahead of the 2027 elections.

He also argued that the NDC had gained a strong presence in northern Nigeria and that the party now has a “formidable team” given that many Nigerians seeking to solve the country’s problems are with the party.

The former governor believes the NDC’s popularity has become a concern for the governors backing Mr Tinubu’s re-election bid.

“I believe that there is no governor who is not concerned about the popularity of our candidate, the ticket itself, and of course our party.

“So I personally believe that the governors don’t understand the dynamics now. But I believe that on election day, they will realise that the APC has made very serious mistakes over the years,” he said.

‘Hardship and insecurity will make Tinubu and the APC fail’

Mr Kwankwaso argued that Mr Tinubu and the APC’s popularity have diminished due to growing hardship and insecurity across the country.

“The issue of security, especially in northern Nigeria. The issue of poverty, everybody is very much aware of it.

“You can see that the major issues in this country are not being addressed,” he said.

Continuing, the politician said: “People are in a very difficult situation today. Many of them have left their villages and towns and have been away for many years now.

READ ALSO: Mbah speaks on shootings at NDC secretariat

“But I can tell you, outside here, and even here in Abuja, people are very angry. And people are looking for a way out.”

The NDC vice-presidential candidate then expressed concern that the ruling APC might rig the 2027 election.

“Normally, as politicians, if they (APC) realise that they are not popular and that they are not being loved by their people, the tendency is for them to start thinking of ways and manners (to rig the elections).

“And we have heard many of them, especially the people around them, that as usual, they are boasting that even if they get 1,000, they will write the result for themselves,” he said.

World.title: Will a Nobel solve the world’s Trump problem? The president thinks so, By Azu Ishiekwene
World.content:
The trouble remains that the US, under a MAGA-shared delusion, railroaded a demagogue to the White House, and must imagine that their hysteria would press the world, including the Nobel Committee, to bestow a laurel on a gangster hero.

US President Donald Trump doesn’t just think a Nobel will solve the world’s Trump-inflicted problems. He believes it. He has said, quite clearly, that he deserves a Nobel Peace Prize for his extraordinary labour of peace, especially in his second term.

He claims he has ended eight wars, from the Israel-Hamas War to the Israel-Iran War, the India-Pakistan War, the Thailand-Cambodia War, and the DR Congo-Rwanda War.

Can you think of anyone who has, in his words, saved millions of lives and done so much for world peace and security in the last nearly two years? And each settled war, for Trump, is the equivalent of one Nobel – eight prizes in all, yet he has been denied even one!

He’s not the only important person who thinks he has done what Napoleon could not do, and yet remains largely despised. In a meeting at the White House in January, the Venezuelan opposition leader, Marina Corina Machado, presented Trump with her 2025 Nobel Peace Prize gold medal, to right the wrong of the Nobel Committee.

Proxy Medal Not Enough

Yet, the proxy medal has not appeased Trump. From his reaction when the Committee announced the 2026 winners in Oslo last week, the President is dying to get the real thing. That prize appears to be worth more than the combined value of Cuba, Greenland, the Strait of Hormuz, and the rash of trade tariffs.

He used bad words on the Nobel Committee, describing it as “forever discredited” and calling the members “a handful of radical ideologues who are anti-democracy and really enemies of civilisation.”

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Trump also launched an attack on the prize winner, Navi Pillay, calling her a “mystery person nobody has ever heard of.”

Solicitation As Strategy

Solicitation is a rare thing in the history of the Nobel. But what Trump cannot undo does not exist. In the cases of Leo Tolstoy and Albert Einstein, there were repeated third-party nominations, never a demand for the prize from the nominees or the nominators. The nomination of Adolf Hitler by a Swedish parliamentarian in 1939 was clearly a parody, and the nomination was quickly withdrawn.

This is why the 2026 Nobel Prize for Peace will go down in the records as one of a kind. Not just the laureate but the committee, the domicile country and the International Criminal Court are all in hot water because of the outrage of a sore loser.

Yet, the Trump-engineered ceasefire in Gaza has turned out to be a bloody campaign under a white banner. More than a year since the ceasefire came into effect on 10 October, 2025, international monitoring groups and independent news analyses note that Israel has conducted daily air and drone strikes – attacking the territory on roughly 325 out of the first 361 days of the “ceasefire.”

President Trump has updated his list of “disgraced countries,” once an exclusively African collection, to include Norway, perhaps making it a list to be proud of.

Who Nominated Trump?

Who nominated Trump for a Nobel Peace Prize? The Nobel Committee reportedly keeps lists of nominees and nominators confidential. It neither confirms nor denies claims during the period. Last year, US Republican House of Representatives member for Florida, Anna Paulina Luna, publicly announced that she nominated the President for his self-acclaimed role in brokering the Israel-Hamas ceasefire.

Yet, the Trump-engineered ceasefire in Gaza has turned out to be a bloody campaign under a white banner. More than a year since the ceasefire came into effect on 10 October, 2025, international monitoring groups and independent news analyses note that Israel has conducted daily air and drone strikes – attacking the territory on roughly 325 out of the first 361 days of the “ceasefire.”

According to data from the Gaza Ministry of Health and UN Humanitarian reports, at least 1,493 Palestinians, including women and children, have been killed. Also, about 5,299 people have been wounded during the ceasefire. While Trump covets the peace prize, Israel continues to breach the ceasefire without consequence.

Bombings, shootings, restrictions, encroachment by Israeli settlers, expropriation, theft of livestock and farm produce, and blockade of access to food and medicines in Gaza continue under the full glare of the peacemaker, Trump.

If that’s the ceasefire for which even Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif is also reported to have nominated Trump for a peace prize, then they left the Nobel Committee no chance other than simply to create a new Prize for War.

MAGA Delusions

The trouble remains that the US, under a MAGA-shared delusion, railroaded a demagogue to the White House, and must imagine that their hysteria would press the world, including the Nobel Committee, to bestow a laurel on a gangster hero.

The dilemma of Trump and his supporters was captured in the press conference on Iran, where the US Secretary of State, Marco Rubio, laid out the Middle East conflict in stark, anachronistic rhetoric. It’s a tragedy that the Trump White House is wantonly destroying the world order of peace and security and damaging institutions that the US was at the forefront of building after World War II – institutions that have served the US and the world well, despite their shortcomings.

Meanwhile, from Europe to the Middle East, and from Asia to Africa and North America, the world is reeling from the blows of the rash policies of this Nobel-Laureate-Wannabe, and paying the price in supply chain disruptions, rising inflation, geopolitical tensions, and worsening global misery.

The Nobel Committee recognised Pillay for “pressing states and national leaders to comply with the rule of law,” a subject in which the Trump administration has set one of the worst precedents ever. Pillay, a worthy recipient of the peace prize, had variously chaired investigations into serious human rights violations in places like Myanmar, Rwanda and Gaza – the last one an active crime scene where Trump’s policies have enabled travesties.

L’État, C’est Moi.

Trump didn’t stop at attacking the Committee. Being the state and the grandmaster rolled into one like Louis XIV of France, he has got the US to impose sanctions on the ICC; sanctions that are as doomed as his adventures in the Strait of Hormuz.

The indictment of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and the likely future indictment of Trump for war crimes in Gaza and Iran, respectively, by the ICC, must be upsetting to Trump, who wishes to “obliterate” every suspicion with a grand Nobel.

As he did to undermine the UN – instituting a Board of Peace filled with carefully chosen billionaire oil sheikhs – Trump might well be considering a parallel award in the class of the Nobel Prize, even if the sole objective is to give him this proze. That’s how much the president craves recognition to evade accountability.

Midterm Blues? Perhaps

Unfortunately, the world is stuck with these hallucinations for the remainder of Trump’s term – which seems like an eternity. The flicker of hope that the mid-term elections might produce a Democratic majority in the US Congress is tenuous. Demagogues like Trump seldom leave events to chance. The Capitol Hill invasion in January 2021 was a clear indicator that, when push comes to shove, institutional guardrails are the first casualties.

If Trump could park the world into Mar-a-Lago, or cram the seas and oceans into Trump Tower, he would have them like sausages. He would rename the Earth “Trump Island” and crown himself His Imperial Majesty and the owner of Planet Earth.

His Footprint Speaks

Meanwhile, from Europe to the Middle East, and from Asia to Africa and North America, the world is reeling from the blows of the rash policies of this Nobel-Laureate-Wannabe, and paying the price in supply chain disruptions, rising inflation, geopolitical tensions, and worsening global misery.

It’s a joke that the current White House should think its president worthy of a peace prize, even a fake one. What does it take to call this insanity by its name?

Azu Ishiekwene is Editor-In-Chief of LEADERSHIP and author of the book,Writing for Media and Monetising It.

World.title: Anambra ‌‌demands more benefits from oil, gas sector
World.content:
Law Mefor, Anambra Commissioner for Information and value reformation, urged the federal government to ensure the state fully benefits from the nation’s oil and gas-related programmes and initiatives.

He said it was unfortunate that as an oil-producing state, Anambra was yet to be fully integrated into the nation’s oil and gas master plan.

The commissioner said this in Awka on Thursday while declaring open a one-day workshop on Nigerian Content capacity building for media stakeholders.

The event was organised by the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB).

Mr Mefor commended the organisers for bringing the workshop to Anambra.

He said Nigeria has the human capacity to manage its oil and gas resources effectively.

Speaking earlier, the Executive Secretary of NCDMB, Felix Ogbe, said the workshop was part of the federal government’s inclusivity drive for the industry.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Mr Ogbe, represented by Omomehin Ajimijaye, director of planning, research and statistics, urged the media to properly educate communities on the importance of participating in the board’s initiatives.

The General Manager, Corporate Communications, NCDMB, Obinna Ezeobi, urged the media to raise awareness about opportunities in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry.

He also urged them to hold industry operators accountable, particularly regarding compliance with local content requirements.

Mr Ezeobi advocated for better reporting on Nigerian content issues to enable more locals and businesses in Anambra to participate actively in the oil and gas value chain.

He said the media has a critical role in advancing the implementation of the Nigerian Oil and Gas Industry Content Development Act.

He said they can do this by informing the public about industry opportunities, explaining government interventions and monitoring compliance with relevant laws.

He urged journalists to use their positions as agenda-setters and gatekeepers to draw attention to issues affecting the industry and highlight opportunities for Nigerian businesses and professionals.

He further urged them to ensure that oil and gas operators met their local content obligations.

According to him, the workshop was designed to deepen journalists’ understanding of the Nigerian content framework.

He said it was also meant to improve the quality of their reportage and strengthen collaboration between the board and media organisations in Anambra.

He described Anambra as an important location for the engagement, noting that the state is recognised as an oil-producing state and ranks as the second-highest oil producer in the South-east.

(NAN)

World.title: Eno reveals lawmaker leaking Akwa Ibom Assembly’s secrets to him
World.content:
Akwa Ibom State Governor Umo Eno said the Leader of the State House of Assembly, Otobong Bob, has been leaking information to him whenever state lawmakers plot a “coup” against him.

Mr Eno disclosed this on Friday during a constituency briefing organised by Mr Bob, who represents Nsit Ubium State Constituency, the governor’s own local government area.

“Sometimes he’ll come to me in the night and whisper to me. Most times when they’re planning a coup. He’ll come to me and tell me we should dissolve this coup before it crystallises,” the governor said of the young lawmaker, whose father, Effiong Bob, a former senator, is a top politician in the state.

As Mr Eno spoke, Mr Bob, standing, gestured toward the deputy speaker, KufreAbasi Edidem, prompting both lawmakers to smile. The governor was also captured smiling as he made the remarks.

Mr Eno, however, did not explain the nature of the “coups” or identify the lawmakers involved.

The governor described Mr Bob, a lawyer, as his “son” and the “stabiliser of the assembly”, praising his role in managing internal political disagreements.

Mr Eno also described members of the current assembly as the most “enjoyed” since Akwa Ibom State was created, insisting that official records supported his claim.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Let me say without any contradiction that this House of Assembly, as far as I know, has enjoyed more than any assembly since the creation of this state. I stand to be challenged. The figures are clear; the documentation is clear. But they are very good people. All of them are my friends,” he said.

Bob pledges support for Eno’s re-election

In his remarks at the event, Mr Bob thanked Governor Eno for his support for the legislature and pledged the support of Nsit Ubium people for his re-election bid in 2027.

“This is an opportunity for me to tell the people of Nsit Ubium what I have been doing with the mandate they entrusted to me at the Akwa Ibom State House of Assembly. It is also an opportunity to demonstrate practical representation,” he said.

“I thank Your Excellency for the support you have shown to the Akwa Ibom State House of Assembly.

“I want to assure you of the support of the people of Nsit Ubium as you seek re-election in 2027. We will support all our candidates, from the Presidency to the House of Assembly, in the 2027 general elections.”

The lawmaker gifted several items, including cars, minibuses, generators, hair dryers, motorcycles, and sewing machines, to his constituents at the event.

Political background

Mr Bob, a lawyer serving his second term in the assembly, was elected on the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) platform for his first two terms before defecting to the All Progressives Congress (APC) alongside Mr Eno.

He has secured the APC ticket to contest for a third term in the 2027 elections.

His father, an ally of the governor, leads the Akwa Ibom North-East Senatorial District.

Mr Eno’s remarks highlight the close relationship between his administration and the assembly leader as political alignments take shape ahead of the 2027 elections.

Mr Bob did not respond to PREMIUM TIMES’ call and a text message seeking his response to the governor’s remarks at the time of filing this report.

World.title: 2027: Why I asked Atiku to step down for Peter Obi – Kwankwaso
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Vice-presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Rabiu Kwankwaso, has explained why he wants former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), to step down for NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi ahead of the 2027 general election, citing their longstanding political relationship and the need to make way for a new political arrangement.

Kwankwaso gave the explanation while speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Thursday, where he recounted decades of political dealings with Atiku, explained why he aligned with Obi and outlined the NDC’s position on fuel prices and subsidy.

Asked whether he was insisting that Atiku should abandon his presidential ambition this time, Kwankwaso answered in the affirmative. “Well, yes,” he said.

The former Kano State governor explained that he recently used a visit by a group of Fulani people from across the country as an opportunity to encourage them to speak with Atiku about stepping aside.

“I had some people, coincidentally, a group of Fulanis from across the country who came for a courtesy visit to my house. And I thought it was an opportunity for me, really, to talk to them and ask them that they should create time before they go back to their towns and villages to talk to him,” he said.

Kwankwaso stressed that his call was not motivated by hostility towards Atiku, whom he said he had known and worked with for many years.

“His Excellency Vice-President Atiku Abubakar is somebody that I know fairly well. And we have done so much together with him in the past. In fact, more than anybody who is around him today,” he said.

How Kwankwaso, Atiku worked together from 1993

To explain the depth of their political relationship, Kwankwaso traced their history to 1993, when both were involved in the political movement led by the late General Shehu Musa Yar’Adua.

“I remember in 1993, he was in our group under the leadership of General Shehu Musa Yar’adua and he was our choice for the presidential candidate of the SDP,” Kwankwaso said.

“We supported him. We did everything possible to make him our candidate of the SDP. And when it didn’t work out, of course, we tried also under General Shehu Musa Yar’adua to ensure that we got the ticket of the Vice-President.”

He recalled that the political effort did not succeed but said their relationship continued into the transition to civilian rule in 1999, when Olusegun Obasanjo emerged as the presidential candidate.

“It didn’t work. And we thank Almighty God we are still alive in 1999. I was Governor-Elect of Kano when we elected His Excellency Olusegun Obasanjo in Jos, the same Jos that we went in 1993,” he said.

Kwankwaso said he was close to Atiku during that period, when the latter served as Obasanjo’s running mate and subsequently became vice-president.

“And at the end of the day, of course, Obasanjo won. And I know he played some roles because I was very close to him, I was Governor-Elect at that time and he was Vice-president, and we were very happy,” he said.

He also recalled Atiku’s political role in 2003 and the support he received from Kano in the 2007 presidential election.

“And also, in 2003, he played a lot of roles. And I think that’s a very long story, maybe one of these days we will have an opportunity to discuss it. So also in 2007, almost 90% of our votes from Kano were given to Alhaji Atiku Abubakar,” Kwankwaso said.

He noted that they did not always belong to the same political party, pointing out that Atiku was in the Action Congress of Nigeria (ACN) in 2007, while he was not a member of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

“In 2007, I think he was in the ACN. Of course, I was not in the ACN,” he said.

Kwankwaso further recalled that they worked together in 2011 and were both presidential aspirants in the APC ahead of the 2015 general election, which former president Muhammadu Buhari won.

“And 2011, when we worked together. In 2015, I’m sure you know we were all aspirants in the APC. Buhari was number one, I was number two, he was number three. That’s 2015, so you can go on and on,” he said.

Summarising his position, Kwankwaso insisted that his appeal should not be interpreted as opposition to Atiku personally.

“What I’m trying to say is that we are not against him. The two sides, we’ve worked together with him so everything has time,” he said.

World.title: Beyond Limitations: How cerebral palsy survivor paints dreams with her feet
World.content:
Toma Umu

Refusing to be defined by her physical impairment, Toma Umu transforms lived experience into vibrant art while championing disability inclusion and self-acceptance. From learning to feed herself with her toes to studying Special Education, her journey reveals how community support and inner resolve uncover purpose in adversity.

By Ebunoluwa Sessou

Toma Umu, an artist and advocate for persons living with disabilities, stands tall against the stigma surrounding physical impairment. Despite being unable to use her hands due to cerebral palsy, Umu discovered she could use her legs to feed herself—and eventually, to create canvas art.

Her creative journey began out of necessity. “There was a time I wanted to eat and there was nobody to feed me,” she recalled. “I decided to try using my leg. It was not easy at first, but with practice, I became better.”

Seeing her independence, her late friend Adeyinka recognized potential beyond self-care. She asked Umu: “Since you can use your leg to feed yourself and you have control over it, why can’t you try painting?” That nudge altered her life path. “She introduced me to painting,” Umu shared. “She passed away in 2016, but her work can never die because of the impact she made in my life.”

Inspiring Through Nature and Color

Umu draws deep creative energy from the natural world, using bold palettes to convey hope and divine craftsmanship.

“I love nature and I love colors,” Umu explained. “I believe my painting comes from God and nature. God is the greatest artist… Even when you look at the sky, it is not just one shade of blue. There are different shades and colors. When I look at nature and what is happening around me, I draw inspiration from those things and bring them into my artwork.”

Her artistry extends beyond traditional mediums into textured materials like thread. One thread-based work was inspired by a discussion on whether people with disabilities experience love.

“The threads in the painting represent different kinds of lives and different ways of thinking,” she noted. “Everybody has their own journey. Some people find love in church, some on the streets, some at parties… The different threads represent those different paths.”

Redefining Ability and Identity

Through her public speaking—including a recent address at the anniversary of Place of Liberty—Umu continuously reframes narrative standards around disability, preferring to highlight varied human potential rather than limits.

“Look at me. I cannot make use of my hands, and some people may look at that and think everything is over for me. But God has given me the grace to use my legs. That is an ability,” she declared. “It is about not giving up on yourself. Don’t focus only on the condition you are in. Identify the good things you can do and try to make an impact.”

This philosophy drives her opposition to restrictive labels like “disabled.”

“I believe we are all wonderfully and fearfully made,” Umu said. “I believe God is a God of variety. He created people in different forms, shapes, sizes, and abilities. We are all different, and those differences can be a way for God’s creativity and purpose to be revealed.”

Navigating Education and Overcoming Skepticism

Umu’s academic record stands as proof of her determination. Despite critics who asserted her physical condition would prevent her from writing or learning, supportive networks enabled her to push forward.

“Throughout my life, there were people who told me that because of my impairment, I could not write or that I was not capable of achieving certain things,” she said. “But I had people around me who believed in me.”

She went on to earn an NCE in Special and Adult Education from the College of Education, Oyo, and later completed a degree in Early Childhood Education at the National Open University of Nigeria.

A Call for Support and Self-Love

For Umu, personal realization is only half the journey; the surrounding community plays a crucial role in bringing out individual talent. She urges parents, caregivers, and society to look past physical limitations.

“Sometimes, all a person needs is somebody who will look beyond the condition and see the ability within them,” she said. “We cannot always discover everything by ourselves. Sometimes God uses people around us to help us discover what we can do.”

Her primary message to anyone struggling with self-worth or discouragement remains grounded in self-acceptance and perseverance.

“For me, you have to love yourself first,” Umu emphasized. “When you love and accept yourself, it becomes difficult for what people say to shake you… Disability is not inability. Tell yourself that you can make it. Don’t allow your condition to define the limits of your life.”

Vanguard News

World.title: Broken System, Stolen Innocence: The silent agony of Nigeria’s rape survivors
World.content:
•How systemic flaws, delayed justice, and social stigma force victims into hiding while perpetrators walk free; A 16-year-old survivor’s tragic ordeal exposes the deep fractures in the nation’s criminal justice system

By Ebunoluwa Sessou

Rape has plagued Nigerian society for generations, but social media has amplified survivors’ voices and exposed hidden stories. Despite numerous reports of sexual assault against adults and children, few perpetrators ever see the inside of a jail cell. Flaws in the justice system, weak prosecution, and societal stigma continue to fuel the scourge rather than prevent it.

The World Health Organization reports that one in three women worldwide has faced physical or sexual violence. About 8 percent of women aged 15 and above—roughly 263 million—have experienced sexual violence by a non-partner at least once since age 15.

A Holiday That Became a Nightmare

Sixteen-year-old Goodness from Benin Republic travelled to Lagos to spend the holiday with her uncle, Mr. Tunde, a 38-year-old carpenter who lives in the Isheri-Olofin area of Alimosho with his wife and four children.

For Goodness, staying with her mother’s brother was meant to be a fresh start—a chance to go to school and learn hairdressing. Instead, her dreams were shattered within two months.

Vanguard discovered Goodness while researching teenage pregnancy in her neighbourhood. Her sister, Mercy—herself a teenage pregnancy survivor—sat silently throughout the interview before revealing, “My sister was raped.”

Getting Goodness to speak was difficult. She wailed, hissed, and sobbed as if the world was crumbling around her. Finally, she found words.

“I was going to fetch water in the afternoon, around 3pm. Our area is quiet. Nobody was around,” she said. “I noticed movement but didn’t take it seriously. Before I knew what happened, I had passed out.

“I saw three young men behind me. They covered my nose with a handkerchief and dragged me into a building. One told me to keep quiet, but I kept screaming because I was afraid. Nobody came. They brought out a knife and threatened to stab me if I screamed again. I was terrified. I knew I couldn’t fight them. They raped me, took turns on me, and left me there.”

Goodness woke up in a neighbourhood clinic hours later. A friend had found her lying almost lifeless and called for help.

Three Weeks of Silence

When she regained consciousness, Goodness went home and told no one. Fear of her uncle’s reaction—and of her attackers—kept her silent for three weeks.

“I was moody. I didn’t talk to anyone,” she recalled. “My uncle noticed something was wrong and kept asking questions until I finally told him I was raped by three men. My body was completely broken. I couldn’t even stand on my own.”

Her health deteriorated severely. She became extremely anemic, suffered breathing difficulties, and couldn’t sleep. People tried home remedies to build her blood—mixing milk with tomato paste or soda—but nothing could heal the deeper wounds.

Her older uncle and friends were angry, insisting those responsible should face justice. Yet her alleged attackers remain free while she battles physical and emotional torment.

Today, Goodness has been relocated back to Benin Republic by her uncle. She could not withstand the shame while her perpetrators walk the streets freely.

Beyond Goodness: A National Crisis

Goodness’s story is far from isolated. In 2021, Nollywood actor Olanrewaju James, known as Baba Ijesha, was convicted of six counts involving sexual assault and indecent treatment of a child.

The National Human Rights Commission recorded 6,943 rape cases and 45,986 sexual-violence cases in 2024. Between January and March 2025, another 409 rape cases and 2,711 sexual-violence cases were documented.

The National Bureau of Statistics estimates 1.4 million Nigerians experienced sexual offences between May 2023 and April 2024—yet only 22.7 percent were reported to police.

The Justice Gap

Mr. Raphael Odoh, National Coordinator of the UCcareforall Initiative, lamented that Nigeria lacks a unified national database tracking rape and sexual assault cases.

“Only a small fraction of reported rape cases result in arrest, prosecution, and conviction,” he said. “About 15 to 25 percent of reported cases lead to arrest. Only 1 to 15 percent make it to formal prosecution. When calculated from initial police reports, only about 0.5 to 6.5 percent result in conviction and incarceration.”

Odoh blamed poor enforcement, poverty, corruption, lack of rehabilitation for offenders, and inefficient judicial processes.

Lagos State’s Response

Mrs. Titilola Vivour-Adeniyi, Executive Secretary of the Lagos State Domestic and Sexual Violence Agency (DSVA), said the state is responding on three fronts: prevention, protection, and accountability.

“Between September 2021 and July 2026, DSVA recorded 1,171 defilement cases, 420 rape cases, 428 sexual harassment cases, and 100 cases of sexual assault by penetration,” she said. “Between January and July 2026, about 385 sexual violence cases were charged to court, and the state has secured over 160 convictions in the past year.”

Vivour-Adeniyi acknowledged that justice is a chain where one weak link can undermine an otherwise strong case.

“The major challenge is often not the absence of laws, but what happens between reporting and the courtroom,” she said. “Delayed reporting may mean critical forensic evidence is lost. Inadequate investigation can weaken a strong case. Survivors sometimes withdraw because of family pressure, stigma, or the emotional burden of a prolonged trial.”

She emphasised that Section 30 of the Lagos State Domestic and Sexual Violence Agency Law, 2021, provides three years imprisonment for anyone who knowingly conceals a sexual offence.

The Church’s Role

Rev. Israel Kristilere, Senior Pastor of Shepherdhill Baptist Church, said religious institutions have a significant role to play.

“Religious leaders must teach respect, dignity, consent, and bodily integrity through sermons, Bible studies, counselling, and youth programs,” he said. “They can establish policies that make members know there are boundaries, and when complaints arise, how to deal with them. Religious institutions should model accountability and compassion.

For survivors like Goodness, justice remains elusive. Their voices echo in courtrooms and communities, but too often, the system fails them. Until investigation, prosecution, and survivor support work as one chain, pain and shame will continue to be their only companions—while perpetrators walk free.

Vanguard News

World.title: Atiku, Obi to Tinubu: ‘You can’t campaign through surrogates’
World.content:
Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar

By Henry Umoru and Luminous Jannamike

ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to defend his record before Nigerians rather than hide behind governors, ministers and defectors campaigning for his re-election, saying political surrogates cannot shield him from public anger over economic hardship.

Read Also: 2027: Atiku, Obi, Duke, Makinde no match for Tinubu, APC declares

This came as the Media Office of the Presidential candidate of Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi ahead of 2027 general election, has taken a swipe at President Tinubu for saying he would not accompany the All Progressives Congress Presidential Campaign Council, APC-PCC, to every campaign event, citing the need to prioritise governance, economic obligations and efforts to attract investors.

Atiku said Tinubu must answer for the hardship Nigerians have endured over the past three and a half years before seeking another four-year mandate, insisting that voters would judge him by their lived experiences, not the promises of his political allies.

In a statement, yesterday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku said: “Tinubu says he may miss campaign rallies because Nigeria needs his attention. Where was that urgency when Nigerians pleaded for relief?

“He has had three and a half years to govern. In that time, families have been forced to cut meals, postpone medical care and watch their earnings lose value before they get home.

“Let him look a mother in the eye and explain what his government has done to make food affordable. Let him tell pensioners why they cannot afford their medicines. Let him explain to young Nigerians why years of study and hard work have still not brought them decent jobs,” he said.

“Tinubu says American creditors cannot wait. Nigerians cannot wait either. They have bills to pay, children to feed and lives to rebuild. They deserve a President who treats their suffering with the same urgency he gives creditors and investors.

“He can fill every campaign stage in Nigeria. He cannot fill an empty pot with surrogates. He cannot send a politician into a market to persuade prices to fall.

“The people on his campaign council did not receive the mandate in 2023. Tinubu did. He made the promises. He took the decisions. He must face the questions.

“Nigerians will hear whatever his surrogates have to say. But when they vote, they will remember what they have lived through. No crowd of politicians can stand between Tinubu and his record,” Atiku said.

You can’t campaign through surrogates, Peter Obi Media Office to Tinubu

On its part, the Peter Obi Media Office, POMR, in a statement by its Spokesman, Idris Zekeri, yesterday, said: “President Tinubu reportedly said the demands of governance may keep him away from the campaign trail. Nigerians deserve to ask: If he cannot make time to face the electorate, why should surrogates be sent to ask for their votes?

“The President cannot delegate accountability. He cannot outsource the defence of his record to political allies, party chieftains, and praise singers while millions of Nigerians struggle with the consequences of his government’s policies.

“Surrogates can speak for the President, but they cannot answer for his failures. They can repeat his promises, but they cannot make those promises a reality. They can campaign in his name, but they cannot carry his responsibility.

“If the administration has delivered on its promises, why should the President be reluctant to defend that record before Nigerians himself? If the economy is improving, let him explain how that improvement is reflected in the cost of food, transportation, electricity, housing, and necessities. If his policies are working, let him face the citizens who want to know when the hardship will end.

“Mr President, governance is not an excuse to avoid accountability. In a democracy, governance is the very record a candidate must defend before asking for another mandate.

“Nigerians are not being asked to elect your surrogates. They are being asked to assess you, your policies, your promises, and your performance. No surrogate can stand in your place when it is time to answer for the state of the nation.

“You cannot send surrogates to collect the votes while keeping the President away from the questions. You cannot delegate the campaign and expect Nigerians to forget who must answer for the record.

“The Nigerian people deserve a direct conversation with their President, not a relay of rehearsed talking points from political messengers.

“If there is a record to defend, let the President defend it. If there are promises yet to be fulfilled, let him explain them. And if Nigerians are being asked to renew his mandate, let him have the courage to face their questions.

“A President who seeks the people’s mandate must be prepared to face the people. Surrogates may carry the message, but they cannot carry the burden of accountability.”

World.title: 2027: Atiku, Obi, Duke, Makinde no match for Tinubu, APC declares
World.content:
*Says OBJ/Atiku spent N300b on non-existent roads *’Ex-VP wants to scrap NELFUND while charging millions in own varsity’

By Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA

The ruling All Progressives Congress, APC, has declared that Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, Mr. Peter Obi, Mr. Donald Duke and Engr Seyi Makinde are no match for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 election.

The quartet are the presidential candidates of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, People’s Redemption Party, PRP, and the Allied People’s Movement, APM.

National Chairman of the party, Professor Nentawe Yilwatda, made the declaration, yesterday, while receiving the Forum of APC House of Representatives Aspirants, led by Danjuma Mohammed, at the party’s national secretariat in Abuja.

“No political party, as it stands today, has a more credible candidate than President Bola Tinubu. We have facts, we have records that if we put them vis-à-vis any other candidate that is on this ballot, none matches our own candidate. None. I mean, none,” he declared.

He said the opposition could not stand a side-by-side comparison of records. “Show the scorecard of other presidents, of other candidates, and then we now put them side by side Mr President; none of them comes close to matching Mr President, even in terms of building institutions.”

Obasanjo/Atiku

On roads, Yilwatda said Nigerians could not point to anything built under the N300 billion road budget released when Chief Olusegun Obasanjo was president and Atiku was in his government.

“We were here live. When the president gave road projects of over N300 billion, when another person was the Minister of Works, we couldn’t find even the road that was patched with that budget. We are struggling to find the roads.

“Show me one road, a span of 500 kilometres, that was constructed with that money, just one. You can’t find it, but I can pinpoint many roads across the country that were constructed just in three years”, he stated.

Yilwatda then listed what he said the Tinubu administration had completed or has under construction. “From Abuja to Kaduna is over 441 kilometres. From Abuja to Kaduna to Kano, it is under construction. We are almost near completion.”

Of the Trans-Sahara Superhighway, he said: “We’ve done almost 30, 40 per cent of that one. Tell me which president has done that much? And that span alone is over 1,400 kilometres of roads. Just that span alone, before you take the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway.”

He also pointed to the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) gas pipeline project. “That same gas will be used for fertiliser. That same gas will be used for CNG. It will take gas to homes, fire turbines for electricity to power homes, power industries, and you tell me that Mr President has not done well?”

The APC chairman also criticised Atiku’s position on the student loan scheme, which he said he would scrap, if elected.

“I just listened to one of the spokespersons of the ADC, your former party, who was saying, how can President Tinubu be giving N20,000 to students?”

He said such critics were out of touch with ordinary Nigerians. “They don’t know the value of N20,000 to an ordinary man on the streets.”

Yilwatda, a former university lecturer, said he knows the cost of school fees first-hand. “I know how many students dropped out of school because they could not afford school fees. I taught them.”

He told the story of a student who saved part of the N20,000 monthly upkeep, bought a second-hand refrigerator and began selling iced fish to schoolmates. “That’s how that N20,000 is building homes, and somebody is saying that when he comes, the first thing he would do is scrap it.”

Then he turned on the critics’ own institutions.

“But they all have their universities. They charge, you know, in millions of naira, but they come back and say that the money we are giving the students is too small.

“Meanwhile, even students in those institutions have access to student loans. So, we are supporting their own universities too.”

Earlier, Mohammed told the APC leadership that the forum was formed in 2022 under the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP “with the primary objective of uniting aspirants who participated in the party’s primary election but did not emerge as candidates.”

He said its mission then was to mobilise support for Atiku and his running mate, Senator Ifeanyi Okowa. “Following subsequent political developments, many members of our forum have joined the APC.”

Mohammed said members were “united by our resolve to support the direction of President Bola Tinubu, and his Vice President, Kashim Shettima, for a second term.”

The forum, he said, draws members “from across the 360 federal constituencies in Nigeria.”

He added: “We are not seeking to establish a parallel structure or undermine existing party organs.”

He asked the party to approve and support “the production and nationwide distribution of these important campaign materials in major local languages across multiple media formats”, and proposed a political conference in each of the six geopolitical zones to disseminate them.

“We finally believe that united aspirants constitute a formidable political force,” Mohammed said.

Yilwatda assured the group of a place in the party’s machinery. “We have a directorate that works with you already, and I will link you up with the directorate so that the work will start.”

He also drew on his own electoral setbacks to urge the aspirants not to lose heart. “I contested for governorship election on the Plateau. I lost. I went to the Supreme Court. I lost at the Supreme Court. When I returned back to serve the party, I never grumbled.”

On the party’s strength, he said: “Our party has over 261,000 Exco. Just executive members of the party, not to talk of members. We want to convert those numbers to victory, and we need to form that partnership. Partner with us, work with us, and victory is sure for all of us.”

World.title: Dangote IPO: Firm reaffirms commitment to regulation compliance
World.content:
Dangote Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) trucks loading Premium Motor Spirit (PMS) at the Dangote Petroleum Refinery gantry, during a press conference to mark the first anniversary of petrol rollout and the official presentation of CNG-powered trucks for fuel distribution at the Dangote Petroleum Refinery, Lekki, Lagos, on Monday, 15 September 2025.

By Lawani Mikairu

Following the Security and Exchange Commission, SEC, notice that the general public should beware of buying Dangote Refinery’s Initial Public Offering, IPO, through WayvePay digital banking platform, the bank, yesterday, clarified its involvement with the IPO sales.

A statement by Kingsley Ezenwa, Head of Corporate Communications and Marketing, WayvePay, said the bank was currently engaging with SEC after explaining its involvement with the IPO sales with the regulatory authority.

The statement said: “Wayve Microfinance Bank Limited, operator of the WayvePay digital banking platform, acknowledges the recent communication by SEC, concerning the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals IPO.

“The bank takes the SEC’s communication and the concerns raised seriously and remains committed to engaging constructively with the commission and other relevant regulatory authorities to address the issues and clarify the circumstances surrounding the matter.

“Wayve Microfinance Bank Limited is a financial institution licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, with eligible deposits insured by the Nigeria Deposit Insurance Corporation, NDIC, subject to applicable coverage limits and terms. The Bank considers it important to clarify its regulatory status and distinguish its licensed banking operations from the specific matters raised in connection with the IPO.

“Regarding the IPO-related arrangement, the bank wishes to clarify that its involvement was undertaken in partnership with Coronation Secuities under a duly executed agreement between the parties. Under this arrangement, the WayvePay digital banking platform was linked to Coronation Securities to facilitate the relevant IPO-related activities, with subscription funds directed to Coronation Securities rather than directly to Wayve Microfinance Bank Limited.

“Following the SEC’s communication, the bank has withdrawn the relevant promotional materials and removed the associated link from its mobile application. Since the publication of the promotional materials, no investors has subscribed for shares in the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals IPO through the WayvePay platform.

“Wayve Microfinance Bank Limited is engaging with the appropriate regulatory authorities, providing relevant documentation and clarifying the circumstances surrounding the arrangement. The Bank will continue to cooperate with the SEC and respond to the issues raised through the established regulatory processes.

The Bank recognises the SEC’s important mandate to protect investors and promote confidence in Nigeria’s capital market. It remains committed to transparency, responsible business practices and compliance with the regulatory requirements applicable to its operations. The Bank will continue to address the matter constructively and take appropriate steps in response to regulatory guidance,” the statement added.

World.title: Sanwo-Olu orders immediate repairs of Lagos roads
World.content:
Gov Sanwo-Olu

By Olasunkanmi Akoni

Lagos State Governor, Babajide Sanwo-Olu, has directed the State Public Works Corporation (LSPWC) to commence immediate road reconstruction and rehabilitation across the state, taking advantage of the dry season to address deteriorating infrastructure.

The General Manager of LSPWC, Engr. Tokunbo Ajanaku, disclosed this on Thursday during an inspection tour of ongoing projects, assuring residents of improved road networks as weather conditions become more favourable for construction work.

Ajanaku said Oshodi-Isolo Local Government Area was a major focus of the exercise, with reconstruction underway on Godwin Omonuwa Road, Taiwo Street, Salamotu Street, Peter Agah Street and Ibeh Street.

He said the projects were undertaken at the governor’s direction to address infrastructure deficits and improve connectivity within communities.

“These roads are important links within the Oshodi-Isolo axis, serving residents, traders, business owners and other road users daily.

“Their reconstruction will not only improve mobility but also reduce transportation costs, enhance road safety, boost commercial activities and create a more conducive environment for businesses and residents,” Ajanaku said.

He added that the inspection covered other ongoing rehabilitation projects across the state, including Ogunnusi Road in Ojodu Local Council Development Area (LCDA), Awolowo Way in Ikeja Local Government Area, Lanre Awolokun Road and Idowu Olaitan Street in Shomolu, as well as Idimu-Ikotun Road in Alimosho.

According to him, heavy rainfall often limits asphalt laying, but the corporation maintained emergency palliative interventions during the rainy season to keep critical roads motorable.

He said the agency was now shifting towards more comprehensive and durable repairs with the return of dry weather.

Ajanaku added that much of the maintenance and asphalt-laying work was being carried out at night, under appropriate safety measures, to minimise traffic congestion across the metropolis.

He appealed to residents to be patient, explaining that road repairs were prioritised based on road conditions, traffic volume and the urgency of intervention.

The general manager said the corporation would progressively extend its operations to other parts of the state.

He also urged residents to protect public infrastructure by avoiding practices that contribute to road deterioration, including dumping refuse in drainage channels, spilling petroleum products and discharging wastewater onto roads.

“Our roads are our collective heritage. Government has the responsibility to provide and maintain them, but citizens also have a duty to protect them. Road preservation must therefore be a shared responsibility,” Ajanaku said.

World.title: APC group rallies Southeast support for Tinubu
World.content:
By Vincent Ujumadu

The Tinubu Support Group (TSG) in the Southeast, led by former All Progressives Congress (APC) National Auditor, Sir Paul Chukwuma, on Thursday held a rally in Awka, Anambra State, to mobilise support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027.

At the rally, the Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Benjamin Kalu, urged voters in the zone to support APC candidates across all levels in the 2027 general elections.

Chukwuma, a former governorship candidate in Anambra State, and the APC senatorial candidate for Anambra Central, Uche Ekwunife, also urged voters to support Tinubu and other candidates of the party.

They expressed confidence that the APC would secure substantial votes across the five Southeast states, arguing that Tinubu’s actions and policies had earned him support in the region.

However, some APC leaders in Anambra State reportedly expressed dissatisfaction with what they described as the party’s national leadership relying on the strength of the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA) to secure votes for Tinubu in the state.

The APC state secretary, Sir Obiora Okpala, said the party should be adequately recognised in political arrangements in Anambra, given its status as the ruling party at the national level and a major political stakeholder in the state.

He argued that the APC should be carried along in the process, rather than APGA being given what he described as undue advantage over the party in Anambra.

World.title: Tinubu Meets CDS, Service Chiefs, Musa, NSA, IG, Gaidam over 2027 Polls Security
World.content:
• Matawalle, Famadewa, other heads of agencies in attendance

• Tells military he wants free, fair, credible polls next year

• Gives marching order for rescue of those kidnapped, abducted nationwide

•Musa: we’ll secure nation for all eligible voters to exercise their franchise without fear

• Pledges military’s neutrality during elections

•Says president will soon launch 10 aircraft and helicopters to boost nation’s aerial surveillance

Deji Elumoye in Abuja





President Bola Tinubu, yesterday, presided over the National Security Council (NSC) meeting at State House, Abuja, essentially to discuss the security of the 2027 general election.

The meeting, which lasted for about five hours at the first floor office of the president, was attended by National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu; Minister of Defence, General Christopher Musa; and Minister of Police Affairs, Senator Ibrahim Gaidam.

Present, also, were Minister of State for Defence, Bello Matawalle, and Special Adviser to the President on Homeland Security, Major-General Adeyinka Famadewa (rtd).

Others included Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Olufemi Oluyede and the three service chiefs – Chief of Army Staff, Lieutenant General Waidi Shaibu; Chief of Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Idi Abbas; Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Sunday Aneke – and Chief of Defence Intelligence, Lieutenant-General Emmanuel Undiandeye.

In attendance, too, were Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu; Director-General of National Intelligence Agency (NIA), Ambassador Mohammed Mohammed; and Director-General of Department of State Services (DSS), Adeola Oluwatosin Ajayi.

Addressing newsmen after the meeting, Musa said the essence of the meeting was to brief the president on the security situation in the country ahead of the January 2027 polls.

He disclosed that they had an intensive deliberation with the president, who told the security chiefs that he was desirous of a free, fair, and credible poll next year.

Musa assured all stakeholders, including the political parties, that the military would be neutral during the elections.

He stated, “Today’s meeting was to brief Mr. President on the security situation within the country. You know, the elections are coming in January, and it’s important that we keep him abreast on what is ongoing. You can see all heads of security agencies are here.

“We had an intensive discussion, and Mr. President made it very clear he wants a free, fair, and credible election. We must do everything possible to ensure that the country is safe and secure for the citizens to go out and vote.

“And so, we want to assure Nigerians that we are committed. We are determined to ensure that we provide safety and security for all Nigerians. Everyone should come out and vote. Vote for whoever they want.”

Musa added, “The president wants the atmosphere to be free, and it’s important for all other political parties to understand that the security forces are going to be neutral.

“We are going to ensure that we give everybody opportunity to go and serve, so they have nothing to worry about, nothing to be afraid of, and that nobody is going to intimidate them for whatever reasons.”

The defence minister also defended the military institution against allegations of recruitment of underage soldiers, saying such act might have been carried out by terrorist groups but not Nigerian military.

According to him, “We are all professionals. We are fully committed, and it’s also important for us to mention the issue of recent (alleged recruitment of underage soldiers). We have seen some people trying to make a case as if the emphasis is using underage children in our operations.

“There is nobody that is underage that is being brought here. I think the discussion that was made was that the accusation was on the terrorists using the underage.

“Well, we know that we don’t have control over what they do, and that’s why it’s important for us to understand that we must not allow them remain wherever they are.”

Musa further stated that the president gave the military a marching order to ensure the rescue of all those kidnapped and abducted in different parts of the country.

He stated, “The directive from the president is: all of us must go all out to fish out and rescue all those that have been abducted, kidnapped wherever they are. There shouldn’t be any camp of any tourists or bandits anywhere in Nigeria.

“As we go forward, we are showing Nigerians that we’re fully committed, and that is what we’re going to work towards. So, we thank Mr. President for his support and to assure Nigeria that we’re all working as a team, as Nigerians for Nigeria. We assure you that.”

Musa revealed that the president would soon inaugurate 10 additional aircraft and helicopters to boost the country’s aerial security surveillance.

He also disclosed that the president planned to extend the new salary structure to police and other paramilitary personnel and pensioners.

Musa stated, “I want to assure you, very soon Mr. President is coming to commission a set of new aircraft and helicopters that have been bought. I think about 10 of them, and to show Nigerians that despite the economic issue, the issue of security is in the front burner of Mr President’s view.
