World.title: Rwanda: Kagame Calls for African Collaboration On F1 Grand Prix
World.content:
President Paul Kagame has called for African countries to work together to make Formula 1 African Grand Prix in Rwanda a success for the continent, following messages of support from South African President Cyril Ramaphosa and Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema.

Responding to Ramaphosa's congratulations and offer of support on X, Kagame said Rwanda looked forward to working with other countries to make the event a continental achievement.

ALSO READ: African drivers welcome historic Rwanda-F1 Grand Prix deal

"We look forward to working with you and all who share this vision as we make this a truly African Grand Prix in every way possible, and take motorsport to new heights on our continent," Kagame said in the post.



Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema also congratulated Kagame and the people of Rwanda on securing hosting rights of the African Grand Prix, describing the Rwanda-Formula 1 agreement announced on Tuesday in Kigali as a historic achievement reflecting resilience, vision and hard work.

ALSO READ: Ramaphosa congratulates Rwanda on 10-year Formula 1 deal

"Zambia shares your pride in this milestone for Rwanda and Africa," Hichilema said.

In response, Kagame described the agreement as a milestone for both Rwanda and Africa, expressing his readiness to work with Hichilema and other African leaders to make the event a success for the entire continent.

"This is a milestone for Rwanda and for Africa, and we look forward to working with you and our African brothers and sisters to make the African Grand Prix a success for the entire continent," Kagame said.

The 10-year agreement will see Rwanda host a Formula 1 Grand Prix in the early 2030s on a circuit planned for construction in Bugesera. It will be the first to be hosted on the African continent since the 1993 South African Grand Prix.

World.title: Zimbabwe: Mnangagwa Promotes Tagwirei, Demotes Obert Mpofu in Zanu-PF Shake-Up
World.content:
President Emmerson Mnangagwa has promoted close ally Kudakwashe Tagwirei into Zanu-PF's powerful Politburo.

Tagwirei, who was appointed Minister of Economic Development in Mnangagwa's Cabinet a week ago, is being tipped to take over from him.

He was appointed a Senator soon after the passing of the controversial Constitutional Amendment Act 3, which extended Mnangagwa's stay in power beyond 2028 to 2030.



A statement, signed by party spokesperson Christopher Mutsvangwa, confirmed his appointment and the relegation of once powerful general secretary Obert Mpofu, who has now been demoted to Zanu PF's Council of Elders.

"Comrade Emmerson Dambudzo Mnangagwa, through the Secretary General, Cde Jacob Mudenda and in accordance with the Constitution of the Party, specifically Article 7, on the appointment of Central Committee members, Article 8, regarding appointments to the Council of Elders and Article 9, regarding the appointment of Politburo members, has made the following appointments and redeployments.

"Cde Mayor Wadyajena has been appointed a Central Committee member, Cde. Obert Moses Mpofu, formerly the Secretary for Science and Technology has been appointed to the Council of Elders.

"Senator Kudakwashe Tagwirei has been appointed to the new re-designated position of Secretary for Economic Affairs and Investment Promotion," reads the statement.

Tagwirei's rise, from an appointment into the Central Committee, Senate, and now Politburo, is a direct slap to Vice President Constantino Chiwenga, who is also eyeing the presidency after Mnangagwa.

World.title: Africa: Chinese President XI Outlines Four Principles for Resolving African Conflicts
World.content:
Nairobi — Chinese President Xi Jinping has outlined four principles for resolving conflicts in Africa, calling for African-led solutions, respect for national sovereignty, an end to hostilities, and efforts to address the root causes of insecurity.

Xi presented the principles during a meeting with Togo's President of the Council of Ministers, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, who was on an official visit to China on October 13, according to China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The remarks come as several African regions continue to face conflict and security challenges, including Sudan, the Great Lakes region and the Horn of Africa, where regional and international efforts have sought to advance ceasefires, dialogue and lasting political settlements.

Xi said African people should remain central to decisions affecting the continent, insisting that outside parties involved in resolving conflicts should respect Africa's leadership in regional affairs.



"African people are the true masters of the continent and should therefore play a central role in regional affairs," Xi said, according to the Chinese Foreign Ministry.

His first principle emphasised African leadership, positioning the continent's people and regional actors at the centre of efforts to resolve conflicts.

The second principle called for fairness and justice, with Xi urging parties involved in conflict resolution to adhere to the United Nations Charter and respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the countries concerned.

He also called for an end to hostilities, arguing that war and unilateral sanctions cannot fundamentally resolve disputes between countries.

Xi urged parties to pursue mutual respect, extensive consultations and compromise, including seeking common ground despite differences.

His fourth principle called for addressing both the immediate security threats and the underlying causes of conflict, saying efforts to restore security should be accompanied by long-term development planning.

"Addressing immediate security concerns should go hand in hand with long-term development planning," China's MFA said.

The principles place emphasis on political dialogue and African ownership of peace processes, alongside measures to address the conditions that can sustain instability.

China-Togo bilateral ties

Xi's remarks came as China and Togo announced plans to elevate their bilateral relations to a China-Togo community with a shared future in the new era.

Close 

During the meeting, Xi said the two countries should strengthen political exchanges, deepen cooperation and support each other on issues concerning their respective core interests.

He also encouraged Togo to take advantage of China's zero-tariff arrangements for African products and measures to facilitate exports to the Chinese market.

China further expressed readiness to expand cooperation with Togo in renewable energy, digital technology and intelligent industries to support the West African country's industrialisation.

Gnassingbé welcomed China's development experience and called for stronger cooperation in trade, infrastructure, science and technology.

He also endorsed Xi's four principles for addressing African conflicts and said Togo was ready to strengthen multilateral cooperation with China in defence of multilateralism and the interests of developing countries.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi attended the meeting.

African-led peace

Xi's principles echo a central theme in African and international peace efforts: the need for political solutions led by African actors, supported by international cooperation and respect for national sovereignty.

The African Union and the United Nations have also emphasised African-led mediation in conflicts, including in Sudan and the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, as well as coordinated action to address tensions in the Horn of Africa.

World.title: Kenya: WHO Urges Vigilance After Kenya Confirms Second Ebola Case
World.content:
The World Health Organization (WHO) continues to support Kenya's efforts to contain Ebola after a second person tested positive for the Bundibugyo virus, the UN agency's representative in the country said on Thursday.

The patient, a 39-year-old man, is a relative of Kenya's first case - related to the ongoing deadly outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) - who died in hospital on 5 October.

He was among contacts who were placed in quarantine and developed symptoms on 13 October.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

'We all have a role to play'

"I congratulate the Government for taking this important step to ensure that contacts are listed and quarantined," WHO Representative Dr. Neema Rusibamayila Kimambo told UN News in Nairobi, a day after the Ministry of Health confirmed the new case.

"But to defeat this disease, it's not about the Government, it is not about partners It is about everybody," she insisted. "We all have a role to play and if each one of us plays our part, then we should be able to contain the disease and stop community spread."

Casting a wide net

Kenya's first Ebola patient and fatality was a local man who had been living in the DRC, where the record outbreak continues to spread in the east.

He arrived in Nairobi via Uganda on 3 October and died in hospital two days later.

Dr. Kimambo commended health authorities who "cast the net very wide" to identify people who had come into contact with him - whether in the air or on the ground.

The more than 40 people included airline passengers and crew, airplane cleaners, airport workers, baggage handlers and immigration officials, as well as health personnel and family members.

Most are in quarantine, while a few low-risk contacts have self-quarantined and are being monitored. Meanwhile, every effort is being made to reach six passengers who have been difficult to locate because they have foreign phone numbers.

Stepping up preparedness

Even before the first case , WHO and the Kenyan Government were stepping up Ebola preparedness after the outbreak was declared in the DRC in May. Neighbouring Uganda also confronted the disease, with any outbreak officially ruled out in late August.

Teams are working across all areas, including surveillance and contact tracing. WHO has also brought in a senior incident manager who participated in the Ebola response in Uganda, as well as other experts.

Close 

"We are building on the work that we started during the preparedness phase, so case management and IPC (infection prevention and control) are critical at this time in the quarantine centres," Dr. Kimambo said.

WHO also continues to provide assistance to Kenya in various other ways. The UN agency has donated some $70,000 worth of supplies, including IPC and laboratory items, since the first Ebola case was identified.

Additionally, more than 4,000 health workers have been trained, including for screenings at ports of entry.

Keep borders open

While Dr. Kimambo said there still is no need to impose travel restrictions or close national borders, she underlined the importance of appropriate screening to identify travellers who may pose a health risk.

Preventing Ebola begins with understanding how the disease is transmitted, she said, which is through contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person.

She reiterated the advice to practice regular handwashing, use hand sanitizer and avoid shaking hands.

As Ebola symptoms include fever, vomiting and diarrhoea - which mimic symptoms of malaria and other diseases - she stressed the need to seek medical care quickly. In the interim, Kenyans are urged to keep calm and stay safe.

"I think one is not to over panic and be very fearful because we do not have community spread," she said. "But two, let us be responsible. Whoever is sick, let's make sure we go to a health facility and get care. And also, let us ensure that we take IPC measures."

World.title: Jerry Seinfeld turns tables on radical anti-Israel agitators after chaotic Chicago stunt backfires
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Comedian Jerry Seinfeld turned the tables on anti-Israel hecklers who attempted to derail his Chicago performance last Friday, mocking the protesters as security removed them from the venue.

Viral video from the confrontation shows activists shouting at Seinfeld at the Chicago Theatre, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" in Gaza and alleging that American taxpayer dollars are funding the deaths of thousands of civilians.

"Twenty-two thousand Palestinians who are children now are killed with our taxpayer money, and you’re making jokes!" a woman shouted in clips posted online.

JERRY SEINFELD GIVES BLUNT THREE-WORD RESPONSE TO INFLUENCER ASKING FOR A 'FREE PALESTINE'

Seinfeld then dances on stage and mocks the protesters with sarcastic remarks, calling himself "racist" and saying, "It’s a genocide. I’m into it." He also joked that he would find out how much the protesters paid for their tickets and send the money directly to Israel.

As security personnel escorted the demonstrators out of the auditorium, one audience member shouted, "Rough her up!"

The Anti-War Committee Chicago and the Chicago branch of the US Palestinian Community Network have taken credit for organizing the disruption, writing on Instagram, "Friday’s disruption sent a clear message: Those who defend Israel’s genocide and ethnic cleansing of Palestinians in Gaza and throughout Palestine will be met with protest and are not welcome on Chicago’s stages without opposition."

COMEDIAN DECLARES JERRY SEINFELD 'UNCANCELLABLE' DESPITE 'WOKE' ANTI-ISRAEL FESTIVAL BOYCOTT

Fox News Digital reached out to Seinfeld’s team for comment but did not hear back.

The altercation is the latest in a string of protests targeting the 72-year-old Jewish comedian over his staunch defense of Israel.

ANTI-ISRAEL PROTESTERS LABEL MAMDANI A 'TRAITOR,' ACCUSE HIM OF 'GENOCIDE' OUTSIDE OCT 7 VIGIL

Comedian and media analyst Tim Young told Fox News Digital he believes protesters are paying top dollar to hijack comedy shows for viral attention rather than political discourse.

"They know that once they start yelling, everyone will whip their cameras out, and it is a very direct interaction and maybe one of the only direct interactions protesters get to have with celebrities and with the internet," Young said.

"If you are in a very intimate environment where everyone is quiet, listening to one person, you will be heard. And, so, that's what they're taking advantage of here."

Young compared the disruptions at Seinfeld's shows to protests at political rallies, arguing that some activists are willing to pay steep ticket prices to confront the comedian.

"It seems like people are going to Jerry Seinfeld's shows like they're going to a Trump rally to protest," Young said. "They wanted to get Jerry's attention. They want to, for some reason, they're very, very adamant on getting him to react to the Israel-Palestine conflict."

Young also linked the disruptions to Seinfeld's past criticism of performing at universities.

30% OF COLLEGE STUDENTS SAY VIOLENCE ACCEPTABLE WAY TO STOP SPEAKERS ON CAMPUSES, SURVEY FINDS

"It's why Jerry doesn't like to go and perform at college campuses. And he said he hates performing at college campuses specifically for that reason," Young said.

"He doesn't want to get into the political thing. He doesn't want to have protesters yelling back and forth with him. It's a waste of the rest of the audience's time, and he knows that."

In May 2024, dozens of students walked out during Seinfeld's commencement address at Duke University, some holding Palestinian flags.

Seinfeld returned to the university in September 2025 to introduce freed Israeli hostage Omer Shem Tov at a campus event, where he addressed anti-Israel protests, saying, "Free Palestine is, to me, just — you’re free to say you don’t like Jews. Just say you don’t like Jews."

QUIET PART OUT LOUD: ANTI-ISRAEL MOBS WANT ONE STATE CALLED 'PALESTINE,' ERASING ISRAEL

"By saying ‘Free Palestine,’ you’re not admitting what you really think," he said. "So, it’s actually — compared to the Ku Klux Klan, I’m actually thinking the Klan is actually a little better here because they can come right out and say, ‘We don’t like Blacks, we don’t like Jews.’ OK, that’s honest."

Seinfeld also faced controversy overseas last month when several European acts withdrew from the inaugural MEO Commedia a La Carte Fest in Lisbon, Portugal, where he is scheduled to headline later this year.

The acts did not name Seinfeld directly in their withdrawal statements, but some cited concerns about the Israel-Gaza conflict. One performer said someone involved in the festival defended ideas they considered indefensible.

Young, who previously dismissed efforts to cancel Seinfeld over his support for Israel, argued that protesters target the billionaire comedian because of his influence and celebrity status.

"This is all about control. It's all about power. And it's all about the left having power over these very influential and powerful people," Young said. "And they’re not having it."

World.title: Democrat's debate 'cue cards' steal spotlight in high-stakes Senate clash
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Alaska Democratic Senate hopeful Mary Peltola faced ridicule Thursday night after her use of notecards during a debate with Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan drew mocking responses from GOP critics — including a pointed jab from her incumbent opponent.

Sullivan is in an unusually close race with Peltola, a former congresswoman, that is further complicated by another candidate with his same name but a different middle initial, as Republicans fight to hold their narrow Senate majority.

"Really, Mary? Reading off a script? You can't cue-card your way through the Senate," Sullivan wrote on X after Peltola appeared to have a notecard-sized paper with bullet points that she looked down at for several seconds while responding to earlier questions.

GOP SENATOR, EX-HOUSE DEM EMERGE FROM ALASKA’S ‘JUNGLE PRIMARY’ DESPITE FAR-LEFT MEDDLING

The criticism quickly became a flashpoint in the candidates' debate-night exchanges, with Republican commentators seizing on Peltola's apparent use of prepared notes.

"Mary, blink twice if you are okay. It seems you can't string a sentence together without reading from the talking points your Lower 48 handlers wrote you," NRSC official Joanna Rodriguez posted on X.

Another social media user took aim at Peltola's apparent reliance on notes even while discussing personal details.

"Mary Peltola can't read her name or that she's a grandmother without needing a cue card," the user wrote, adding a laughing emoji.

After Peltola appeared to read from her card another time, Sullivan cut in that he had a question for the moderators.

'THEY WERE SPYING': SULLIVAN SOUNDS ALARM ON JOINT RUSSIA-CHINA MOVES IN U.S. ARCTIC ZONE

INSERT CLIP: 6389131701112

"We weren't supposed to get these questions beforehand, were we?" he asked the debate moderators.

"No sir," Alaska's News Source reporter Wil Courtney replied. "Absolutely not," added Alaska Public Media chief editor Lori Townsend.

"OK," Sullivan said. "I’m just watching my opponent."

Peltola defended herself, interjecting that she was better "prepared."

The Republican Party's research arm hit back on X, highlighting a clip of Peltola appearing to read from her card:

"Mary Peltola — who did not introduce a single bill to help Alaska fisherman during her first term in Congress — has to read off of a script when talking about Alaska's fishing industry," the party tweeted.

The debate also turned personal when Sullivan confronted Peltola over allegations that she mistreated former staffers, citing reporting by The New York Times and claiming that 25 employees had quit while working for her.

Peltola rejected the allegations as "outright fabrications or mass exaggerations of the truth," arguing that the election should not be about her "worst day."

The heated exchange prompted moderators to call for decorum and warn that microphones could be shut off if the candidates continued interrupting one another. Sullivan maintained that the allegations reflected a pattern of behavior, while Peltola accused her opponent of exploiting the controversy for political gain.

The candidates also faced questions over Alaska's long-discussed liquefied natural gas pipeline after moderators reported South Korea had not committed to investing in the project despite President Donald Trump's public promotion of a potential deal.

Sullivan defended the administration's efforts, arguing Seoul had committed funding through a broader trade agreement while acknowledging that the specific investment amount remained under negotiation.

DEM SENATE HOPEFUL VOWS TO UNLEASH ALASKA OIL — BUT HER RECORD TELLS A DIFFERENT STORY

Peltola also expressed support for the pipeline but cautioned against raising expectations without firm commitments, saying Alaska should not be "promoting falsehoods that just have no substance."

Both candidates emphasized the project's economic potential, although the exchange exposed uncertainty over whether promised foreign investment would materialize.

Peltola previously became the first Democrat in decades to represent Alaska in the House after the death of Republican Rep. Don Young, and her Senate candidacy again carries potentially sweeping statewide and national repercussions.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

The showdown comes as Republicans fight to defend their narrow Senate majority, with Sullivan's seat emerging as a major Democratic pickup opportunity in a state President Donald Trump carried in 2024. The Cook Political Report rates the contest a toss-up, making Alaska one of several battlegrounds that could determine which party controls the chamber in January.

World.title: Denver Broncos survive ugly offensive night to beat Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in overtime
World.content:
Broncos kicker Wil Lutz drilled a 53-yard field goal in overtime to elevate Denver to a 17-14 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night.

Seattle got the ball first in sudden death and faced a third-and-7 from its own 28. Sam Darnold tried forcing a throw into double coverage along the sideline, losing sight of Denver cornerback Ja’Quan McMillian. McMillian read it the entire way, stepped in front for the pick, and set the Broncos up at Seattle’s 43-yard line.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Broncos HC Sean Payton ran the ball three straight times to milk the clock and center the hash, and Lutz did the rest.

BRONCOS THROWBACK ORANGE CRUSH UNIFORMS MEET SEAHAWKS THROWBACK ROYAL BLUE IN RARE NFL COLOR VS COLOR GAME

With clock management blunders headlining last week's slate of NFL action, it was refreshing to watch a coach who knows how to properly win a game.

For the first twenty minutes, Payton’s script was dialed to perfection.

Denver dominated time of possession and built a 14-3 halftime lead behind two methodical touchdown drives finished off on short plunges by J.K. Dobbins and RJ Harvey. Then came the second half.

Denver’s offense looked like a unit that had never practiced together. Bo Nix finished the night with only 107 passing yards and zero downfield threat.

Seattle mounted a fierce fourth-quarter comeback, pulling within 14-11 on a George Holani touchdown and a two-point conversion pass from Darnold to Rashid Shaheed. After Denver stalled out again with barely a minute left, Jason Myers nailed a 34-yard field goal with three seconds on the clock to force overtime.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

The Broncos managed just 36 yards on eight second-half possessions, racked up three-and-outs, and turned punter Jeremy Crawshaw into the busiest man in Colorado.

If you sat through the final two quarters of that Denver offense, you are owed an apology. The only reason Denver didn't get blown out was Vance Joseph's defense.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Playing without Patrick Surtain II, Denver’s front seven spent all night hitting Darnold. The Broncos dropped him five times and generated turnovers whenever Seattle threatened to take control. Nik Bonitto stripped wideout Rashid Shaheed in scoring territory, Kris Abrams-Draine pulled down a fourth-quarter interception, and McMillian delivered the dagger in overtime.

Seattle put up 353 total yards and Jaxon Smith-Njigba caught 12 passes for 134 yards, but three turnovers wiped it all out.

Bo Nix has plenty to clean up, and Payton gets a 10-day mini-bye before hosting the Arizona Cardinals to figure out how to move the ball past the line of scrimmage. It was ugly, but it counts in the standings as the Broncos move to 4-2, sitting behind undefeated Kansas City.

NFL'S DUMBEST MOMENT OF WEEK 5 HAD THE COMMANDERS TAKING A TIE MORE OFFENSIVE THAN REDSKINS NICKNAME EVER WAS

Denver's defense won a game they had no business winning, and Darnold gave them the assist when it mattered most.

World.title: Brewers officially end Dodgers dynasty with ridiculous 6-4 comeback in game four to complete NLCS sweep
World.content:
The 2026 NLCS was a complete mismatch, though, not in the way many fans expected.

Despite winning 103 games in the regular season and employing a series of players unexpectedly having the best years out of their career, many believed the Milwaukee Brewers were big underdogs heading into the series. But through the first three games, it was the Los Angeles Dodgers who looked like an overmatched small market franchise flailing against the big-budget Brewers.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Milwaukee, riding a combination of impossibly good relief pitching, exceptionally, uh, unexpected outcomes on balls in play, home runs, and a penchant for turning every ball put in play into an out, took a commanding 3-0 series lead into game four on Thursday night.

WANT TO KNOW HOW TO WIN IN OCTOBER? THE 2026 MILWAUKEE BREWERS ARE PROVIDING THE BLUEPRINT

In game one, they beat Tarik Skubal 2-1. In game two, they went 6-14 with runners in scoring position without a single hard-hit ball. In game three, they scored five straight runs after falling behind entering the seventh inning to coast home with a 6-2 win.

Game four then, set up an opportunity for Milwaukee to reach their second-ever World Series and first since 1982. For the Dodgers, it was the first of four win-or-go home games to try and save their dynasty and win a third straight championship.

For a few minutes at least, it seemed like they'd cruise toward forcing a game five on Friday night.

Against Milwaukee opener Shane Drohan, the Dodgers put together a quick rally. Kyle Tucker led off with a single, forcing Brewers manager Pat Murphy to go to his bullpen and bring in Dustin May. Teoscar Hernandez singled Tucker to third, and after Max Muncy struck out, Andy Pages finally came through with a runner in scoring position, lacing a single up the middle to give LA a 1-0 lead.

May got Kiké Hernandez to fly out, bringing up the Dodgers' struggling superstar, Shohei Ohtani. Ohtani, who hadn't driven in a run in the postseason, hadn't hit a home run in nearly two months, and had been clearly battling multiple health issues, promptly destroyed a 1-1 pitch at 113 mph and 428 feet to make it 4-0 LA.

You could see how much it meant to Ohtani and the Dodgers with the rare show of emotion afterward.

But as always, in this NLCS, the Brewers superteam offensive machine battled right back. In the fourth, Brice Turang worked a one-out walk, and William Contreras crushed a ground-rule double to left field. Jake Bauers, who until recently was one of the worst hitters in professional baseball, followed it with another ground-rule double to right field. While the Dodgers struggled with runners in scoring position this series, the Milwaukee superteam took advantage of every opportunity. And why not? With superstar players like Bauers and Contreras, who was 9% better than league average offensively in 2026.

In the fifth, they pulled even. Sal Frelick worked a one-out walk, then stole second. The unremarkable offensive player, David Hamilton, continued his exceptional run by driving in Frelick with a single and raising his postseason batting average to .500.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Two Dodgers relievers, Evan Phillips and Alex Vesia, then walked three straight Milwaukee hitters, including Bauer yet again, to tie the game at 4-4 heading into the bottom of the fifth inning. But that's what unbeatable superteams do, they come back from 4-0 in two innings behind the best players in baseball, Jake Bauers and David Hamilton.

Sure enough, the Brewers untouchable bullpen immediately got to work, getting a shutdown inning as JoJo Romero got Ohtani, Mookie Betts, and Freddie Freeman in order on just 12 pitches.

In the sixth? The offensive juggernaut sprung into action. Garrett Mitchell, facing elite lefty reliever Tanner Scott, crushed a homer to right field, playing small ball and just making contact instead of trying to hit for power. Mitchell had two home runs against lefties in years worth of major league hitting, then proceeded to hit two homers off of Blake Snell and Tanner Scott in back-to-back nights. The Dodgers 4-0 lead, erased in a few minutes by the unstoppable force of Milwaukee's unbeatable offense.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

In the sixth, the Dodgers got a one-out double from Kyle Tucker, but the Dodgers did what they do best: go hitless with runners in scoring position to waste the opportunity. In the seventh, they did it again. Andy Pages led off the inning with a double against super-reliever Aaron Ashby, and LA played small ball, bunting him to third with one out. Ashby though, wearing the correct uniform, got Ohtani to strike out on three pitches, and Mookie Betts to ground out to shortstop to end the inning. At that point, LA was once again 2-9 with RISP, the Brewers were 2-5.

Amazingly, the Dodgers did it again in the eighth. Will Smith doubled to left, advancing to third on an error from Sal Frelick. Once again, LA had the tying run at third base with just one out, and once again, the single greatest bullpen ever assembled in the history of professional baseball clamped down. Kyle Tucker popped up to center, and Teoscar Hernandez struck out on a ball off the plate by about two and a half feet. 2-11 with RISP. As one Dodgers' commentator wrote, "some of the most pathetic at bats" you'll ever see.

David Hamilton, who, again, is one of the worst hitters in professional baseball, provided the exclamation point with a home run off Edwin Diaz in the ninth inning. Why not? The Dodgers outhit Milwaukee, because of course they did, but when you have stars like Hamilton, nothing actually matters.

Milwaukee's bullpen has allowed just two runs in the entire postseason in almost 40 innings pitched. A unit that had a 3.40 ERA in the regular season has an ERA approaching zero in the playoffs. The Dodgers stranded the tying run at third base in three consecutive innings, and it wasn't even difficult for the single greatest pitcher who's ever lived, Aaron Ashby. Fittingly, in the ninth, Ashby endured a 110-mph out from Tommy Edman and an obliterating 108-mph line drive from Kiké Hernández that was caught for an out. Because Ashby knew that allowing hard-hit balls is simply playing the game the right way. That's how you reach the World Series, and Milwaukee did it.

The Brewers have shown how you ruin baseball, develop superstars like Garrett Mitchell, sign the best free agents available like Jake Bauers, use Cy Young caliber pitchers like Shane Drohan, Dustin May, JoJo Romero and Aaron Ashby to shut down talented offenses, and listen when your manager tells you to hit home runs or put the ball in play to the correct spot, instead of making outs.

That's the right way to play the game, and the Brewers do it in spades. The Dodgers, after playing the game the right way in 2024 and 2025, stopped playing the game the right way in 2026, and it cost them.

For Los Angeles, it's a depressing end to what seemed like a dynasty. In 2024 and 2025, the breaks, the clutch hitting and the quality pitching went their way. In 2026, that all came back to bite them in a single series. Milwaukee, though, proved why they should always have been overwhelming favorites to win the World Series: they simply have better players who are able to choose to hit .500 when it matters, instead of playing like they have their entire careers.



Sarcasm aside, that's how baseball works. The teams that win get hot at the right time, and all the payroll and talent in the world can't predict which teams will get hot at the right time. There's no explanation for it, it's not a process or approach thing, there's nothing to learn from it, it's not meaningful or predictive, the postseason is a tournament, and tournaments have weird outcomes.

OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD

Milwaukee will now advance to face the winner of the Guardians-Rays series, while the Dodgers will start the long offseason targeting their next class of highly paid stars: David Hamilton and Jake Bauers.

World.title: FBI returns 'Most Wanted' fraudster to US after India arrest in alleged $600K SNAP food stamp scheme
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A fugitive accused of stealing more than $600,000 in federal food stamp benefits has been returned to the United States after being arrested in India last month, FBI Director Kash Patel announced.

Manjit Singh Bedi, one of the FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters, was wanted on federal charges stemming from an alleged Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) fraud scheme at a grocery store in Tacoma, Washington.

"BACK IN THE U.S. - Manjit Singh Bedi, one of the FBI’s Most Wanted Fraudsters, arrested in September in India," Patel posted on X.

Patel highlighted the FBI's recent success in bringing fugitives back to the United States.

EXCLUSIVE: FBI'S FIFTH MOST WANTED FRAUDSTER CAPTURED AFTER ALLEGED SNAP SCAM SUSPECT ARRESTED IN INDIA

"This is the latest in an unprecedented stretch of success in bringing high-value targets back to the United States through strong partnerships with our foreign law enforcement counterparts," Patel said.

"Over the past 20 months, we’ve secured 260 extraditions and removals — an increase of more than 70% compared to the previous 20-month period," he added.

According to federal officials, Bedi allegedly defrauded the U.S. government of at least $600,000 through a SNAP fraud scheme between March 2024 and June 2025 while operating an Asian grocery store in Tacoma.

MILLION-DOLLAR SNAP FOOD STAMP FRAUD SCHEME IN WALZ'S BACKYARD SPARKS OUTRAGE: 'CRUEL JOKE'

The FBI said Bedi allegedly swiped SNAP recipients' Electronic Benefit Transfer (EBT) cards, provided cash instead of eligible food purchases and kept roughly half the benefits for himself.

After being indicted in connection with the scheme, Bedi allegedly drove to Canada before fleeing to India.

A federal arrest warrant charging him with violating the conditions of his release was issued on May 21, 2026.

Patel said Bedi is now one of six fugitives captured through the FBI's Most Wanted Fraudsters program since the list was created three months ago.

FBI ADDS 2 FUGITIVES TO 'MOST WANTED FRAUDSTERS' LIST AMID HISTORIC $6.5B HEALTHCARE TAKEDOWN: PATEL

"This marks yet another significant moment for the historic FBI’s Most Wanted Fraudsters program," he said.

Bedi, a naturalized U.S. citizen, was previously the subject of an FBI reward offering up to $150,000 for information leading to his arrest and conviction.

Patel said Bedi will now face justice in the United States for his alleged crimes.

"Thank you to our outstanding partners for their assistance in this case," Patel wrote.

World.title: Less than 2 years after coaching college hoops in Florida, Karl Smesko leads Atlanta Dream to WNBA Finals
World.content:
Karl Smesko enjoyed notable success during his time coaching the Florida Gulf Coast women’s basketball team. But rather than remain at the college level, where he had built a powerhouse at FGCU, Smesko chose in pursue a new challenge in the WNBA.

When Smesko arrived at FGCU, the program competed in Division II. By the time he left to become the next head coach of the Atlanta Dream, the Eagles had established themselves as one of the premier programs in Division I women’s basketball.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

Under Smesko, FGCU routinely led the nation in 3-pointers made. The Eagles also recorded eight 30-win seasons and advanced to the NCAA tournament 10 times with Smesko at the helm, but he never captured the ultimate prize: an NCAA Division I championship. Perhaps the call about the opportunity in Atlanta came at just the right time for Smesko. He may have accomplished nearly everything possible at FGCU, effectively reaching the program's ceiling.

ATLANTA DREAM ADVANCE TO WNBA PLAYOFFS SEMIFINALS FOR FIRST TIME SINCE 2018 WITH GAME 2 WIN

Perhaps Smesko realized that his long-sought dream of hoisting a championship trophy would require him to step outside his comfort zone and take a chance with the actual Dream at the professional basketball level.

So far, Smesko’s gamble has worked out. He has guided Atlanta to back-to-back 30-win seasons, and after a first-round exit last year, the Dream have swept their first two opponents in the 2026 postseason to reach the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013.

The championship he was never going to get at FGCU is now four wins away, with the title series against the favored Golden State Valkyries set to begin on Saturday.

"As good as we were at Florida Gulf Coast, the odds were very stacked against us to make that type of championship run," Smesko said. "In the pros, I definitely thought there was more of an opportunity. It’s a more equal playing field to win the whole thing and that was appealing to me."

GOLDEN STATE VALKYRIES ERASE 16-POINT DEFICIT, STUN DALLAS WINGS TO REACH WNBA SEMIFINALS

The 2026 Finals will feature a matchup of second-year coaches: Smesko in Atlanta and Natalie Nakase in Golden State, which is in just its second year of existence. The Valkyries went 3-0 against the Dream this season, making them just the second team to sweep Smesko’s club in his tenure there. Las Vegas did it last season, and the Aces went on to win the WNBA title as well.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

But in Smesko the Dream trust.

"He’s a coach that really believes in you and he knows what’s best," Dream star Angel Reese said. "And I’m really thankful for him, for being able to help me with my career and help me be better for the team — because I don’t think I would be in this situation and thriving as I am individually without him."

Smesko is quiet in many ways, and fiercely loyal. The offer from the Dream came as FGCU was starting its 2024-25 season; he wound up leaving after two games that year, though some at the school believe he was tempted to try to handle both jobs at once for a few months and finish that season.

He ended up turning the keys to FGCU over to longtime top assistant Chelsea Lyles. She ended up following in her mentor’s footsteps, winning 30 games and taking the Eagles to the NCAA Tournament.

Lyles wound up following Smesko to Atlanta after that season, as did others with FGCU ties. He has made clear that the familiarity has made life easier.

"It’s been huge," Smesko said, "because we think about the game a little differently."

The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream will face off at Chase Center in San Francisco in Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Finals on Oct. 17.

World.title: Katie Zacharia addresses brevity of first press briefing, defends legal credentials after criticism
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

New White House press secretary Katie Zacharia said that she did her "very best" during her first briefing as she defended herself against criticism surrounding her legal credentials on "Hannity" Thursday.

The Pepperdine Law graduate made her White House briefing room debut on Tuesday, just days after President Donald Trump announced her appointment on Friday, leaving her with what she said was little time to prepare for the high-profile role.

"What I feel is I really stepped up to the plate to do the press conference," she told host Sean Hannity. "With very little prep time, I received briefing materials in the morning of Tuesday."

TRUMP'S NEW PRESS SECRETARY FACES FIRST MAJOR TEST AS WHITE HOUSE BRIEFING ROOM ENTERS NEW ERA

Zacharia was heavily scrutinized for taking only three questions during her roughly 14-minute briefing, much of which she spent touting the Trump administration’s accomplishments ahead of the midterm elections.

HOCHUL'S OFFICE MOCKS KATIE ZACHARIA WITH AARON RODGERS INJURY POST DESPITE GOVERNOR'S PRESS SECRETARY SCANDAL

She pushed back on criticism of her performance, saying she was on the job for less than eight hours before stepping behind the podium. She also challenged criticism that she fielded questions exclusively from conservative-leaning news organizations.

"Given the fact that I'd been on the job less than maybe eight hours and had a briefing book in the morning, I feel like I did my very best, Sean, to deliver for the American people that day," Zacharia said.

FEDERAL JUDGE ORDERS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TO RESTORE WHITE HOUSE ACCESS TO CNN, MS NOW AND POLITICO

"I took several questions and I think it's been mixed because they've said I only took questions from conservative outlets. However, the Daily Mail is not known to be a conservative outlet or friendly to conservatives so I do challenge that narrative."

Zacharia delivered a piece of major breaking news during her debut, that the Trump administration had asked Kimberly Guilfoyle to resign from her ambassador role.

"I was able to deliver breaking news, which I do believe was the right thing to do as the press secretary," she said.

The scrutiny surrounding Zacharia’s debut was compounded by questions about her legal credentials after The Wall Street Journal reported that she had failed the California bar exam.

TRUMP NAMES LEAVITT SUCCESSOR AFTER WEEKS OF SPECULATION — AND SHE'S NO STRANGER TO MAGA

Hannity challenged Zacharia over social media posts in which she had been identified as an attorney.

"There's a report out tonight that showed 15 social media posts where you identify yourself as an attorney," Hannity asked the press secretary.

"I think they were retweets, and I corrected the record and said that there's not endorsing the title. They were retweets of a title that had been given," Zacharia responded.

Zacharia revealed that after failing the bar the first time after graduating law school, she did not take the test a second time.

"I graduated Pepperdine, got married in the same week, and we had all intent to move out to China," she explained. "I had already preregistered for the bar exam and... during the summer, I knew I would be living in China and the results of the bar were inconsequential, and I sat for it because I didn't wanna have a withdrawal status."

DANA PERINO SHARES HOW SHE SECRETLY PUSHED BACK AT REPORTERS DURING WHITE HOUSE BRIEFINGS

"When I went to go engage in media and give legal analysis, I consulted attorneys and legal professionals as to whether or not they agreed that I could be labeled a lawyer, both because I had a valid juris doctor from a good law school, a reputable law school, Pepperdine Law School, and in conjunction with the fact that I did have actual substantive legal experience."

After facing days of intense backlash, including from comedian Jimmy Kimmel, who compared Zacharia’s intelligence to that of a kindergartner, she vowed to continue fighting.

She said she hopes to develop stronger relationships with members of the White House press corps and have more substantive interactions with reporters going forward.

World.title: Trans neo-Nazi accused of plotting Hindu temple massacre, will receive hormone treatment in jail: officials
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

A transgender 19-year-old who authorities say identified himself as a neo-Nazi allegedly plotted a mass shooting at a Hindu temple outside Chicago, but a tip from a coworker helped authorities thwart the attack, according to police.

Alexandros Paporakis, of Palatine, was arrested on Sunday after allegedly plotting to open fire at a Hindu temple in Aurora, a suburb of Chicago, Palatine Police said at a news conference on Thursday.

Paporakis faces one felony count of making a terrorist threat and one felony count of unlawful possession of a weapon.

A Cook County judge has ordered Paporakis held without bond and has put a jailhouse healthcare order into place, saying that the teenager receives hormone injections for gender transition and is being treated for ADHD, depression and anxiety, according to NBC Chicago.

NEVADA TRANSGENDER SUSPECT WITH MASSIVE WEAPONS CACHE ACCUSED OF LAS VEGAS TERRORISM-RELATED THREATS

Prosecutors allege Paporakis drove to the Hindu temple in Aurora armed with a modified rifle and about 300 rounds of ammunition and equipped with body armor and other tactical gear. Authorities said Paporakis intended to carry out a shooting, but returned home after the rifle malfunctioned.

After making it home, the suspect searched the internet trying to learn how to unjam the gun and allegedly called a colleague informing them of the intent to carry out a mass shooting, according to police.

Paporakis' coworkers at Taco Bell reported to Mount Prospect Police that they had received a suspicious message that day from Paporakis, leading police to obtain a search warrant and detain Paporakis before the suspect could return to the scene to carry out the alleged attack.

Authorities praised those who reported the threat and encouraged others who come across something suspicious to report it to law enforcement.

MALL OF AMERICA TERROR PLOT THWARTED; SUSPECTED ISIS SYMPATHIZER ARRESTED, FBI ANNOUNCES

"I want to praise and offer my personal, sincerest thanks to the individual who stepped forward in many successful disruptions by law enforcement and potential acts of violence or terrorism attacks. It is a single, courageous member of the public who comes forward to prevent attacks," FBI Chicago Field Office acting special agent in charge Lucas Rothaar said at a press conference on Thursday.

Police said they identified a red Acura registered to Paporakis after receiving the tip. Surveillance video showed the suspect in the vehicle entering the parking lot at the Hindu temple at 12:25 p.m. before exiting a few minutes later.

Paporakis was later observed driving to a residence on Rand Road in Palatine shared with the suspect's mother. Police executed a search warrant and found a rifle, a loaded magazine, hundreds of rounds of rifle ammunition and other tactical gear in Paporakis' possession.

Police also found what they described as an eight-page manifesto, which authorities said detailed the alleged attack and Paporakis' white supremacist views.

The writings "expressed words of hate, violence, superior race and mass shooting of Indian people. [Paporakis'] hatred was against Jewish people, African-Americans, Indians, and 'non-white' people," according to police. Paporakis described them as "subhumans" and planned to kill as many of them as possible.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Police said the suspect "expressed pleasure calling himself a sociopathic white supremacist Neo-Nazi filled with hatred, fantasizing about mass murder nearly every day."

The manifesto also referred to Paporakis as the "Aurora Shooter."

A judge ruled that Paporakis will remain in jail, with the next court appearance scheduled for Oct. 30.

The temple said it was aware of the recent security threat and has boosted security.

"Please know that the safety of our devotees, employees and volunteers is our highest priority, and we have implemented additional security measures effective immediately, including increased armed security presence at the Temple and are taking additional steps to ensure an ongoing safe environment for everyone at the Temple," the temple said in a message on its website.

World.title: Trump looms as tensions flare in final Maine Senate debate
World.content:
BANGOR, Maine — The marathon of debates in the Maine Senate race has ended, but there is still one unanswered question: Just how large will President Donald Trump loom in November?

That question was at the center of the clashes between Democrat Troy Jackson and longtime GOP Sen. Susan Collins as they faced off in four debates over the last two weeks, including a finale Thursday hosted by Maine Public Broadcasting Network, the Portland Press Herald and NBC affiliate WCSH of Portland.

Jackson is betting voters’ views of Trump, who has never won Maine, will dominate their views of this Senate race, which could determine which party controls the chamber next year.

He repeatedly tied Collins to Trump throughout all four debates. Collins, meanwhile, tried to appeal to Mainers who want a senator willing to break with his or her party.

“I voted against my own party more often than any other senator on either side of the aisle,” Collins said during the final debate. “That is not something that Troy could ever say. He’s going to be an automatic vote for the Democratic position, no matter what. We have lost a lot of the centrists, and one reason I’m running again is we need people who will work across party lines.”

Jackson countered: “The reality is that 100% of the time, when Donald Trump needs her, Susan Collins is going to be there. That has happened time and time again.”

Trump’s policies were intertwined with the major topics covered in all four debates, including high costs, the war in Iran, immigration enforcement and an ongoing trade war with Canada, which Maine borders.

On Thursday, Collins was also pressed about her support for some Trump Cabinet officials, including Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. She said she didn’t regret having voted to confirm him while noting that she disagrees with Kennedy’s vaccine skepticism. Collins said Kennedy has helped release more funds from a program to help low-income Mainers buy heating oil amid soaring prices.

Jackson, meanwhile, said he would vote to convict Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on impeachment charges.

“But that’s not my focus,” he quickly added. “My focus is delivering healthcare, prescription drugs, child care, the things that Mainers need right now more than ever, and getting out of the Iran war so we can stabilize prices.”

Tensions were high after four debates in rapid succession. This one was the first in front of a live audience, with roughly 200 people gathered in a theater at Husson University.

Around 20 minutes into the debate, a young man stood and shouted about his concerns about data centers, exclaiming that he was scared for the future.

“Thirty years for what?” the protester shouted as he was escorted out of the theater, referring to Collins’ time in the Senate.

Collins claimed the protester was a Jackson supporter, and Jackson remarked, “Oh, shut up. I don’t even know that kid.”

While the protester questioned her decades in the Senate, Collins has argued that her seniority makes her an effective advocate for Maine. She often touts her role as chairwoman of the powerful Appropriations Committee, arguing she has helped bring home huge sums of federal money to fund projects in the state.

Collins stressed that she has broken with Trump on some key issues, noting she voted against Trump’s sweeping “big, beautiful” tax and spending law last year, though she did vote to allow the measure to proceed on the floor.

“I nevertheless voted against the bill, even though it was the president’s top legislative priority. I’ve also voted nine times against the president on the Iran war,” she said.

Jackson has argued that Collins could have done more to oppose the military action.

Asked where he would break with his own party, Jackson pointed to his pledge not to accept donations from corporate political action committees.

“I think the Democrats are still too close to that,” Jackson said. “I don’t accept corporate PACs. I don’t accept corporate money. This is a campaign about fighting for everyday working-class people, and that’s one thing that I’ve been consistent on.”

Collins tried to undermine that argument, using her one question to ask Jackson about ads run in coordination with the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, which does accept corporate PAC money.

Jackson countered that he doesn’t approve those ads. While he acknowledged he has had some support from billionaires, he said his campaign is powered by small-dollar donors.

Jackson raised more than $20 million from July through September, according to a fundraising report filed Thursday. That is nearly four times Collins’ $5.2 million haul over the same period.

Jackson, a former state Senate president and logger, then pressed Collins about her claims that he couldn’t be effective in the Senate.

“I have the experience fighting for working-class people, and they deserve a senator that respects them. Is it just me that you look down on, or is it working-class people overall?” he asked.

“Troy, I do not look down on you or on anyone. I grew up in Caribou. My first job was picking potatoes,” Collins countered, saying she has “literally” worked since she was 10 years old.

“I have supported all the social safety net programs,” she said later.

Collins’ experience in the Senate is a major reason her supporters are backing her for a sixth term.

“He is just not strong on the mechanics of government,” Collins supporter Mary Ann Lynch said of Jackson. Lynch is a lifelong Democrat but is backing Collins. And she said in a phone interview Wednesday that the debates hadn’t changed her mind.

“Just watching the debates, it’s hard for me to say that if we sent Troy Jackson to Washington, he would ever be able to cut a path of leadership,” said Lynch, 71, a former member of the Cape Elizabeth Town Council.

But Jackson’s push to tie Collins to Trump does resonate with voters leaning toward supporting him, like Dan Tremble.

Tremble, a Penobscot County commissioner, said he was “pretty solid” in his decision to support Jackson as he entered the theater in Bangor on Thursday night.

“Susan Collins has done a lot for the state of Maine,” Tremble, 61, a Democrat, said when he was asked why he wasn’t certain he’d support Jackson. “But I think having her in the Senate, I think, would still leave a majority for the president in the United States Senate, and that’s very worrisome with this president.”

“He says, ‘Vote like I’m on the ballot,’” Tremble added, referring to Trump. “I will.”

CORRECTION (Oct. 15, 2026, 10:17 p.m. ET): A previous version of this article misidentified the Cabinet secretary Troy Jackson said he’d vote to convict on impeachment charges. It was Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, not Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

World.title: Musk donates over $150 million to Senate GOP group, assisting Paxton
World.content:
Billionaire Elon Musk donated $158 million last month to the main super PAC supporting Senate Republicans, which almost immediately sent the money to a group that supports GOP Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton, according to Federal Election Commission filings.

Republicans are fighting to hold on to the Texas Senate seat, as polls point to a tight race between Paxton and Democratic opponent James Talarico.

The assist from Musk — along with tens of millions of dollars in donations to other groups — marks a decisive return to large-scale political giving for the world's richest man, who spent over a quarter of a billion dollars backing President Trump and other Republican candidates in 2024.

Musk donated $75 million to the Senate Leadership Fund PAC on Sept. 9, and $83 million two weeks later, the group reported Thursday. Combined, the two super-sized donations from Musk made up more than half of the super PAC's total receipts in the third quarter of this year.

One day after each donation, the Senate Leadership Fund PAC disbursed the same amount to Texas PAC. That group reported over $100 million in pro-Paxton and anti-Talarico spending.

Musk also donated more than $80 million from July to September to his own group, America PAC, which was the primary vehicle for his political giving in 2024. The group reported spending on the Texas Senate contest and several other competitive congressional races.

Musk — who has strongly criticized Talarico in recent weeks — is a resident of Texas, and his largest companies, SpaceX and Tesla, base many of their operations in the state.

Talarico is attempting to become the first Democrat to win a statewide race in Texas in more than three decades. He has sought to capitalize on Paxton's history of scandal, and on still-lingering divides among Texas Republicans after Paxton defeated incumbent Republican Sen. John Cornyn in a bitter primary contest earlier this year. Paxton and his allies, including Mr. Trump, have argued Talarico is too far to the left for Texas' electorate.

Most recent polls show Talarico with a within-the-margin-of-error lead. If Paxton loses the seat, it could deal a serious blow to Republicans' efforts to hold on to the Senate.

After Musk served as the country's top political donor in the 2024 cycle, it was initially unclear whether he planned to spend similar sums in future elections. His stint leading the Trump administration's Department of Government Efficiency ended with him briefly feuding with the president, and he suggested at one point last year that he planned to scale back his political spending, joking during one interview, "I think I've done enough."

America PAC spokesperson Andrew Romeo said in a statement to CBS News: "If Democrats take control of Washington and win key gubernatorial and attorney general races this November, then America risks becoming a socialist, woke and borderless country. These robust investments have allowed the G.O.P. apparatus to get its message out so Republicans can have a fighting chance to defy history."

World.title: Justice Dept. sues California, claims noncitizens were sent ballots
World.content:
Washington — The Justice Department sued California on Thursday, alleging that the federal government has identified more than 20,000 noncitizens who are unlawfully registered to vote.

The lawsuit, filed in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California, came after Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter sent letters to counties earlier this week, including Los Angeles, ordering them to review a list of names of suspected noncitizens who he alleged received mail-in ballots for the upcoming midterm elections.

"State-facilitated voter fraud is unacceptable in the United States of America," Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement announcing the lawsuit.

"If found responsible in a court of law, the State of California will have seriously undermined confidence in our electoral system and violated laws that protect our nation's representative system of government."

In the letter that McCotter sent to the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk, he enclosed a password-protected thumb drive that he said contained names compiled by the Department of Homeland Security, and imposed a 48-hour deadline for the clerk's office to review the list.

Dean Logan, the registrar-recorder and clerk, said in a statement responding to McCotter's demands that the county would not be reviewing the materials on the thumb drive because doing so would conflict with "established data privacy and information security protocols." He said the device was not considered a "secure medium."

Secretary of State Shirley Weber, meanwhile, said the Justice Department had not provided the list of names and blasted the Trump administration for what it said were "unsubstantiated claims" that California had 190,000 noncitizens on its voter rolls.

In Thursday's lawsuit, the Justice Department accused the state of failing to work with the federal government to correct the alleged problems with its voter rolls.

"The Federal Government asked California to work collaboratively to identify any noncitizens registered to vote in the State. California made no serious effort to do so," the lawsuit said.

"The United States thus seeks commonplace election relief when a ballot is called into question. This Court should enjoin California from presently tabulating vote-by-mail ballots from likely noncitizens in the upcoming federal election until the voter's citizenship status can be determined," it added.

In a statement provided to CBS News, the California Secretary of State's office said, "Due to the pending litigation, we have no further information we can share regarding the matter." It directed CBS News to its news release on the situation and Weber's letter to McCotter.

CBS News has also reached out to the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk for comment.

The Justice Department's Civil Rights Division has filed 31 lawsuits in an effort to force states to hand over unredacted copies of their voter rolls. The division has said it wants to ensure states are keeping clean voter lists, but it has since acknowledged that it also intends to share the data with the Department of Homeland Security so that the lists can be screened for noncitizens.

Harmeet Dhillon, the assistant attorney general for the Civil Rights Division, sent letters to all 50 states in July threatening to take criminal action if they knowingly allowed noncitizens to remain on their voter rolls.

So far, the Justice Department has lost 26 of those cases, and has not achieved one legal victory to date.

It has resorted to using publicly available voter lists and other investigative means to try to identify noncitizens who may be registered in those states.

World.title: Soaring heating oil prices put struggling Maine families in a bind
World.content:
In Freeport, Maine, Chris and Cheryl Oliver are making tough choices as they try to make ends meet on roughly $60,000 a year.

"Am I going to get food this week, or am I going to get gas this week?" Cheryl Oliver told CBS News.

Then came another blow. Just as diesel and gas prices have risen considerably since the start of the Iran war, the price of heating oil in Maine has soared from $3.34 per gallon one year ago to $5.97 today, a jump of roughly 79%.



The Olivers qualified for 100 gallons of free heating oil through a local community center, help worth about $700. Unfortunately, it still won't get them through the winter.

"I was panicking, like, how are we going to fill our tank and how are we going to stay warm?" Cheryl Oliver asked.

Nationwide, more than 4 million households use heating oil as their primary fuel source, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, and of those, 82% are concentrated in the Northeast.

Tony DiMarco, co-founder of the Freeport Wood Bank, a food pantry of sorts for firewood, said the demand right now is "extremely high." Donations keep it running.



"I don't think people fully recognize how big of an impact it's going to have when heating oil costs twice as much as it did last year, and people are already spending as much as they did last year," DiMarco said. "I just don't think people fully grasp the severity of the problem."

The Freeport Wood Bank is one of about 17 similar wood banks across the state. Freeport can supply about 50 families with firewood, but DiMarco says it will run out of its supply by the middle of winter.

This week, DiMarco delivered two free cords of firewood to help the Olivers stretch their heating oil. It's a lifeline for a family already struggling. Chris Oliver lost one of his legs to diabetes and later suffered a heart attack.

"Tony and that place, they're unbelievable," an emotional Chris Oliver said. "I don't know without them if we'd have heat."

World.title: Vance says "selling access to the White House" is "disgusting"
World.content:
Vice President JD Vance told CBS News on Thursday that anybody who is "selling access to the White House" should "suffer consequences."

Vance spoke with "CBS Evening News" anchor Tony Dokoupil during a one-hour town hall in Michigan that is set to air on Saturday evening, less than three weeks before the midterm elections.

Dokoupil pointed to a string of recent reports, including Mr. Trump's staggering cryptocurrency earnings, and the ousting of U.S. Ambassador to Greece Kimberly Guilfoyle over allegations she asked a man who was seeking help from the Trump administration to wire her $100,000.

"First of all, if somebody's selling access to the White House, that's disgusting and despicable and they should suffer consequences," Vance responded.

He went on to say, "I want to make those judgments based on the facts and not based on a random news media report that I read."

Guilfoyle has denied wrongdoing. Mr. Trump has denied any conflicts of interest.

Congressional Democrats have vowed to investigate the Trump administration if they win control of the House or Senate, which would grant them control over committees and allow them to issue subpoenas to administration officials.

Asked if the administration would comply with any subpoenas, Vance said: "Of course I will. Look, I mean, we follow the law."
